title: TUI porting specification
introduction: Source-only audit of the frozen TypeScript interactive host, components, appearance/theme system and terminal library against the independently reviewed native Rust TUI and product host. The 151 entries combine 84 product/UI contracts with 67 terminal contracts. Exact source/test read ranges, hashes, connector redactions, baseline-dirty test qualifications, candidate dispositions and native preservation notes are recorded in the TUI evidence manifests. Tests and application code were read, never executed. Final publication and cross-area acceptance belong to the coordinator.

entries.title: JSON theme format, semantic color tokens and ANSI rendering
entries.source:
Runtime format and token predicates: `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/theme.ts:26-238`; color algorithms and Theme class: `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/theme.ts:246-593`; parser/runtime construction: `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/theme.ts:685-811`. Published editor schema: `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/theme-schema.json:1-349`. Tests: `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/theme-detection.test.ts:102-123`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/scrollbar-theme.test.ts:30-48`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/max-thinking.test.ts:29-63`. User format documentation: `ice:packages/coding-agent/docs/themes.md:133-285`.

`ThemeColorValue` — `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/theme.ts:110`. `ThemeColor` — `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/theme.ts:114`. `ThemeBg` — `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/theme.ts:163`.
entries.what: Loads user and package JSON palettes, resolves reusable colors, and styles each semantic UI role while adapting hex colors to truecolor or a 256-color terminal.
entries.mechanism:
A theme file is validated before runtime construction, then every color variable is resolved and each foreground/background role is converted to an ANSI prefix. This allows the same JSON palette to work across terminal color capabilities while retaining separate colors for messages, tools, syntax and all thinking levels.

JSON parsing failures are wrapped as `Failed to parse theme <label>: <error>`. Runtime TypeBox validation requires string name and all 51 required color tokens; color values are strings or integers from 0 through 255. Missing required colors are accumulated, sorted, and reported separately from other instance-path errors. The explicit name assertion rejects any slash because slash separates automatic light/dark names. The published schema additionally declares a nonempty slash-free name pattern and additionalProperties:false at the top level, colors and export; the runtime schema construction does not explicitly include those options. Do not substitute published schema strictness for an unverified library default (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/theme.ts:26-107`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/theme.ts:685-751`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/theme-schema.json:12-15`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/theme-schema.json:309-342`).

Variable resolution returns numeric, empty or '#' prefixed values immediately. Other strings recursively index vars, fail with `Variable reference not found: <name>` when absent, and track visited names to fail with `Circular variable reference detected: <name>`. It does not interpret a '$' prefix. Before resolution, missing/nullish thinkingMax inherits thinkingXhigh; thinkingUltra inherits thinkingMax then thinkingXhigh; scrollbarThumb inherits selectedBg. Runtime Theme construction repeats the compatible optional-token fallbacks. Seven background keys are selectedBg, scrollbarThumb, userMessageBg, customMessageBg, toolPendingBg, toolSuccessBg and toolErrorBg; all other resolved keys become foreground colors (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/theme.ts:416-508`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/theme.ts:775-800`).

Color mode is an explicit argument or getCapabilities().trueColor ? truecolor : 256color. Empty strings yield SGR39/49 terminal defaults. Integers yield 38;5 or 48;5 without RGB conversion. A '#' string removes the first '#', requires six remaining characters, and parseInt-parses each two-character channel, rejecting only NaN channels; this is less strict than a full six-hex-digit regular expression. Truecolor emits 38;2;r;g;b or 48;2;r;g;b. The 256 approximation chooses each nearest cube channel from [0,95,135,175,215,255], preserving the earlier index on a tie; cube index is 16+36*rIndex+6*gIndex+bIndex. It also computes the nearest 24-step gray ramp (8+10*i), using rounded 0.299*r+0.587*g+0.114*b and weighted squared distance with those coefficients. Gray is selected only when maxChannel-minChannel<10 and its distance is strictly less than the cube distance. Other string colors fail `Invalid color value: <value>` (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/theme.ts:246-258`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/theme.ts:308-414`).

Theme.fg/bg fetch their precomputed map entry, throw for unknown tokens, and append only SGR39 or SGR49 respectively. They do not append SGR0. getFgAnsi/getBgAnsi expose the prefix; getColorMode exposes the selected mode. bold/italic/underline/inverse/strikethrough delegate to chalk. Thinking border closures use dedicated off/minimal/low/medium/high/xhigh/max/ultra tokens, with unexpected levels falling back to off; Bash border uses bashMode (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/theme.ts:518-593`).

Diff tint generation uses the first six-digit hex background among toolPendingBg, userMessageBg and selectedBg to classify a light surface by (0.2126*r+0.7152*g+0.0722*b)/255>=0.5. For hex toolDiffAdded/Removed it derives hue, saturation zero for neutral colors or clamp(delta/(1-|max+min-1|),0.35,0.6), and HSL lightness 0.92/0.82 for line/word on light surfaces or 0.14/0.24 on dark surfaces. HSL conversion rounds channels and emits background ANSI for added/removed × line/word. Numeric/default/non-six-digit diff colors have no generated tint (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/theme.ts:260-305`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/theme.ts:497-515`).
entries.interfaces:
Runtime schema fragment (verbatim): `Type.Integer({ minimum: 0, maximum: 255 })`. JSON contract: `{name:string, $schema?:string, vars?:Record<string,string|integer>, colors:{...}, export?:{pageBg?:ColorValue,cardBg?:ColorValue,infoBg?:ColorValue}}`, where ColorValue is a string or integer 0..255. Required color keys: accent, border, borderAccent, borderMuted, success, error, warning, muted, dim, text, thinkingText, selectedBg, userMessageBg, userMessageText, customMessageBg, customMessageText, customMessageLabel, toolPendingBg, toolSuccessBg, toolErrorBg, toolTitle, toolOutput, mdHeading, mdLink, mdLinkUrl, mdCode, mdCodeBlock, mdCodeBlockBorder, mdQuote, mdQuoteBorder, mdHr, mdListBullet, toolDiffAdded, toolDiffRemoved, toolDiffContext, syntaxComment, syntaxKeyword, syntaxFunction, syntaxVariable, syntaxString, syntaxNumber, syntaxType, syntaxOperator, syntaxPunctuation, thinkingOff, thinkingMinimal, thinkingLow, thinkingMedium, thinkingHigh, thinkingXhigh, bashMode. Optional color keys: scrollbarThumb, thinkingMax, thinkingUltra. Public methods: parseThemeJsonData(label, json), createThemeFromData(label, json, mode?), loadThemeFromPath(path, mode?), isThemeColorToken(string), isThemeBgToken(string). Theme constructor takes resolved foreground/background records, mode and optional name/sourcePath/sourceInfo; sourceInfo remains mutable. Theme methods are fg, bg, bold, italic, underline, inverse, strikethrough, getFgAnsi, getBgAnsi, getDiffBgAnsi(kind, emphasis), getColorMode, getThinkingBorderColor(level), getBashModeBorderColor().

entries.dependency_text: Uses JSON parsing, TypeBox validation, chalk styling and terminal capability discovery. SET-033 owns resource discovery/trust/source metadata; native primitive capability handling is reviewed in the terminal fragment.
entries.rust: Rust has typed ThemeColors, Color and Theme with many corresponding semantic roles, but no JSON palette/variable/parser interface in the independently read implementation (`rust:crates/ice-tui/src/theme.rs:15-106`, `rust:crates/ice-tui/src/theme.rs:173-264`). Color supports Default/Ansi16/Ansi256/Rgb; RGB emits truecolor directly without this capability-dependent approximation. Color::fg appends full SGR0. Color::bg reapplies its background after each nested SGR0 and finishes with SGR0 (`rust:crates/ice-tui/src/theme.rs:186-221`). Native typed fields do not include the TS syntax token set, per-level thinking border colors, scrollbarThumb or separate userMessageText token. ThemeSpacing and native inline/block code backgrounds are existing capabilities to retain. Native preset loading accepts only dark/light/monochrome (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui.rs:972-984`); copying a TS custom-theme JSON alone cannot make it load through this path.
entries.port: Implement a validated JSON Theme model and explicit conversion into a runtime palette in ice-tui, plus file loading through ice-cli's trusted resource loader. Preserve native spacing/code-background fields with documented defaults when converting a TS file. Use serde/serde_json and typed error reporting; implement variable-cycle detection and exact optional fallbacks. Decide explicitly whether strict full-hex validation, published-schema extra-key rejection and attribute-specific reset semantics are compatibility requirements or documented improvements. TUI-002, TUI-003 and TUI-007–008 cover catalog/runtime behavior separately.
entries.priority_reason: Required for custom theme migration and complete palette fidelity across existing UI roles.

entries.title: Bundled palette assets and exact catalog identities
entries.what: Ships 100 named JSON palettes whose semantic colors are interpreted by the common theme loader, including the built-in dark/light defaults and the other catalog themes.
entries.mechanism:
Each asset supplies a filename-matching name, reusable variables, all 51 required semantic color roles and three export background roles. The loader resolves these data through the same parser as user themes, so catalog completeness includes the exact names, values and optional fallbacks as well as the presence of files.

All 100 assets were read in full at the frozen hash. Every asset supplies all 51 required roles; only dark and light explicitly add scrollbarThumb and thinkingMax, and no asset explicitly supplies thinkingUltra. The remaining 98 inherit scrollbarThumb from selectedBg and thinkingMax/thinkingUltra from thinkingXhigh through TUI-001. All reachable color/export values in the read assets resolve to empty terminal-default strings or six-digit hex strings. The supplemental static JSON inspection in evidence/tui-palette-catalog.json preserves every original value, resolved role, exact reference and SHA; it did not execute the theme loader or tests.

Ninety-four assets use the empty string for text, userMessageText and customMessageText. The six exceptions are:

| Palette | text | userMessageText | customMessageText |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| dark-poimandres | #a6accd | #ffffff | #ffffff |
| dark | #d4d4d4 | #d4d4d4 | #d4d4d4 |
| light-cyberpunk | #1B1B2A | #1B1B2A | #1B1B2A |
| light-poimandres | #506477 | #ffffff | #ffffff |
| light-retro | #2b2b2b | #2b2b2b | #2b2b2b |
| light | #1f2328 | #1f2328 | #1f2328 |

Dark uses text #d4d4d4, accent #8abeb7, selectedBg #3a3a4a, userMessageBg #343541, customMessageBg #2d2838, pending/success/error tool backgrounds #282832/#283228/#3c2828, thinkingMax #ff5fff, and export page/card/info backgrounds #18181e/#1e1e24/#3c3728. Light uses text #1f2328, selectedBg #d0d0e0, userMessageBg #e8e8e8, tool backgrounds #e8e8f0/#e8f0e8/#f0e8e8, thinkingMax #af005f, and export #f8f8f8/#ffffff/#fffae6. Their scrollbarThumb is selectedBg by variable reference (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/dark.json:1-89`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/light.json:1-88`).

Dark-poimandres and light-poimandres also define fifteen numeric variables with names ending 256 and values 235,238,109,103,66,86,44,79,153,117,79,169,211,229,110. No color or export role references them, directly or transitively; their runtime roles resolve through the hex variables and use the normal color-mode conversion. These unused definitions do not implement a separate automatic indexed palette (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/dark-poimandres.json:1-102`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/light-poimandres.json:1-102`).

Onyx uniquely spells the root metadata key schema instead of $schema at line 2. That conflicts with the published editor schema's additionalProperties:false. Runtime TypeBox extra-property defaults were not accessible for independent verification, so this audit does not claim that runtime loading rejects the asset (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/onyx.json:1-77`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/theme-schema.json:12-21`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/theme-schema.json:342-349`).

The complete catalog is explicit below. Bundled dark-lavender/light-lavender are distinct identities from the historical custom lavender-ice theme mentioned in the active porting report. No real user theme directories were read; historical import status remains unverified.
entries.interfaces: Exact bundled names (100): alabaster, amethyst, anthracite, basalt, birch, dark-abyss, dark-arctic, dark-aurora, dark-catppuccin, dark-cavern, dark-copper, dark-cosmos, dark-cyberpunk, dark-dracula, dark-eclipse, dark-ember, dark-equinox, dark-forest, dark-github, dark-gruvbox, dark-lavender, dark-lunar, dark-midnight, dark-monochrome, dark-monokai, dark-nebula, dark-nord, dark-ocean, dark-one, dark-poimandres, dark-rainforest, dark-reef, dark-retro, dark-rose-pine, dark-sakura, dark-slate, dark-solarized, dark-solstice, dark-starfall, dark-sunset, dark-swamp, dark-synthwave, dark-taiga, dark-terminal, dark-tokyo-night, dark-tundra, dark-twilight, dark-volcanic, dark, graphite, light-arctic, light-aurora-day, light-canyon, light-catppuccin, light-cirrus, light-coral, light-cyberpunk, light-dawn, light-dunes, light-eucalyptus, light-forest, light-frost, light-github, light-glacier, light-gruvbox, light-haze, light-honeycomb, light-lagoon, light-lavender, light-meadow, light-mint, light-monochrome, light-ocean, light-one, light-opal, light-orchard, light-paper, light-poimandres, light-prism, light-retro, light-sand, light-savanna, light-solarized, light-soleil, light-sunset, light-synthwave, light-tokyo-night, light-wetland, light-zenith, light, limestone, mahogany, marble, obsidian, onyx, pearl, porcelain, quartz, sandstone, titanium. Each file is packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/<name>.json, with name equal to its basename. Every export block supplies pageBg, cardBg and infoBg; full per-role values are retained in evidence/tui-palette-catalog.json. TUI-001 defines the format and fallback semantics; TUI-003 defines name resolution, loading and registry behavior.
entries.dependency_text: Requires the common JSON theme parser and catalog loader. SET-033 owns discovery/source metadata rather than palette interpretation.
entries.rust: Native ThemePreset has Dark, Light and Monochrome and ThemeManager loads those fixed constructors; the CLI startup path accepts only dark/light/monochrome (`rust:crates/ice-tui/src/theme.rs:223-338`, `rust:crates/ice-tui/src/theme.rs:343-386`, `rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui.rs:972-984`). Dark's native constants are a separate palette: primary text is terminal default, several colors are fixed ANSI256 approximations, Markdown code and tool backgrounds deliberately use native RGB values, and custom message text is terminal default (`rust:crates/ice-tui/src/theme.rs:108-169`). Thus even shared dark/light names do not establish identical data. Existing native Monochrome, ThemeSpacing and code-background behavior should remain available when adding the TS catalog. No loader for the other 98 exact names was present in the independently read native path.
entries.port: Package the complete 100-asset catalog alongside the typed JSON format loader, with deterministic filename/name identity and source hashes or build-time validation. Preserve terminal-default colors and optional-token fallbacks, retain native presets/extensions without silently aliasing differently valued palettes, and decide explicitly how to handle the onyx metadata spelling. Convert the original values through the compatibility color-mode rules rather than replacing them with ad hoc native approximations. Verification should cover every asset and reference resolution, plus exact default/optional role values; this audit has performed source inspection only.
entries.priority_reason: Required for existing named-theme selection and portable theme/profile imports; the source catalog is much larger than the three native presets.

entries.title: Named theme registry, global live switching and selector integration
entries.source:
`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/theme.ts:622-828`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/theme.ts:983-1066`; controller `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/theme-controller.ts:18-140`; selector `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/theme-selector.ts:1-68`. Tests: `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/theme-picker.test.ts:25-75`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/legacy-compat/runtime-contracts.test.ts:149-157`, extension UI integration `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/interactive-mode-status.test.ts:313-372`.

`ThemeSelectorComponent` — `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/theme-selector.ts:13`.
entries.what: Lists available palettes, previews selections, and switches the process-wide theme so interactive components and extensions see the same current palette.
entries.mechanism:
Available names combine the built-in catalog, valid custom JSON files and registered runtime themes, while the current palette is shared through a global symbol. Selection and preview update the live palette, with explicit dark fallback and error reporting when a load fails.

getAvailableThemesWithPaths first adds built-ins with their bundled JSON paths, then custom files under getCustomThemesDir, then registered themes with optional sourcePath; the first name wins in this listing, and final output sorts by name.localeCompare. Custom files are enumerated in Node readdir order, accept only a lowercase .json suffix, are individually parsed/constructed, and contribute the content name; errors are ignored here for the resource loader to report. getAvailableThemes returns names only. Runtime loading has a different precedence: registeredThemes.get(name) is returned first, then loadThemeJson. JSON loading itself prefers built-ins, then reads a registered sourcePath, rejects registered in-memory objects without a source path for export, then tries customDir/name.json. getThemeJsonData returns a structuredClone. getThemeByName suppresses any error and returns undefined. Consequently a content name differing from its custom filename is discoverable, but named loading needs the resource registry or a matching filename; the picker test proves discovery only (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/theme.ts:622-683`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/theme.ts:738-828`).

setRegisteredThemes clears the old Map and adds only truthy names, validating slash prohibition and letting later duplicate names replace earlier values. theme is a Proxy over globalThis[Symbol.for('@zykairotis/ice-coding-agent:theme')]; property access before initialization throws. This global object is shared by module loaders, while the registered Map/current name/watcher/callback are module state. The proxy returns the current property directly. initTheme chooses an explicit name or environment-derived default, loads it, optionally starts watching, and silently falls back to dark on error. setTheme records the requested name, loads, optionally starts watching and invokes the one registered onThemeChange callback; any error in that try block falls back to dark and returns success:false with a string message. A fallback load failure can still throw. enableWatcher:false does not explicitly stop an existing watch (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/theme.ts:983-1053`).

setThemeInstance installs the provided instance, sets current name to '<in-memory>', stops the watcher and invokes the callback; it has no local catch. onThemeChange replaces one callback rather than maintaining a subscriber collection. InteractiveThemeController.setThemeName and setThemeInstance disable automatic synchronization, apply the theme and call notifyChanged. applyThemeName records the requested name on success or dark on failure, invalidates the UI, invokes the supplied onChanged callback and optionally reports the load error plus dark fallback. preview resolves a setting/name against the current terminal theme, applies with watching, invalidates and requests render only on success; it does not replace activeThemeName or persist settings itself (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/theme.ts:1055-1066`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/theme-controller.ts:69-112`).

ThemeSelectorComponent builds one item per available name, marks the exact current name, preselects it when present, displays 10 visible rows with primary column min 12/max 32, and surrounds the SelectList with DynamicBorder. Selecting invokes onSelect(name); moving selection invokes onPreview(name); cancellation delegates onCancel. The component itself writes no settings. Extension-facing instance/name selection and name persistence are specified in EXT-049 (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/theme-selector.ts:5-67`).
entries.interfaces: `ThemeInfo { name: string; path: string | undefined; }`; getAvailableThemes():string[], getAvailableThemesWithPaths():ThemeInfo[], getThemeJsonData(name):ThemeJson, getThemeByName(name):Theme|undefined, setRegisteredThemes(Theme[]), initTheme(name?, enableWatcher=false), setTheme(name, enableWatcher=false):{success:boolean;error?:string}, setThemeInstance(Theme), onThemeChange(callback). Shared symbol key is @zykairotis/ice-coding-agent:theme. Controller has applyFromSettings, rebindTui, setThemeName, setThemeInstance, preview, disableAutoSync, getTerminalTheme; automatic behavior is TUI-007.
entries.dependency_text: Built-in palette contents are TUI-002. Depends on the settings manager, UI invalidation/render callbacks and trusted resource discovery. It needs no external service.
entries.rust: The global OnceLock<ThemeManager> stores a cloned Theme behind Mutex; reads fall back to default on poison, and set bumps an AtomicU64 revision even if the lock fails. Native components can invalidate caches by revision (`rust:crates/ice-tui/src/theme.rs:343-386`, `rust:crates/ice-tui/src/theme.rs:507-526`). Startup applies exactly three known strings to global and local managers (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui.rs:972-984`). The /theme selector lists only dark/light/monochrome and applies both managers, but does not persist selection; its comment about enabled package themes is stale (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/selectors.rs:449-506`). The settings picker applies/persists and reports save failure (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/settings.rs:390-433`). Direct /theme <name> lowercases, rejects unknown values, applies globally and writes settings while discarding save errors (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/commands.rs:320-349`). There is no named JSON registry or source-aware picker in these paths.
entries.port: Extend the native registry and selectors to accept trusted resource Theme models, retaining global revision-based cache invalidation. Specify name collision precedence consistently across listing, runtime lookup and export, or document any deliberate correction to the TS precedence mismatch. Keep previews separate from committed settings and restore the chosen theme on cancellation at the caller. Keep native presets available; reconcile the native /theme selector's nonpersistent behavior with settings/direct-command persistence.
entries.priority_reason: Turns imported palettes into usable, consistent interactive theme choices.

entries.title: Resolved theme colors and optional palette values for HTML export
entries.source: `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/theme.ts:1154-1267`; export tests `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/theme-export.test.ts:18-104`; format docs `ice:packages/coding-agent/docs/themes.md:252-264`. Missing-configured-theme export regression: `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/suite/regressions/5596-missing-theme-export.test.ts:26-88`.
entries.what: Supplies CSS-compatible palette values and optional page/card/info backgrounds to session HTML export.
entries.mechanism:
Export helpers resolve a named theme's JSON independently of the live ANSI objects and convert palette indices into CSS colors. Optional export backgrounds fail softly, while the complete color-map helper propagates load or resolution errors.

ansi256ToHex maps indices 0–15 to #000000,#800000,#008000,#808000,#000080,#800080,#008080,#c0c0c0,#808080,#ff0000,#00ff00,#ffff00,#0000ff,#ff00ff,#00ffff,#ffffff. For 16–231 it decodes the 6×6×6 cube and maps channel 0 to 0, otherwise 55+40*channel. For 232–255 it repeats gray 8+10*(index-232). getResolvedThemeColors uses the explicit name, else currentThemeName, else environment default; loads the original JSON with the TUI-003 precedence; applies optional token fallbacks; resolves recursive vars; then converts numbers to hex and empty strings to '#000000' only when the exact name is 'light', otherwise '#e5e5e7'. Empty backgrounds receive that same fallback here. Other resolved strings are returned unchanged. Custom light-looking names are not analyzed (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/theme.ts:1154-1225`).

isLightTheme returns themeName==='light' exactly, without reading the current name or luminance. getThemeExportColors chooses the same effective name and loads export; absent export returns {}. Each optional pageBg/cardBg/infoBg resolves vars, maps numbers to CSS hex, maps empty to undefined and preserves other strings. Missing values remain undefined. Any load/resolve error returns {} for the whole operation. Tests assert recursive aliases, index 24→#005f87 and empty infoBg→undefined (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/theme.ts:1227-1267`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/theme-export.test.ts:38-103`).

An in-memory runtime Theme with no sourcePath cannot be reconstituted by the JSON loader for this export route. This entry covers palette production; SESSION-038 owns session export invocation and current-state context, while the HTML template remains a separate caller responsibility.
entries.interfaces: getResolvedThemeColors(themeName?):Record<string, string>; isLightTheme(themeName?):boolean; getThemeExportColors(themeName?):{pageBg?:string;cardBg?:string;infoBg?:string}. JSON export format: `{ "export": { "pageBg": ColorValue, "cardBg": ColorValue, "infoBg": ColorValue } }`, with each field optional and ColorValue as in TUI-001.
entries.dependency_text: Used by HTML export; no browser or network call is made by these palette helpers.

entries.title: Syntax highlighting, Markdown theme and interactive chrome adapters
entries.source:
Theme adapters and extension map: `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/theme.ts:1275-1527`; full highlighting renderer: `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/syntax-highlight.ts:1-147`; tests: `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/syntax-highlight.test.ts:6-75`.; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/dynamic-border.ts:1-26.

`HighlightFormatter` — `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/syntax-highlight.ts:4`. `renderHighlightedHtml` — `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/syntax-highlight.ts:80`.
entries.what: Applies the selected semantic palette to code, Markdown and reusable selection/editor/settings controls.
entries.mechanism:
Code highlighting uses highlight.js output converted from nested HTML spans to ANSI formatting. The theme adapter selects explicit languages only, avoiding auto-detection for unlabelled prose; syntax formatter functions are cached by Theme object identity.

The renderer recognizes span tags with a first hljs-* class, tracks nested scopes, resolves formatter by exact scope then first dot prefix then first dash prefix, and searches outward through parents before theme.default. Unscoped nested spans preserve parent formatting. It flushes text at span boundaries and decodes entities through decodeHtmlEntityAt once. Unmatched close spans simply pop when possible; malformed/unrecognized markup is copied as text. highlight(code,{language?, ignoreIllegals?, languageSubset?, theme?}) calls explicit hljs.highlight or, only without language, highlightAuto; supportsLanguage delegates to hljs.getLanguage.

Semantic mappings are keyword/name→syntaxKeyword;built_in/class/type→syntaxType;literal/number→syntaxNumber;regexp/string→syntaxString;comment/doctag→syntaxComment;meta→muted;function/title→syntaxFunction;attr/variable/params→syntaxVariable;operator→syntaxOperator;tag/punctuation→syntaxPunctuation;emphasis/strong/link→italic/bold/underline;addition/deletion→toolDiffAdded/Removed. highlightCode validates the supplied language and returns per-line mdCodeBlock color for absent/unknown languages, passes ignoreIllegals=true, and returns raw uncolored lines if highlighting throws. getMarkdownTheme's otherwise parallel callback returns mdCodeBlock-colored lines on exceptions. Neither adapter requests auto-detection.

getLanguageFromPath lowercases the final dot-separated portion, even for a basename without a dot. Exact aliases: ts/tsx→typescript;js/jsx/mjs/cjs→javascript;py→python;rb→ruby;rs→rust;go;java;kt→kotlin;swift;c/h→c;cpp/cc/cxx/hpp→cpp;cs→csharp;php;sh/bash/zsh→bash;fish;ps1→powershell;sql;html/htm→html;css/scss/sass/less;json;yaml/yml→yaml;toml;xml;md/markdown→markdown;dockerfile;makefile;cmake;lua;perl;r;scala;clj→clojure;ex/exs→elixir;erl→erlang;hs→haskell;ml→ocaml;vim;graphql;proto→protobuf;tf/hcl→hcl. An unmapped extension returns undefined.

getMarkdownTheme supplies live semantic formatting closures for headings/link/URL/inline code/code block/borders/quote/rule/bullets plus styles and highlighting. A global optional InteractiveChromeThemeOverride supplies select-list selection/description/hints, settings label/value/cursor, editor border, scrollbar backgrounds and border family/color. Most returned formatting closures consult the current override on each call; cursor strings and borderStyle/borderColor properties are captured when a theme adapter object is created. none/undefined chrome border becomes undefined, track defaults to identity and thumb to theme scrollbarThumb background.

DynamicBorder renders one row of at least one horizontal border character using an explicitly supplied color function or the live theme border color. It has no cache and its invalidate is a no-op; the module comment requires an explicit color callback when extension loading creates a separate module cache (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/dynamic-border.ts:1-26).
entries.interfaces:
HighlightTheme=Partial<Record<string,(text:string)=>string>>; HighlightOptions {language?:string;ignoreIllegals?:boolean;languageSubset?:string[];theme?:HighlightTheme}. Exports highlightCode(code, lang?)->string[], getLanguageFromPath, getMarkdownTheme, getSelectListTheme, getEditorTheme, getSettingsListTheme, getInteractiveScrollbarTrackStyle/getInteractiveScrollbarThumbStyle, getInteractiveChromeBorderStyle/getInteractiveChromeBorderColor, setInteractiveChromeThemeOverride.

Exported supporting type (verbatim):
```ts
export type HighlightFormatter = (text: string) => string;
```
Source: `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/syntax-highlight.ts:4-4`.

renderHighlightedHtml(html:string, theme:HighlightTheme={}):string; HighlightFormatter is the named formatter alias in the verbatim declaration.
entries.dependency_text: Uses highlight.js and the shared HTML entity decoder. TUI-010 overlays appearance presentations; TUI-024 installs live chrome overrides. Terminal worker owns Markdown parsing/layout and primitive controls. MISC-025 owns single-pass HTML entity decoding; the span parser and inherited syntax scope behavior remain here.
entries.rust: Native Highlighter is a stateful handwritten tokenizer, invoked on fenced Markdown lines before ANSI-aware wrapping (`rust:crates/ice-tui/src/syntax_highlight.rs:15-65`, `rust:crates/ice-tui/src/syntax_highlight.rs:212-397`, `rust:crates/ice-tui/src/markdown.rs:221-246`, `rust:crates/ice-tui/src/markdown.rs:669-694`). It maps comments/strings/numbers/keywords to muted/success/info/accent instead of the nine syntax roles, tracks block comments only across lines, scans quoted strings on one line and broadly consumes alphanumeric/dot/underscore numeric tokens. Unknown languages receive base code color. All SlashSlash profiles use Rust keywords and all Hash profiles Python keywords, despite unused per-language tables for JS/Go/C/shell; SQL keywords are uppercase-only. The first general '#' line-comment branch also makes a later whitespace guard ineffective. It lacks highlight.js scopes, regex/template semantics, language coverage and diff addition/deletion token styles. Native tests cover basic Rust/comments/string/JSON but do not establish those missing contracts (`rust:crates/ice-tui/src/syntax_highlight.rs:431-491`). Native Theme contains Markdown/chrome color roles, but no equivalent appearance override adapter object (`rust:crates/ice-tui/src/theme.rs:1-133`, `rust:crates/ice-tui/src/theme.rs:343-386`).
entries.port: Extend ice-tui highlighting with per-language grammar/token state and a semantic syntax palette, or adopt a maintained Rust highlighter behind the same fallback contract. Preserve unknown-language behavior and distinguish raw versus colored error fallback deliberately. Add language/path alias and nested-scope/entity tests, plus JS/Go/shell keyword and diff/regex/HTML cases. Keep chrome formatting live across theme/appearance changes and explicitly invalidate captured border/cursor values.

entries.title: Unicode, Nerd Font and ASCII symbol presets with locale defaults
entries.what: Chooses a consistent set of glyphs for the prompt, tool status, Git/footer indicators and interface borders, including an ASCII fallback for terminals and locales.
entries.mechanism:
The process-local preset initializes from environment, can be set explicitly and is read by sym(key). TERM exactly dumb selects ASCII; otherwise the first nonempty LC_ALL, LC_CTYPE, LANG is inspected for utf8 or utf-8 case-insensitively. An explicitly non-UTF-8 locale selects ASCII; no locale selects Unicode. The Nerd Font preset is never auto-detected.

The 22 keys are logo, bullet, toolPending, toolSuccess, branch, ahead, behind, dirty, gutter, boxTopLeft, boxTopRight, boxBottomLeft, boxBottomRight, boxHorizontal, boxVertical, separator, ellipsis, warning, error, update, prompt, runDone. Unicode values in that order are ❄,●,›,✓,⎇,↑,↓,±,⎿,╭,╮,╰,╯,─,│,·,…,⚠,✗,↑,❯,✻. Nerd copies Unicode except logo U+F0717, warning U+F071, error U+F057, update U+F0AA. ASCII values are *,*,>,+,@,+,-,~, L,+,+,+,+,-,|,-,...,!, x,^,>,*. The ASCII ellipsis occupies three cells despite the module comment saying every glyph must occupy one.

getSymbolTable returns the shared table with only a compile-time Readonly type, not a frozen copy. setSymbolPreset assigns without runtime validation. Interactive apply resolves the stored symbols value auto versus an explicit preset, then replaces the default editor prompt with sym(prompt)+' '. Changing the setting persists it, reapplies the prompt, invalidates chat and requests rendering; components that call sym dynamically pick up the current table.
entries.interfaces: SymbolPreset='unicode'|'nerd'|'ascii'; setting symbols adds 'auto' (storage owned by SET-017). resolveDefaultSymbolPreset(env), setSymbolPreset, getSymbolPreset, sym(SymbolKey), getSymbolTable(preset). Environment names TERM, LC_ALL, LC_CTYPE, LANG with the exact precedence described.
entries.dependency_text: Glyph consumers include footer, message/tool panels, status and editor prompt. Font availability and terminal width handling are external conditions, not inferred from the selected preset.
entries.rust: The explicit crates-wide search for symbol preset, Nerd Font, locale precedence and named glyph keys found no equivalent registry or auto-selection. Native Theme contains a border style and fixed preset palette (`rust:crates/ice-tui/src/theme.rs:133-209`), and native assistant/user components use their own fixed glyph/text formatting (`rust:crates/ice-tui/src/assistant_message.rs:147-176`, `rust:crates/ice-tui/src/user_message.rs:58-83`). These do not provide a shared Unicode/Nerd/ASCII table or locale-based selection.
entries.port: Add a shared symbol registry in ice-tui with explicit/auto selection and a settings bridge in ice-cli. Route all glyph consumers through it and test actual visible widths, especially the three-cell ASCII ellipsis and font-dependent private-use glyphs. Preserve the exact environment precedence and avoid assuming a Nerd Font is installed.

entries.title: Terminal background detection and automatic light/dark theme synchronization
entries.what: Chooses an initial palette from the terminal background and can follow terminal appearance changes using a paired lightTheme/darkTheme setting.
entries.mechanism:
A single theme name is fixed, while a setting with exactly one slash selects a light and a dark palette. The interactive controller queries terminal hints, falls back to environment evidence and keeps automatic settings synchronized with later terminal color-scheme notifications.

parseAutoThemeSetting returns undefined for absent/empty strings, zero or multiple slashes, or either trimmed side being empty. A valid pair returns trimmed lightTheme/darkTheme. resolveThemeSetting selects a side by terminalTheme; malformed strings containing slash return undefined; other strings are returned unchanged. COLORFGBG detection splits semicolons and scans backward, parseInt-parsing each trimmed field until an integer 0..255 is found; it can therefore skip an invalid trailing field. ANSI index→RGB uses the fixed palette described in TUI-004. RGB luminance linearizes each channel c/255 using c<=0.03928 ? c/12.92 : ((c+0.055)/1.055)^2.4, then weights 0.2126/0.7152/0.0722; luminance>=0.5 means light. Valid COLORFGBG evidence is high confidence; no valid hint gives dark/fallback/low (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/theme.ts:832-937`).

Background detection first awaits ui.queryTerminalBackgroundColor({timeoutMs}); an RGB answer returns high-confidence terminal-background evidence. Missing/error answers fall back to COLORFGBG. Automatic detection first tries optional queryTerminalColorScheme with the same timeout; if absent/failing it performs background detection. These two sequential queries can each consume their timeout. getDefaultTheme uses environment detection only (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/theme.ts:939-977`).

Controller construction derives terminalTheme from environment, resolves settings.getThemeSetting, initializes with watching and binds one terminal color-scheme callback. applyFromSettings on a pair queries with timeout 100 ms, enables notifications and applies the appropriate palette. For an explicit nonpair setting it disables automatic sync and applies the setting. With no setting it queries background at 100 ms, applies the detected palette, and persists/flushes only high-confidence detection; low-confidence fallback remains unpersisted. setThemeName/setThemeInstance disable automatic sync. rebindTui unsubscribes the previous callback, rebinds and restores the enabled notification state (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/theme-controller.ts:18-79`).

A notification is ignored unless automatic sync is enabled. Otherwise it updates terminalTheme, re-reads the current setting, disables sync if no longer a pair, and applies the selected side only when it differs from activeThemeName. Preview resolves against the recorded terminalTheme without itself changing automatic enablement. UI invalidation occurs through the controller's notifyChanged callback (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/theme-controller.ts:82-140`).
entries.dependency_text: Requires terminal color-query and notification primitives from the low-level TUI fragment; no external service. SET-017 owns theme setting access/persistence.
entries.rust: Reviewed startup matches only Some('light'), Some('monochrome') and Some('dark') and applies those presets; all other names, including a slash pair, are ignored by this block (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui.rs:972-984`). The native preset enum and manager have no automatic pair or terminal-background resolver (`rust:crates/ice-tui/src/theme.rs:343-386`, `rust:crates/ice-tui/src/theme.rs:499-505`). Direct theme selection rejects unknown strings (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/commands.rs:328-343`). Terminal primitive availability is being independently compared in the terminal fragment; it does not establish this controller wiring.
entries.port: Add an interactive theme controller over existing theme state, terminal color queries and notification hooks. Preserve 100 ms query timeouts and confidence-based first-run persistence or document changed timing. Re-check the effective setting when notifications arrive, and detach/rebind listeners when terminal ownership changes. Ensure automatic changes invalidate component caches through the existing native revision mechanism.
entries.priority_reason: Keeps light/dark palettes readable across terminal appearance changes and first-run defaults.

entries.title: Active custom-theme file watching, debounce and error retention
entries.what: Updates the active custom palette after edits while retaining the last valid palette during transient missing or malformed files.
entries.mechanism:
Starting a theme watch closes the old watcher/timer and watches the custom-theme directory for the active name's JSON file. Reloads are debounced 100 ms, ignore stale theme names, and retain the previous valid palette when a save is incomplete.

The watch is skipped only for absent currentThemeName or exact dark/light names. It derives getCustomThemesDir()/currentName.json and requires that file to exist before starting. It does not use Theme.sourcePath, so project/package themes or custom filenames differing from content names do not automatically get source-path watching through this function. The comment says built-ins are skipped, but only dark/light are explicitly excluded; another built-in name can watch a colliding custom filename (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/theme.ts:1068-1084`).

Each matching filename event, or an event without a filename, clears the pending timer and schedules a 100 ms reload. At firing it clears the timer slot, verifies currentThemeName still equals the captured name, and returns if the file is absent. It loads/validates/constructs from that path, replaces the registry entry under the captured name, installs the global palette and invokes the change callback. Any error in that try block is ignored. A changed content name is not compared against the captured name, so the registry key and runtime Theme.name can diverge (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/theme.ts:1086-1138`).

The filesystem helper wraps fs.watch construction, registers the supplied error callback, and returns null after construction failure. The theme error callback closes the watcher and clears its slot. Although the helper exports FS_WATCH_RETRY_DELAY_MS=5000, neither this helper nor the theme error callback schedules a retry. stopThemeWatcher cancels the timeout and closes/clears the watcher; closeWatcher suppresses close errors. Installing an in-memory theme always stops watching (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/theme.ts:1055-1062`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/theme.ts:1134-1148`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/fs-watch.ts:1-31`).
entries.interfaces: start is internal, selected through initTheme(name, true) or setTheme(name, true). Public stopThemeWatcher():void; onThemeChange registers the one repaint callback. Watched path is customThemesDir/currentThemeName.json, with exact filename equality, case-sensitive .json convention and debounce 100 ms. No user-state path was opened during this audit.
entries.dependency_text: Depends on filesystem watch support and global theme state; resource source-path discovery is SET-033. No external service.
entries.rust: Rust has watch_paths/watch_path polling mtime/existence, default 1000 ms and 5000 ms retry after a caught snapshot panic. It retains a stop flag; close sets it and aborts the JoinHandle, while Drop sets the flag but does not await completion (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/fs_watch.rs:18-112`). Its comment claiming Drop does not stop watching is contradicted by lines 56–59. The sole production call found in the focused ice-cli search watches .git/HEAD for footer branch updates (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui.rs:1126-1134`), not a theme file. No JSON theme loader or active-theme reload callback exists in the reviewed theme paths. Keep the existing general watcher; do not equate its presence with theme hot reload.
entries.port: Wire a watcher to the selected imported theme and rebuild/swap its palette on successful validation. Retain the last valid state on transient file errors, cancel pending work on theme switches, and use revision-based rendering invalidation. Decide whether to watch the actual sourcePath for project/package/content-renamed themes and whether to retry watcher failures; these would improve on the narrower TS path/error behavior and should be documented.
entries.priority_reason: Enables iterative theme customization without restarting a session.

entries.source:

entries.what: Stores user-selected layout, decoration, text styling and animation separately from the color palette, and loads older appearance preferences with deterministic defaults.
entries.mechanism:
Validation produces a complete v2 appearance object together with path-specific issues. Missing sections receive defaults, malformed scalar values often normalize silently, and explicit format, color, enum or structural errors make valid=false while still returning a normalized object.

validateAppearance(undefined) succeeds with defaults; a non-record or version other than 1/2 fails and returns defaults. Version 1 migrates then validates. Migration overlays legacy userMessage/inputBox and thinking label/block, copies the legacy thinking indicator into both thinking.indicator and statusIndicators.working, preserves tableStyle, and adds caseSensitive:true to well-shaped legacy literal rules; malformed entries remain available for diagnostics. New v2 sections retain stock defaults (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/appearance-migrate.ts:16-71`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/appearance-validate.ts:419-463`).

General normalization uses floor and clamp for finite numeric values, fallback for other types; styles filter to allowed names and deduplicate in original order without issues; booleans accept only actual booleans. PaddingX is 0..8 and paddingY 0..4. Indicator interval is 16..5000 ms; at most the first 128 supplied frames are considered, each nonempty and <=64 UTF-8 bytes; invalid entries are skipped and an empty result is an issue. Thinking verbs consider the first 256 entries, trim/deduplicate, require nonempty strings <=128 UTF-8 bytes; empty result is an issue. The two format fields allow <=512 UTF-8 bytes and exactly one {message}/{verb}; other placeholders matching {letter[letters, digits,_,-]*} fail. These format/frame/verb checks do not reject all control characters. Hidden thinking label permits empty and <=128 UTF-8 bytes, otherwise silently defaults. Invalid selection values silently become cycle (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/appearance-validate.ts:46-158`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/appearance-validate.ts:237-337`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/appearance-validate.ts:465-620`).

Color objects distinguish theme/custom/terminal-index/terminal-default/none. Theme token length is 1..128 JS code units and must belong to the foreground or background token set for its role. Custom values <=128 code units must be #RGB/#RRGGBB, rgb(integer 0..255,...) or hsl(hue 0..360, saturation/lightness 0..100%). Eight-digit alpha hex is rejected. Terminal index must be an integer 0..255. None is accepted for explicitly transparent background fields, not foreground/border roles or most TextPresentation backgrounds. Unknown kinds/tokens return the field default plus an issue (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/appearance-validate.ts:163-235`).

Footer order filters known IDs, removes duplicates, then appends omitted default IDs; visibility is normalized independently. Separator allows <=32 UTF-8 bytes and rejects C0/DEL. Heading override h1..h6 is normalized only for truthy supplied values, using the default heading base rather than the supplied shared base. Every object section is read through isRecord fallback; the main validator does not diagnose every malformed section shape. Literal rule validation examines the first 65 items, records an issue if supplied length>64, defaults missing IDs to rule-<index>, consumes IDs before matcher validation, requires literal pattern length 1..128 code units, truncates display name to 64, defaults enabled/caseSensitive unless exactly false, clamps priority 0..1000 with original index fallback. A failed validation may therefore return 65 normalized rules, but callers must honor valid=false (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/appearance-validate.ts:106-135`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/appearance-validate.ts:352-417`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/appearance-validate.ts:638-693`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/appearance-validate.ts:892-1044`).

entries.rust: No appearance document, migration, profile or customizer implementation was found by a crates-wide case-insensitive Rust search for appearance/customize/theme_profile/theme_bundle. Independently read native Theme has palette, spacing and border fields but no versioned per-domain appearance model (`rust:crates/ice-tui/src/theme.rs:15-171`, `rust:crates/ice-tui/src/theme.rs:264-386`). Native user rendering exposes one output_pad and a surface background (`rust:crates/ice-tui/src/user_message.rs:41-75`); native assistant options contain hide_thinking, hidden_thinking_label and output_pad (`rust:crates/ice-tui/src/assistant_message.rs:41-59`). These existing capabilities are a starting point, not the stored v2 contract.
entries.port: Add a serde-backed appearance module to ice-tui and global storage adapters to ice-cli through SET-017. Preserve separate palette and layout state. Implement migration and a normalized-value-plus-issues result, with explicit decisions about silently corrected inputs and character/byte bounds. entries.title: Appearance color resolution and text/Markdown presentation adapters
entries.source:
Custom color parsing: `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/appearance-colors.ts:8-94`; shared resolver: `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/appearance-resolve.ts:18-62`; text/Markdown/tool/status adapters: `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/text-presentation.ts:5-99`; user adapter: `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/user-message-presentation.ts:28-105`. Tests: `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/appearance-validate.test.ts:44-65`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/appearance-v2-runtime.test.ts:16-65`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/appearance-acceptance.test.ts:200-220`.

`AppearanceColorRole` — `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/appearance-resolve.ts:5`.
entries.what: Applies appearance foregrounds, backgrounds and text attributes consistently while letting semantic color references follow the currently selected theme.
entries.mechanism:
The shared resolver builds color functions for a foreground/background role and resolves theme tokens dynamically through the live theme proxy. Custom values are parsed once into truecolor wrappers, terminal indices retain their exact palette number, terminal-default emits a closing reset only, and none returns text unchanged.

#RGB expands each nibble; #RRGGBB requires all six hex digits. rgb accepts three decimal integers 0..255. hsl accepts positive decimal hue 0..360 and percentages 0..100; standard sector conversion rounds/clamps each channel. Invalid direct parser input returns null and custom wrapper becomes identity. Custom output always uses 38;2/48;2 and ends 39/49, with no terminal capability downgrade. Terminal-index emits 38;5/48;5 and 39/49. Unknown/mismatched theme-role tokens become identity. resolveAppearanceColorDecoration applies the wrapper around a NUL sentinel then extracts prefix/suffix (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/appearance-colors.ts:13-94`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/appearance-resolve.ts:18-62`).

applyTextPresentation applies foreground, then background, then wraps each configured style in array order; opens 1/3/4/9/7 and closes 22/23/24/29/27. No-override means both colors terminal-default and empty styles; composition returns the original base function in that case, preserving stock rendering. Otherwise composition calls base(applyTextPresentation(...)); it does not replace base. Markdown heading picks an h1..h6 override if present, otherwise shared base; adapters cover links, URL, inline/fenced code, quotes, rule, bullet, bold/italic/strikethrough, and set codeBlockIndent to paddingX spaces. Border color wrappers enclose existing base border styling. Full block padding/background/border application remains the component/Markdown renderer's responsibility (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/text-presentation.ts:5-79`).

Tool-state adapter picks pending/success/error background; status adapter returns spinner and label closures for each lifecycle kind. User adapter returns format/style flags/layout plus color functions; theme/custom/default/none go through shared resolver or identity, but the terminal-index case falls through to the caller fallback. Thus this user helper does not honor an otherwise valid indexed color the way the shared resolver does. The older validate-module resolveAppearanceColor lookup helper also omits terminal-index and returns undefined for it; do not claim uniform coverage from the type alone (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/text-presentation.ts:81-99`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/user-message-presentation.ts:58-105`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/appearance-validate.ts:1047-1060`).
entries.interfaces:
parseCustomColorToRgb(string) -> {r, g, b}|null; customForeground/customBackground(string)->(text)=>string; resolveAppearanceColorFn(AppearanceColor,'fg'|'bg'); resolveAppearanceColorDecoration -> {prefix, suffix}; applyTextPresentation(TextPresentation, string); markdownThemeWithAppearance(baseMarkdownTheme, MarkdownAppearance); toolStateBackground(appearance, state); statusIndicatorColors(appearance, kind). AppearanceColor is theme{token}, custom{value}, terminal-index{index}, terminal-default or none. Exact ANSI sequences and no-override semantics are described above; these functions change presentation only.

Exported supporting type (verbatim):
```ts
export type AppearanceColorRole = "fg" | "bg";
```
Source: `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/appearance-resolve.ts:5-5`.

Typed native palette fields do not resolve stored appearance colors dynamically by token. Native user Box captures surface and rebuilds on theme revision (`rust:crates/ice-tui/src/user_message.rs:41-47`, `rust:crates/ice-tui/src/user_message.rs:78-115`); assistant thinking uses a fixed italic/thinking_text base style rather than a configurable TextPresentation (`rust:crates/ice-tui/src/assistant_message.rs:257-282`).

Preserve native nested-background repair deliberately; compare it with TS attribute-specific resets. Cover indexed user colors explicitly and document that as a fix to the observed TS omission, not inherited parity.

entries.title: Appearance profile files, partial merge and legacy profile migration
entries.source:
Profile library/merge: `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/appearance-profiles.ts:16-215`; partial validation: `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/appearance-profiles.ts:221-312`; legacy migration: `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/appearance-migrate.ts:74-117`. Tests: `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/appearance-profiles.test.ts:34-64`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/appearance-profiles.test.ts:84-118`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/appearance-profiles.test.ts:126-192`.

`migrateProfileV1ToV2` — `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/appearance-migrate.ts:80`. `ProfileResult` — `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/appearance-profiles.ts:16`. `AppearanceProfileV1` — `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/appearance-types.ts:372`.
entries.what: Saves named appearance presets, duplicates or renames them, and merges selected sections into the current appearance without resetting unrelated sections.
entries.mechanism:
Profiles are JSON files in the global agent directory's appearance-profiles subdirectory. The library validates destination names, writes a temporary sibling then renames it, and exposes partial-profile application separately from filesystem operations.

Names must be nonempty/nonblank, <=64 JS code units, and match ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$. listProfiles lists lowercase .json filenames, strips suffix, sorts, and returns[] for absent directory or any error. readProfile parses JSON, requires record and string name, migrates version 1 or accepts version 2; it does not fully validate contents or require internal name to match filename. Read/delete/source-name operations do not themselves run destination-name validation (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/appearance-profiles.ts:30-47`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/appearance-profiles.ts:104-132`).

saveProfile migrates v1, rejects collisions unless overwrite, checks truthy appearance with validateAppearancePartial, and validates themeSetting shape while deferring installed-name availability. It creates the directory, writes JSON.stringify(..., null,2)+'\n' to <name>.json.tmp, then renameSync to destination. No unique temp suffix, lock or fsync is present; failure returns {success:false, error} and may leave a temp or already-written destination. Rename saves new name before unlinking old; duplicate saves a copied profile. Delete reports not found. A partial rename failure can leave both files (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/appearance-profiles.ts:134-202`).

mergeAppearancePartial clones the base, ignores the patch version and undefined values, recursively merges object/object pairs, replaces arrays or other values wholesale, and returns validateAppearance(merged).appearance without its issues. applyProfileToAppearance rejects a present non-record appearance, then delegates merge. V1 migration retains partial scope, preserves name/description, maps legacy theme string to fixed mode (including opaque slash strings), accepts a supplied typed mode discriminator, changes appearance.version to 2 and fills missing rule.caseSensitive=true (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/appearance-profiles.ts:49-72`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/appearance-profiles.ts:204-215`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/appearance-migrate.ts:80-117`).

Partial validation rejects non-record patches and malformed present object sections using paths derived from defaults, excluding color objects; it explicitly checks border enums for user/assistant/input/code/quote/bash/system and tableStyle. It then merges onto defaults and validates the already-normalized result. Because merge discarded first-pass issues, many invalid colors/formats/rules and chrome/subagent border enums can normalize before this second check; the helper is not equivalent to validating the original partial strictly. Tests cover malformed object sections and several explicit enums, not every discarded issue (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/appearance-profiles.ts:221-312`).
entries.dependency_text: Uses node:fs/path and global getAgentDir; staged UI application is separate from this immediate-write library.
entries.rust: No appearance profile directory/file model, partial merge, migration or profile CRUD counterpart was found by the recorded crates-wide behavior search. Native ThemeManager only gets/sets a Theme value and applies a predefined preset (`rust:crates/ice-tui/src/theme.rs:343-386`); direct /theme updates one settings value, not a profile (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/commands.rs:311-347`).
entries.port: Implement data-only profile serialization and scoped merge in ice-cli or a dedicated ice-tui data module with filesystem adapter. Use validated safe names and durable atomic file replacement as appropriate; separate shape checks from installed-theme availability. Decide explicitly to reject original invalid partial values rather than reproducing diagnostic loss; retain partial section semantics and v1 migration.

entries.title: Portable appearance bundles and import/export validation
entries.source:
Bundle shape: `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/appearance-types.ts:327-388`; importer/exporter: `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/appearance-profiles.ts:217-496`; theme-setting validation: `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/appearance-profiles.ts:74-102`. Tests: `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/appearance-profiles.test.ts:66-82`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/appearance-profiles.test.ts:120-143`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/appearance-acceptance.test.ts:362-378`.

`BundleImportResult` — `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/appearance-profiles.ts:314`. `AppearanceBundleV1` — `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/appearance-types.ts:380`.
entries.what: Imports or exports a portable JSON bundle containing appearance sections, palettes and named profiles without applying or writing anything during parsing.
entries.mechanism:
importBundle accepts a JSON string no larger than 256*1024 UTF-8 bytes and versions 1/2 only. It returns a normalized v2 data object or an error; actual library staging and settings changes are handled separately by the customizer.

V1 accepts a single embedded theme object, validates it with the JSON theme schema and a label derived from trimmed themeName or imported-theme, accepts a record appearance partial after changing its version to 2, and uses a trimmed themeName as fixed selection only when no truthy embedded theme exists. Name/description/author are copied only when strings. Present non-record v1 appearance is silently omitted. This path does not run the full appearance v1 migration, so its behavior is not the same as validateAppearance(version 1) copying the working indicator (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/appearance-profiles.ts:326-383`).

V2 themes must be an array<=64, each schema-parsed; profiles array<=256, each checked for nonempty name length<=64 and version 1/2. V1 profile items migrate immediately; v2 profile items validate present appearance but do not validate every profile metadata/themeSetting field here. Top-level appearance uses partial validation, inheriting its normalization limitations. Unknown top-level fields are discarded. Imported theme schemas are checked but full runtime variable resolution occurs later when draft themes are created (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/appearance-profiles.ts:385-462`).

A concrete source discrepancy exists at top-level themeSetting: importer calls validateThemeSetting(raw.themeSetting,[]), tolerates its 'is not available' failure, then assigns check.setting. Both fixed and automatic validation return before setting on availability failure, so any nonempty otherwise-valid selection produces undefined and is omitted from the returned v2 bundle. This does not affect themeSetting nested in a copied v2 profile in the same way. Record the behavior and a proposed correction; do not copy it as desirable compatibility (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/appearance-profiles.ts:74-101`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/appearance-profiles.ts:403-409`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/appearance-profiles.ts:429-461`).

exportBundle converts v1 via importBundle, otherwise treats its v2 argument as typed data, JSON-stringifies with version forced 2 and indentation 2, rejects output>256 KiB, and returns json without a trailing newline. It does not revalidate all v2 counts/content. Exceptions are converted to error strings. Parsing/export alone performs no filesystem/settings mutation (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/appearance-profiles.ts:474-496`).
entries.dependency_text: Uses data-only JSON and profile/theme validators. Customizer staging, collision decisions and activation are separate entries.
entries.rust: No appearance bundle importer/exporter or embedded palette/profile package model was found by the recorded native search. Native preset theme selection exposes three names and no portable theme JSON input (`rust:crates/ice-tui/src/theme.rs:499-505`, `rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/commands.rs:311-347`). This is distinct from session transcript export.
entries.port: Add bounded serde import/export with version migration, full original-input validation, and a separate staging API. Validate theme-setting shape without requiring an installed-name list during pure parse, then resolve availability after bundled themes are staged. Preserve raw palette values losslessly and distinguish parser success from application success.

entries.title: Custom theme file library and immediate palette editing
entries.source:
Full library implementation: `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/theme-library.ts:12-189`; tests: `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/appearance-theme-library.test.ts:34-87`; JSON versus runtime validation: `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/theme/theme.ts:693-811`.

`ThemeLibraryResult` — `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/theme-library.ts:12`.
entries.what: Creates writable copies of palettes, edits or resets individual colors, and renames, deletes, imports or exports custom theme files.
entries.mechanism:
The library operates on <customThemesDir>/<name>.json and returns success/error objects for writes. It is an immediate filesystem API; the customizer uses a separate in-memory draft so preview operations do not call these writes until apply.

Destination names must be nonblank, <=64 code units and ASCII alphanumeric first followed by alphanumerics/dash/underscore; slash, backslash and '..' are explicitly rejected. isCustomTheme checks only existence of that global filename. readThemeData uses an explicit existing path first, then the global custom file, and schema-parses JSON; otherwise it throws. Source/read/delete names are not checked by the destination validator (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/theme-library.ts:17-48`).

writeThemeFile creates the custom directory, schema-validates a copy with name overridden, writes pretty JSON plus newline to fixed sibling .json.tmp, renames to destination, then runtime-loads that file. Runtime variable/color validation therefore occurs after replacement: load failure can return failure while the destination has already changed. No lock, unique temp name, fsync or rollback appears. save/import reject existing custom destinations unless overwrite is explicitly supported; clone uses catalog source.path and fails if it has no readable file; rename writes new before deleting old. Delete removes only the global custom file. Built-in name collisions are judged by global custom-file existence in these immediate functions, not by the entire registry (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/theme-library.ts:69-137`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/theme-library.ts:177-189`).

Color edit precheck allows integer 0..255, empty, #RGB/#RRGGBB, bounded rgb, syntactic hsl and variable identifiers <=128 code units. Its HSL check does not bound numeric ranges, and the theme runtime expects six-digit hex or variables rather than RGB/HSL strings; passing this precheck is not proof of runtime acceptance. setThemeTokenValue requires an existing custom file and token membership, then writes. resetThemeToken copies one value from a source palette's color map without copying its vars; a copied variable reference may fail runtime load after disk replacement. Export returns indented JSON without trailing newline (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/theme-library.ts:50-67`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/theme-library.ts:139-175`).

entries.rust: Native theme code has no custom palette file library, JSON loader or individual semantic-token edit API; only typed presets and ThemeManager mutation exist (`rust:crates/ice-tui/src/theme.rs:343-386`, `rust:crates/ice-tui/src/theme.rs:499-505`). Native /theme accepts three names and persists a setting (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/commands.rs:311-347`).
entries.port: Implement file-backed palette CRUD in ice-cli with full schema and runtime validation before replacement. Preserve safe-name and write-before-delete behavior, while making rollback/durability and collisions explicit. Use serde_json and the TUI-001 resolver; do not retain a precheck that accepts syntax unsupported by the actual runtime.

entries.title: In-memory theme drafts, variable editing and retryable apply phases
entries.what: Lets users preview palette selection, clones, renames, deletions and variable changes without writing files until they apply the draft.
entries.mechanism:
A ThemeDraftSession tracks selected name, staged entries and deleted original names. It reads palette data lazily, returns copies, constructs preview themes through full runtime validation, and splits persistence into destination writes followed by original deletions.

Construction chooses the requested name if currently available, otherwise first available or dark. listThemes dynamically combines current catalog names minus deleted originals plus staged names, then sorts. Selection validates that list. Editable means staged entry or global custom file; built-ins require a clone. Entries track originalName, isNew, dirty, baseName, written. Cloning deep-copies current JSON, selects new name, records its source base. Rename marks original for later deletion and retains provenance; deleting a new draft drops it, deleting existing custom stages removal and selects first remaining name/dark (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/theme-draft-session.ts:46-162`).

setToken requires the permissive library color precheck and existing token, changes value, runtime-validates complete JSON, marks dirty or restores that value. setVariable requires ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$, changes/adds a var and validates; failure restores/deletes that var. Whole-theme reset copies named/base/dark palette with current name. Token reset copies a base token and then validates but does not restore its mutation on failure. Import validates destination name, rejects existing name unless replace, permits replacement only when isCustomTheme(name), runtime-validates, stages data/provenance and selects it; this also means a newly staged but not-yet-written name is not replaceable via this path (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/theme-draft-session.ts:164-257`).

Variable rename rewrites exact string references across colors, vars and export, renames the var key, validates and restores a full backup on failure. Delete removes var then validates/restores. Runtime creation resolves referenced color vars, so the comment 'reject while references remain' is limited by what runtime construction actually resolves; export-only references and unused variable chains require separate scrutiny. variableReferences enumerates exact matching colors, other vars and export fields; errors produce[] (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/theme-draft-session.ts:259-342`).

commitWrites first runtime-validates every staged entry, then writes entries that are new/dirty/renamed in insertion order. Overwrite is allowed after successful previous write, or for an existing entry retaining its original name. Successful entries mark written=true; failure stops and retains retry state, so prior destinations may exist. commitDeletes then iterates deleted originals, skips ones still staged or no longer custom, deletes and stops on error. It does not clear the theme entries/deletion set after success. commit chains writes/deletes and returns selectedTheme. Dropping the draft before an apply writes nothing; cancel after partial persistence cannot undo already-completed writes (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/theme-draft-session.ts:344-390`).
entries.dependency_text: Filesystem writes are delegated to the immediate custom-theme library only during commit phases.
entries.rust: No native theme-draft transaction, palette-variable editor or split write/delete API was found. Native /theme changes the global manager immediately (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/commands.rs:311-347`); its selector changes live theme on select without a staged palette document (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/selectors.rs:449-517`).
entries.port: Add a draft model independent of rendering and disk I/O, with explicit originals/destinations and validation-before-write. Preserve raw variable references and exact rename mapping; restore failed token resets and validate export references intentionally. Define recovery for partial commits and refresh baselines after successful apply.
entries.priority_reason: Makes interactive palette editing cancelable and protects existing files during rename/import.

entries.title: Staged profile-library changes and overwrite-safe retries
entries.source: Full staging class: `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/profile-draft-session.ts:20-154`; combined-session caller: `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/customization-draft-session.ts:359-397`; profile behavior tests: `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/appearance-acceptance.test.ts:250-308`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/appearance-acceptance.test.ts:349-360`.
entries.what: Stages profile creation, replacement, rename, duplicate and delete alongside a customization session, with no filesystem changes before apply.
entries.mechanism:
The profile draft overlays a Map of staged content on the current disk name list and a Set of deleted names. It separately tracks names already written so a failed apply can retry destinations without collision failures.

listNames takes current files excluding deleted/shadowed names, adds staged names and sorts. exists uses staged or currently-listed nondeleted files. get returns a staged deep copy, otherwise reads a disk profile (including v1 migration) and swallows read errors as undefined. Save validates ASCII safe names<=64; existing disk name requires replace, while an already-staged name can be edited without that flag. It clears deletion intent for the saved name and stores a deep clone; content validation waits for commit. Delete removes staged/written state and marks existing disk names deleted. Rename reads original, validates noncolliding destination, stages deletion then saves copied name; duplicate just saves copied content (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/profile-draft-session.ts:27-105`).

commitWrites checks every staged profile's truthy themeSetting against the supplied available-theme list before writing any profile. It then saves in insertion order; overwrite is true if name was successfully written before or is currently listed on disk. This disk recheck means a file that appears after staging can be overwritten. saveProfile validates each appearance only as that profile is reached, so a later invalid profile can fail after earlier profile writes. Successful names enter written. commitDeletes skips names still staged or absent on disk, deletes in Set order and stops on error; only complete success clears staged/deleted/written. commit chains phases. Pure staging/cancel has zero writes, but there is no rollback of a partial commit (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/profile-draft-session.ts:108-154`).
entries.interfaces: ProfileDraftSession: listNames, exists, get, save(profile,{replace?}), delete, rename, duplicate, hasStagedChanges, commitWrites(availableThemes), commitDeletes, commit(availableThemes). All mutation results use {success:boolean, error?:string}; get returns AppearanceProfileV2|undefined. Destination names follow TUI-011 restrictions.
entries.dependency_text: Uses immediate profile library for reads and final writes/deletes. TUI-016 coordinates theme/profile/settings ordering.
entries.rust: No native profile library or staging state was found; native ThemeManager/setters hold current theme only (`rust:crates/ice-tui/src/theme.rs:343-386`). Native CLI theme changes do not expose a profile transaction (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/commands.rs:311-347`).
entries.port: Implement a staged profile overlay with explicit collision policy and prior-file identity checks if preserving external changes matters. Validate every staged profile's original content before any write, expose partial-commit recovery, and clear staging only after the chosen success boundary.
