entries.title: Unified appearance/theme customization preview, reset, apply and cancel
entries.source:
Appearance preview controller: `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/appearance-controller.ts:12-75`; complete coordinator: `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/customization-draft-session.ts:14-410`. Tests: `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/appearance-controller.test.ts:23-86`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/appearance-acceptance.test.ts:149-198`.

`CustomizationApplyResult` — `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/customization-draft-session.ts:14`.
entries.what: Keeps a single customization draft across appearance settings, theme selection and library edits, supports preview/reset/cancel, and applies the selected state in a defined order.
entries.mechanism:
InteractiveAppearanceController captures a settings baseline and at most one preview. Getters clone; beginPreview refreshes baseline only when not already previewing; valid preview replaces in-memory effective state and calls onChanged; invalid preview leaves state untouched. Commit validates, delegates to SettingsManager.setAppearanceSettings, updates baseline and clears preview only on valid result. Rollback clears preview without writing; refreshBaseline updates from settings and notifies only when not previewing. Callback or settings exceptions are not swallowed (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/appearance-controller.ts:18-75`).

CustomizationDraftSession captures typed theme setting from settings or fixed fallback, terminal dark/light value, a ThemeDraftSession and ProfileDraftSession. It uses previewSide terminal/light/dark to resolve automatic pairs. Fixed-to-automatic copies current theme into both members; automatic-to-fixed chooses the currently previewed member and resets side to terminal. Name setters mutate selection state and invoke draft.select without surfacing that result; final apply checks availability. Its loadProfile merges only appearance; UI separately controls whether profile themeSetting is adopted (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/customization-draft-session.ts:92-234`).

Dirty checks compare JSON.stringify values for the full appearance, each named section and theme setting, plus staged library state. ResetSection copies its captured baseline section (array replacement; object existing keys copied) then previews. resetAll rolls appearance back and reconstructs both drafts from baseline theme setting; it does not reload a new external settings baseline. Cancel similarly rolls back and reconstructs drafts, then resets previewSide; neither reverts already-persisted partial apply files (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/customization-draft-session.ts:236-348`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/customization-draft-session.ts:400-409`).

Apply order is: validate selected theme members against draft list; validate current appearance; themeDraft.commitWrites; profileDraft.commitWrites(availableThemes); setAppearanceThemeSetting; appearanceController.commit; themeDraft.commitDeletes; profileDraft.commitDeletes; return concrete selected theme. Each explicit failure stops later phases. The comment says every staged surface validates before writes, but profile validation begins after theme destinations may already be written, and individual profile appearance checks occur during saves. Theme settings may be persisted before appearance commit fails; cleanup failures occur after both setting updates. There is no all-files/settings rollback, locking or asynchronous flush wait in this coordinator. Selected theme returned uses the preview side, which may differ from the captured terminal member in automatic mode. Actual overlay/runtime refresh after return is audited with the customizer caller (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/customization-draft-session.ts:352-398`).

Validate all destination data first, make failures/retries reviewable, and decide whether settings/library atomicity or compensating rollback is required. Keep terminal theme synchronization separate from preview-side editing and restore runtime state on close.

entries.title: Literal input highlighting with stable source offsets and overlap priority
entries.what: Highlights selected literal phrases in the editor without changing the text used for cursor movement, undo, history, paste or submission.
entries.mechanism:
The engine receives a plain source line and returns nonoverlapping spans indexed by JavaScript code-unit offsets. It selects enabled literal rules, sorts by numeric priority, lets earlier priority/order claim complete ranges, then converts spans into ANSI decorations at rendering time.

It filters enabled/literal rules before taking first 64; stable sort lower priority wins. Patterns must have length 1..128 code units. Case-sensitive scan uses indexOf and advances by pattern length, so it finds nonoverlapping occurrences. Case-insensitive scan folds ASCII A..Z only and checks every source offset, preserving length and allowing overlapping candidate matches; non-ASCII code units compare exactly. Each rule first computes all matches, so scan/match-list cost is not bounded by the later span cap. At most the first 256 candidate matches per rule are considered, including those rejected for overlap; total accepted spans<=1024. Any claimed code unit rejects the entire candidate. Results sort by start (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/input-highlighters.ts:22-65`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/input-highlighters.ts:102-136`).

Accepted spans copy styles and color prefixes from the shared resolver. Terminal-default/none have no prefix and become null here. Style opens are emitted in order with closes prepended in reverse. spanToDecoration combines fg, bg, styles and closes styles then bg then fg; applyHighlightSpans assumes sorted spans, skips any starting before current cursor, copies intervening/source text and closes styles then fg then bg. Neither mutates the original line. These are UTF-16 offsets rather than display columns or grapheme indices; the editor adapter must preserve that mapping (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/input-highlighters.ts:67-100`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/input-highlighters.ts:138-169`).

Low-level editor support must be assessed through the coordinated terminal fragment before claiming a rendering backend is absent.
entries.port: Add a bounded literal-span engine and editor decoration interface to ice-tui, with explicit UTF-8/UTF-16/grapheme offset conversion. Stop match collection at the relevant cap to bound allocation while preserving documented priority and overlap decisions. Keep source text separate from styled output.

entries.title: Thinking verb selection, indicator mirroring and text styling helpers
entries.what: Customizes the words, frame sequence and text style used to present thinking activity and thinking blocks.
entries.mechanism:
ThinkingVerbSelector cycles through configured words with a resettable index or chooses using an injectable random-number function. Empty or out-of-range selection falls back to Thinking. The constructor retains the provided array; format replacement uses split/join for every {verb}, while validation elsewhere requires exactly one.

getThinkingIndicatorFrames returns a copy when reverseMirror is false. When true, zero/one frames remain unchanged; exactly two become [a, b, a]; three or more append reversed interior frames, for example[a, b, c, b]. The two-frame special case repeats a across the cycle boundary despite the comment describing unduplicated edges. styleThinkingBlockText checks membership in a fixed order bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, inverse, independent of the order in the input style list, and calls supplied functions (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/thinking-presentation.ts:3-60`).

Stock frames and 80 ms interval match the common braille spinner, and stock verbs are Thinking, Reasoning, Considering, Working, Analyzing, Planning. Per-kind status indicator frame scheduling and live update wiring are separate component contracts; this module returns data/strings and does not schedule timers.

entries.title: Appearance customizer viewport, navigation, draft validation and disposal
entries.source:
Customizer shell and controls: `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/appearance-customizer.ts:41-52`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/appearance-customizer.ts:210-435`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/appearance-customizer.ts:470-630`; viewport/focus tests: `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/appearance-customizer.test.ts:69-141`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/appearance-customizer.test.ts:174-242`.

`AppearanceProfileActionResult` — `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/appearance-customizer.ts:36`. `AppearanceCustomizerCallbacks` — `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/appearance-customizer.ts:41`.
entries.what: A full-screen appearance editor presents a searchable settings tree beside a live preview and applies or discards an existing customization draft.
entries.mechanism:
The constructor snapshots the session appearance and selected theme, builds a root SettingsList with at most 20 visible items and search enabled, and owns an AppearancePreviewComponent. Tab switches settings/preview focus before submenu input handling, so Tab is intercepted even in text editors. Preview up/down moves one row, page actions move by preview height, and cancel returns focus to settings; root cancel delegates the supplied callback. dispose stops preview activity.

Rendering uses the terminal row count, default 48, reserving two hint rows. Below width 104 it stacks settings above a preview capped at 10 rows and 40% of the body; at 104 or wider the left pane is min(56, floor((width-3)*.45)), with a three-cell separator and remaining width for preview. Each line is visibly truncated/padded, and output is clipped to height. The preview's own first three heading rows are discarded, a pane heading reports visible range, scroll is clamped, and blank rows fill the viewport. List fitting repeatedly reduces maxVisible until it fits. Nested shells have breadcrumbs, optional inline errors, at most 14 initial rows, and hard-coded Enter/Esc hints; structural actions rebuild lists, whereas ordinary updates synchronize values/descriptions/labels.

Root sections cover theme, user/input, three thinking sections, assistant/Markdown/tools/Bash/diff/system/status/footer/chrome/subagent, highlighters, profiles and import/export, plus preview scene, apply and reset. emit passes the local draft through session validation. Invalid edits restore the last effective draft and refresh root items without invoking preview/callback; valid edits clone the normalized result into the preview and onDraftChange. A successful edit does not explicitly clear an earlier themeError. Reset clears pending imports and resets the combined session, then emits appearance; theme instance preview is not directly invoked by that root action. Applying and canceling are callback contracts; filesystem transaction semantics belong to TUI-016.
entries.dependency_text: Uses SettingsList, ExtensionInputComponent and terminal width/keybinding utilities; primitive behavior is covered by the TUI terminal fragment.
entries.rust: Native /settings constructs a single SettingsList and immediately persists value changes. Submenus replace the active selector; cancel returns to the editor. Its complete row builder has theme/model/thinking/scope and operational settings but no appearance customizer, staged Apply/Cancel tree or side preview (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/settings.rs:51-287`). The native /theme selector contains three presets (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/selectors.rs:449-506`). These existing primitives do not implement this screen.
entries.port: Build the customizer over native settings/overlay primitives with explicit draft ownership, deterministic viewport fitting, focus transfer, validation feedback and disposal. Preserve existing settings behavior unless deliberately changing it. Cover narrow/wide layouts, nested cancel, preview scrolling, failed edits and overlay teardown with behavioral tests.

entries.title: Appearance field controls, shared color editor and highlighter-rule editor
entries.source: Color/text editors: `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/appearance-customizer.ts:632-882`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/appearance-customizer.ts:884-1037`; field construction/routing: `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/appearance-customizer.ts:1039-1596`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/appearance-customizer.ts:1611-1758`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/appearance-customizer.ts:1917-2272`; selected tests: `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/appearance-customizer.test.ts:404-418`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/appearance-customizer.test.ts:559-586`.
entries.what: Exposes concrete appearance settings as searchable field controls, nested color editors and editable literal input-highlighter rules.
entries.mechanism:
The shared color screen stages a local color until Accept; cancel discards it. Modes are semantic token, hex, RGB, HSL, terminal index and terminal default, with none only when allowed. Background token choices contain the seven background roles; foreground choices omit syntax tokens even though those are valid theme foreground roles. Hex is accepted only when valid; invalid input is silently retained. RGB uses parseInt then 0..255 clamps; HSL uses parseFloat with H0..360/S, L0..100 clamps and rounding; mode changes construct values from stored channels. Terminal indexes offer 0..9,15,39,201,255 plus exact entry; parseInt permits a numeric prefix such as 39x, and out-of-range input sets an inline error. Local text fields use the single-line ExtensionInput component; long values receive a whitespace-collapsed 60-character summary, not a distinct multiline editor. Connector redaction at source line 883 prevented inspection of that one expression; adjacent explicit token lists, filters and change handling were read and no bypass was attempted.

The UI is a subset of the v2 model. User fields expose format,11 border styles, fit-to-content, both paddings, five styles and fg/bg/border colors. Input exposes five borders, horizontal padding and idle/active colors. Thinking exposes frame presets/pipe-separated strings, mirror, selected interval values, color, word presets/list, cycle/random, label format and block visibility/style/fg. Assistant exposes borders/paddings/background. Markdown exposes table style, selected text foregrounds and code/quote border style, omitting many modeled presentations and geometry fields. Tools expose title/output fg and three state backgrounds; Bash exposes border/padding and command/output/status fg. System cards omit their modeled background control. Status controls expose color/interval/label fg but omit frame/mirror/style editing. Chrome and subagent controls omit selectedStyles. Footer exposes separator/order/colors and visibility checkboxes.

Confirmed TS routing discrepancies are preserved as behavior, not intended requirements. applySectionField splits rowId with a two-element limit: footer.visible.cwd yields rest='visible', so the later rest.startsWith('visible.') branch cannot toggle any footer visibility field (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/appearance-customizer.ts:1917-1921`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/appearance-customizer.ts:2092-2108`). User-message color routing accepts theme/custom/default and allowed none but rejects terminal-index even though the color screen offers it (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/appearance-customizer.ts:1939-1953`).

Highlighter creation trims a nonempty pattern of at most 128 characters, enforces fewer than 64 rules, derives a lowercase sanitized 32-character ID with numeric suffix, and defaults to enabled/case-sensitive/bold/yellow foreground/default background with priority=array length. Rules can edit matcher/name/priority 0..1000/styles/colors, toggle/delete, insert TODO/FIXME/NOTE presets, or move array positions. Moving does not change priority, so priority sorting in TUI-017 can preserve old precedence. Style routing splits on colon and assumes IDs contain none, although imported IDs are not constrained that way. Every mutation ultimately passes normalization through the combined draft.
entries.interfaces: Field IDs name the corresponding v2 sections, with nested color summaries theme:<token>, custom:<color>, index:<n>, default, none. Color modes and editor preset choices are UI values, not additional persisted schema fields. highlighters.addCustom/addPreset/clearAll and per-ID enabled/case/name/pattern/priority/move/delete/color/style actions operate on inputHighlighters.
entries.dependency_text: The complete persisted field contract and normalization limits remain TUI-009; this entry records actual editable controls and their routing.
entries.rust: The native settings row builder exposes operational scalar settings and a three-preset theme submenu, with no appearance color/mode editor or highlighter-rule controls (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/settings.rs:155-287`, `rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/settings.rs:390-433`). The explicit crates-wide source search for appearance/customize/highlighter/theme_profile/theme_bundle/symbol_preset found syntax highlighting but no counterpart to this configuration editor.
entries.port: Implement typed field routing and a shared validated color editor. Preserve the complete v2 model even where TS UI exposes only a subset. Deliberately correct nested footer visibility and terminal-index routing, test imported IDs and priority-vs-order behavior, and keep invalid input in the editor with useful feedback instead of confusing silent reversion.

entries.title: Customizer theme editor, token groups, variables and staged-selection divergence
entries.source: Theme editor: `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/appearance-customizer.ts:2624-3110`; typed draft selection: `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/customization-draft-session.ts:95-175`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/customization-draft-session.ts:359-397`; group/collision tests: `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/appearance-customizer.test.ts:304-384`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/appearance-customizer.test.ts:588-617`.
entries.what: Lets users preview and stage theme choices, edit palette tokens and variables, and manage custom theme files within the appearance draft.
entries.mechanism:
The screen groups tokens into Core, Messages, Tools, Markdown, Diff, Syntax and Thinking levels, with a separate variable screen. It only lists tokens present in the selected raw JSON, so absent optional tokens have no field. Token controls offer nine hex presets and numeric 0/8/15 plus exact entry; all-digit input becomes Number, otherwise the string is retained and checked by ThemeDraft. Variable actions create a default black value, edit, rename exact references or remove variables. ThemeDraft validation and mutation rollback limitations are TUI-014.

Mode controls operate on the combined session's typed fixed/automatic selection; automatic member selectors and preview side call the corresponding session methods. Fixed theme selection instead calls ThemeDraft.select and updates the component's selectedTheme and preview, without calling CustomizationDraftSession.setFixedTheme. Clone, rename, import and deletion similarly manipulate ThemeDraft selection without synchronizing the typed themeSettingDraft. The main runtime onThemePreview merely installs the supplied theme instance, and Apply invokes session.apply using the unchanged typed setting. Therefore selecting a different fixed theme can preview it yet persist the previous fixed theme; renaming/deleting the currently configured theme can make typed-selection validation fail. This is a source-confirmed wiring discrepancy, not a proposed parity target (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/appearance-customizer.ts:2928-2936`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/appearance-customizer.ts:2954-3106`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:5361-5370`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:6030-6040`).

Clone names strip a trailing -custom with optional digits, then choose -custom/-custom2/... until available. Imports parse JSON, use its trimmed internal name or a fallback, and show replace/cancel/rename-incoming choices on collision. Built-in replacement is rejected by ThemeDraft. Reset uses the base/dark palette, deletion requires confirm-delete, and errors stay in component state. Preview creation catches errors and calls onThemePreview with an in-memory Theme before rebuilding preview appearance; it does not write settings itself. Structural editor rebuilding and selection changes do not consistently pass through root appearance emit, so root summaries can lag until later refresh.
entries.interfaces: Theme menu actions include mode, fixed selection, automatic light/dark and preview side; token:<name>, var:<name>, varAdd, varRename/varDelete; clone/rename/reset/delete/import/export with explicit collision choice. External preview callback receives a constructed Theme and selected name. File persistence is deferred to TUI-016's apply phases.
entries.dependency_text: SET-017 owns theme setting persistence; SET-033 owns resource discovery. TUI-021 owns editor-to-draft synchronization.
entries.rust: Native /theme and settings theme pickers select only dark/light/monochrome and call ThemePreset application; the settings version persists immediately (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/selectors.rs:449-506`, `rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/settings.rs:390-433`). Native ThemeManager stores a typed Theme without a palette JSON/variable editor (`rust:crates/ice-tui/src/theme.rs:343-386`).
entries.port: Add a native palette editor backed by the JSON and draft contracts. Use one authoritative typed selection and update it on fixed selection, clone/rename/import/delete; ensure preview, validation and persisted selection agree. Test fixed-theme Apply, automatic-to-fixed changes, deleting/renaming selected themes and collision cancellation, rather than relying only on automatic-pair tests.
entries.priority_reason: Theme editing and preview need consistent persisted selection to avoid apparent success that reverts on apply.

entries.title: Customizer profile and bundle UI, scope selection and partial staging
entries.what: Provides named appearance-profile management and portable bundle import/export with metadata and collision review.
entries.mechanism:
Profile Save uses a trimmed name or default-profile, optional description limited to 200 characters, an include-theme flag and either all appearance or selected sections. The UI requires explicit replace permission on an existing name, stages through ProfileDraft, clears the replace flag after success and emits. Rename/duplicate/delete and description edits are staged. The selected-scope loop indexes draft by APPEARANCE_SECTIONS values; dotted thinking.indicator/thinking.label/thinking.block are not root properties, so choosing only those scopes omits their appearance data. Other root sections copy correctly.

Profile Load first calls session.loadProfile, then applies its theme setting, but emit immediately submits the component's unchanged local draft. Consequently the loaded appearance is overwritten by the old local appearance. The existing automatic-profile test asserts only the theme pair, not changed appearance. A fixed profile theme calls setFixedTheme without first switching from automatic to fixed; setFixedTheme is a no-op while automatic. Automatic profiles explicitly switch mode and stage both members (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/appearance-customizer.ts:1821-1845`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/appearance-customizer.ts:1901-1913`).

Bundle export gathers raw JSON for the current fixed theme or both automatic members, deduplicates names, includes every available profile and full current appearance, and writes metadata name/author/description. It uses exportBundle.json or an empty string, so an export error is not surfaced there; obtaining selected theme data may throw. Import parses a bundle, scans existing theme/profile collisions and displays a pending review before staging. Existing built-ins cannot be replaced; each collision defaults to skip, with replace and incoming-rename choices. Confirmation clears pending state before staging.

Staging runs themes, then profiles, then top-level appearance, then top-level theme selection. Earlier staged mutations remain if a later import fails; there is no atomic rollback of the in-memory bundle operation. Theme imports update selected preview, appearance imports update the local and controller draft, and automatic theme settings switch mode explicitly. Fixed settings repeat the missing-mode-change issue, although TUI-012 already documents the importer losing the top-level v2 themeSetting. The review screen emits again after confirmation, and rebuilt collision rows initialize their displayed value to skip even if a different resolution is stored. Canceling the pending review clears it without staging.
entries.interfaces: Profile scope everything/selected, section checkbox set, includeTheme, description and explicit replaceExisting; profile save/load/delete/rename/duplicate actions. Bundle metadata name<=64, author<=64, description<=200 in UI, JSON import/export, collision skip/replace/rename, Stage/Cancel. File-format validation, limits and persistent paths remain TUI-011/012/015.
entries.dependency_text: Scope/UI routing is distinct from the reusable profile/bundle storage contracts.
entries.rust: Native settings/theme selector paths have no profile catalog, scoped appearance preset, bundle serializer/import-review or staged collision controls (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/settings.rs:51-287`, `rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/selectors.rs:449-506`). The explicit crates-wide appearance/profile/bundle behavior search found no matching implementation.
entries.port: Implement typed section paths and synchronize loaded profile appearance back into component state before notifying preview. Make fixed/automatic mode transitions explicit. Stage bundle operations transactionally in memory or report which mutations remain, retain visible collision resolutions, and propagate export errors. Add tests for thinking-only profile scopes, changed appearance on Load, automatic-to-fixed profile load and a failure late in bundle staging.
entries.priority_reason: Profile and bundle controls are the portable customization workflow and contain uncovered data-selection inconsistencies.

entries.title: Appearance preview scenes, real component samples and animation cleanup
entries.source:
Complete preview component: `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/appearance-preview.ts:1-404`; scene test: `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/appearance-customizer.test.ts:420-430`; disposal coverage: `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/appearance-acceptance.test.ts:395-416`.

`PreviewScene` — `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/appearance-preview.ts:34`. `PREVIEW_SCENES` — `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/appearance-preview.ts:36`. `DEFAULT_HIGHLIGHTER_TEST_TEXT` — `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/appearance-preview.ts:46`.
entries.what: Renders representative conversation, Markdown, tool, input, chrome and footer samples inside the customizer without submitting messages or running commands.
entries.mechanism:
Scenes are all, conversation, markdown, tools, input, chrome, footer; all is default. The component clones appearance, owns Loader and Bash preview instances, and disposes them before every rebuild. setAppearance always rebuilds; setScene rebuilds only on change. dispose stops loaders, disposes Bash previews and empties their arrays. Highlighter sample text defaults to TODO fix this  // FIXME later and is capped at 200 UTF-16 units.

With a UI, input uses a real CustomEditor and fresh KeybindingsManager; tool samples use real ToolExecutionComponent instances for fake pending/success/error results, cwd=process.cwd and showImages=false; Bash samples use fake npm test output and never execute a process. The tools-only scene shows all three states, while the all scene limits tool output. Without a UI it renders simplified styled text/manual borders; the manual editor sample has a nominal inner width at least 10 rather than the real editor's geometry.

Conversation samples use real UserMessage/AssistantMessage/CustomMessage components with appearance applied, but thinking is a separate sample. Thinking animation uses mirrored frames and configured interval; per-kind status samples use raw frames, so reverseMirror is not applied there. Status uses a Loader only when a UI exists and more than one frame is present; otherwise first-frame text. Working/thinking uses its own Loader path and first configured verb. Markdown covers headings, inline styles, link, quote/list/rule/table with the appearance MarkdownTheme and table style. Diff is styled added/removed/context text. Chrome and subagent state samples are static.

Preview coverage is intentionally incomplete in current source: the footer is two static lines and does not exercise actual Footer field order, visibility, separators or extension statuses; Markdown samples do not exercise every modeled padding/background/code-block property; assistant thinking sample and status mirroring differ from runtime paths. Thus a convincing preview is not evidence that every appearance field reaches production rendering.
entries.interfaces:
AppearancePreviewComponent(appearance, ui?) with initial scene='all', setAppearance, setScene/getScene, getHighlighterTestText, setHighlighterTestText, invalidate, render, dispose. Preview runtime timers must stop when the customizer closes or a scene is rebuilt.

```ts
export type PreviewScene = "all" | "conversation" | "markdown" | "tools" | "input" | "chrome" | "footer";
```

entries.title: Interactive appearance application, settings preview and message stamping
entries.source: Runtime application and draft lifecycle: `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:5225-5469`; full-screen customizer callbacks: `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:6020-6048`; settings callbacks: `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:6050-6098`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:6159-6203`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:6309-6319`.
entries.what: Connects persisted or previewed appearance to the running editor, messages, status, footer, diff and Markdown defaults, and shares one customization session between /settings and /customize.
entries.mechanism:
effectiveAppearance falls back to built-in defaults before controller construction. applyAppearanceToRuntime installs global chrome override functions for selected text, descriptions, hints, settings labels/values/cursor, editor/chrome borders and scrollbar backgrounds. It updates the default editor's border and horizontal padding plus a decoration callback over current input-highlighter rules, sets diff appearance and the global table style, updates footer and subagent chrome, and updates the active status indicator; working status additionally receives the effective working-indicator override. It walks direct children of both chat and pending-message containers and calls available appearance setters for user/assistant/thinking/tools/Bash/system cards, then requests render. It does not recurse arbitrary nested containers, stamp a new MarkdownTheme on existing components, update showByDefault through setHideThinkingBlock there, or call updateEditorBorderColor in this method.

A lazily created CustomizationDraftSession captures settings theme or dark resolved against terminal light/dark state. /settings theme staging parses fixed/pair syntax and explicitly sets mode and member(s), unlike the fixed-theme customizer path in TUI-021, then previews via themeController. Apply runs session.apply; failure displays an error and retains the draft, success clears the shared session and starts applyFromSettings without awaiting it before applying appearance. Cancel cancels/clears the session or rolls back the appearance controller, likewise starts theme reapplication without awaiting. Direct appearance commits display validation issues on failure. /settings appearance preview shallow-patches only Markdown, inputBox or thinking.indicator; Apply/Cancel share the same draft session. Closing /settings cancels outstanding preview.

New message stamping applies user appearance, or assistant/thinking appearance plus bullet text and effective hidden-thinking state. Explicit hideThinkingBlock=true wins; explicitly set false forces visible; otherwise visibility is inverse of appearance.thinking.block.showByDefault. Existing message appearance application does not itself restamp that visibility. Working-indicator options supplied by extensions/runtime take precedence over appearance frames; default appearance frames are mirrored and colorized with configured interval. Thinking verbs use cycle index or Math.random, with empty list returning literal Thinking... before format substitution. Editor border selection uses Bash mode, then non-off thinking level, then appearance active/idle determined by editor focus; settings model/thinking paths call that updater separately.

/customize opens a 100% top-left overlay. onDraftChange applies appearance; onApply closes only after successful session apply; onCancel rolls back then closes; onThemePreview installs an in-memory theme instance only. These callbacks confirm the fixed-theme selection and profile-load discrepancies in TUI-021/022 rather than repairing them. Ordinary settings such as images, output padding, tool style and symbols have their own immediate update/rebuild callbacks, covered by their UI contracts and SET-017 storage.
entries.interfaces: Internal effectiveAppearance/applyAppearanceToRuntime; preview/commitAppearanceSection; stageSettingsTheme; getOrCreate/apply/cancelCustomizationDraftSession; stampMessageAppearance; effectiveHideThinkingBlock; getEffectiveWorkingIndicator. Runtime setters are optional duck-typed methods on direct container children.
entries.dependency_text: SET-017 owns stored appearance/theme keys and precedence. This entry owns application timing and coverage; terminal/editor primitives and message internals remain separate.
entries.rust: Native settings immediately calls apply_setting_change and save_settings; theme selection applies global/local ThemeManagers and persists (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/settings.rs:120-153`, `rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/settings.rs:390-433`). Native user messages track global theme revision and rebuild their fixed box/Markdown view (`rust:crates/ice-tui/src/user_message.rs:58-119`); native assistant supports hide-thinking label and a transform hook (`rust:crates/ice-tui/src/assistant_message.rs:41-84`, `rust:crates/ice-tui/src/assistant_message.rs:257-283`). There is meaningful live theme/message machinery, but no v2 appearance controller, shared customization preview transaction or full appearance fan-out.
entries.port: Add explicit presentation state and typed update methods to native components, with one shared draft owner for settings/customizer. Define whether existing messages fully reflect every changed field; update visibility, border focus and nested message groups consistently. Await or otherwise sequence theme application with appearance updates, and test both current and newly created messages across Apply/Cancel, streaming/pending Bash, fixed/automatic selection and extension working-indicator overrides.
entries.priority_reason: A stored appearance schema is insufficient unless every affected live component receives coherent updates.

entries.title: Searchable settings menu, exact choices and extension sections
entries.what: Presents built-in and extension settings in a searchable ten-row menu, dispatching concrete values to runtime callbacks while staging the appearance preview controls.
entries.mechanism:
The component builds the complete settings list from a runtime snapshot and terminal capabilities, then delegates search/navigation to SettingsList. Each row has an explicit value conversion and callback; persistence and live UI changes belong to the callback owner, so the menu does not itself write settings.

Extension items are flattened after the first three compaction rows, use `${settings.name}:${item.id}` as their UI identity and retain all original item fields, including submenu. A Map dispatches the selected value back to settings.onChange with the original item.id; duplicate composite identities overwrite the callback map entry while retaining duplicate rows. This layer performs no async awaiting or error isolation around extension callbacks (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/settings-selector.ts:515-546`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/settings-selector.ts:1009-1014`).

Image visibility and width rows are inserted only when getCapabilities().images is truthy. Resize and block controls remain available even without rendering support. Skill commands, hardware cursor, editor/output padding, autocomplete, clear-on-shrink and terminal progress are inserted afterward; fast mode is independently gated by fastModeAvailable. Other controls remain present even when their available submenu list is empty. DynamicBorder surrounds a SettingsList with maxVisible10 and enableSearch:true. The follow-up explanation uses the current configured key display rather than a hard-coded shortcut.

The exact menu contracts are:

| autocompact | true, false | onAutoCompactChange | boolean |
| compaction-threshold | 10%,20%,30%,40%,50%,60%,70%,75%,80%,85%,90%,95% | onCompactionThresholdPercentChange | parseInt |
| mid-run-compaction | off, pause, resume | onMidRunCompactionChange | enum cast |
| steering-mode | one-at-a-time, all | onSteeringModeChange | enum cast |
| follow-up-mode | one-at-a-time, all | onFollowUpModeChange | enum cast |
| transport | sse, websocket, websocket-cached, auto | onTransportChange | enum cast |
| http-idle-timeout | HTTP_IDLE_TIMEOUT_CHOICES labels | onHttpIdleTimeoutMsChange | exact label lookup; unknown ignored |
| hide-thinking | true, false | onHideThinkingBlockChange | boolean |
| table-style | unicode, ascii, clean, clean-top-bottom, raw | onTableStylePreview | staged preview |
| input-border-style | single, double, round, bold, none | onInputBorderStylePreview | staged preview |
| thinking-interval | 40,80,120,200,500 | onThinkingIntervalPreview | parseInt; staged preview |
| appearance-apply | apply | onAppearanceApply | commit staged preview |
| appearance-cancel | cancel | onAppearanceCancel | discard staged preview |
| cache-miss-notices | true, false | onShowCacheMissNoticesChange | boolean |
| collapse-changelog | true, false | onCollapseChangelogChange | boolean |
| quiet-startup | true, false | onQuietStartupChange | boolean |

| default-project-trust | Ask, Always trust, Never trust | onDefaultProjectTrustChange | labels map to ask/always/never; unknown ignored |

| terminal-progress | true, false | onShowTerminalProgressChange | boolean |

All true/false handlers compare the string to true. Numeric menu values use parseInt without a second validation layer. table-style/input-border-style/thinking-interval call the Preview callbacks, not their declared Change counterparts; the separate Apply/Cancel rows operate on the shared appearance session (TUI-024). WarningSettingsSubmenu clones the incoming object, exposes only anthropic-extra-usage, defaults absent to true, preserves other warning fields and emits a new object on each toggle. The outer menu holds updated warnings for later submenu openings (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/settings-selector.ts:154-194`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/settings-selector.ts:669-681`).

Source tests assert scrollbar cycling auto→always→hidden→auto, compaction 85%→90%, opening Appearance, and SettingsManager defaults/fallbacks for compact footer, compact tools and auto symbols. They do not exercise every row or prove successful persistence. Runtime callback wiring and appearance transaction semantics are separately documented in TUI-024.
entries.interfaces: SettingsConfig and SettingsCallbacks are the exported contracts at settings-selector.ts56–149; getSettingsList() exposes the focus/input target. Config carries booleans, numeric thresholds/padding, enum strings, availableThinkingLevels/availableThemes, terminalTheme, warnings and optional RegisteredSettings[]. Callbacks include all table-listed actions plus optional onThemePreview and declared onTableStyleChange/onInputBorderStyleChange/onThinkingIntervalChange, which this menu's preview rows do not invoke. No SettingsManager is stored in this component.
entries.dependency_text: Settings storage/normalization is coordinator-owned SET; EXT-016 defines named settings registration. Generic SettingsList keyboard/rendering is covered by the terminal fragment.
entries.rust: Native open_settings_selector creates a searchable SettingsList and saves callback changes immediately; its concrete catalog includes theme/default model/default thinking/scoped models plus hide-thinking, images, cache notices, quiet startup, changelog, progress, copy-on-select, double Escape, editor padding, autocomplete and HTTP idle timeout (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/settings.rs:51-300`). apply_setting_change updates thinking/images/cache live, stores copy-on-select, and persists several other options for next launch; idle choices map disabled/30s/1m/other→300000 (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/settings.rs:301-383`). The independently read native menu lacks most TS rows, the extension-injected sections and shared staged appearance controls. Native copy-on-select is an additional setting to retain. Native submenus replace the selector and return to the editor rather than rebuilding the original settings menu.
entries.port: Add the explicit missing menu rows and typed conversions on top of native SettingsList, using the existing settings/session APIs as owners. Implement extension sections through EXT-016 and route appearance preview/apply/cancel through a shared draft. Keep per-setting immediate versus next-launch behavior explicit, refresh controls after relevant changes, and preserve native copy-on-select. Use source-level contract cases for every choice and capability gate rather than relying on generic row rendering alone.
entries.priority_reason: The primary user-facing settings menu exposes materially fewer controls in Rust and lacks extension/appearance integration.

entries.title: Theme, thinking and image choice submenus with preview rollback
entries.what: Allows fixed or automatic light/dark theme selection with previews and cancellation, and supplies reusable bordered thinking/image choice components.
entries.mechanism:
ThemeSubmenu retains the original setting, edits fixed or automatic choices locally, previews cursor movement, and returns a selected setting only on Apply. Nested cancellation restores the current staged theme pair, while cancelling the top theme menu restores the original setting, keeping preview and persistence distinct.

SelectSubmenu renders accent title, optional description, spacer, a SelectList limited to min(options.length,10), and an Enter/Escape hint; its primary column range is 12–32. It preselects an exact current value before installing callbacks. The Automatic sentinel is `/` and appears before named themes. preferredTheme chooses an available preferred name, then fallback, then the first available item or fallback even if the list is empty. A valid existing light/dark setting initializes automatic mode. Converting a fixed theme to automatic initially uses that same available theme for both halves; malformed slash-containing settings fall back through dark (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/settings-selector.ts:196-337`).

Choosing Automatic sets automatic mode, previews light/dark and opens two theme rows plus Apply and Change mode. Light/dark nested selectors preview the hovered single name; selecting updates only that half and previews the combined pair. Cancelling a nested selector previews the current combined setting and calls done without a value. Change mode chooses the active half (light only when terminalTheme is exactly light; dark for dark/unknown), previews it and returns to the fixed list. Fixed selection applies immediately to the parent done callback; automatic Apply sends `${lightTheme}/${darkTheme}`. Top-level Escape previews originalThemeSetting and calls done without a selected value. ThemeSubmenu itself never writes files or invokes onThemeChange; SettingsList routes the selected result back to the parent row callback (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/settings-selector.ts:349-500`).

ThinkingSelectorComponent maps the caller-supplied levels in order, includes descriptions off/no reasoning; minimal~1k; low~2k; medium~8k; high~16k; xhigh~32k; max/maximum; ultra/model-specific, uses all levels as maxVisible, preselects exact current and reports the selected string as ThinkingLevel. It performs no model capability calculation. ShowImagesSelectorComponent exposes yes/no, preselects from the current boolean, uses maxVisible5 and converts selected yes to true. Both expose getSelectList and surround it with DynamicBorder. DynamicBorder renders a colored `─` repeated max(1, width), has no cache and accepts an explicit color callback for extension module-cache contexts. It does not participate in the symbol preset table.
entries.interfaces: ThemeSubmenu(currentThemeSetting, terminalTheme, availableThemes, callbacks, onDone(selectedValue?)); internal selected state is mode/singleTheme/lightTheme/darkTheme with originalThemeSetting retained. ThinkingSelectorComponent(currentLevel, availableLevels, onSelect, onCancel) and ShowImagesSelectorComponent(currentValue, onSelect, onCancel) are exported reusable components; these standalone wrappers are separate from the settings menu's internal submenus. DynamicBorder(color?) implements render(width) and invalidate().
entries.dependency_text: Theme loading and automatic terminal detection are TUI-003/007. The settings menu owns final callback dispatch; generic list behavior belongs to the terminal fragment. Thinking runtime changes are SESSION-036.
entries.rust: Native theme settings show only the three fixed presets and commit immediately (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/settings.rs:385-450`); no paired automatic chooser or hover preview rollback appears there. Native thinking selectors derive model capabilities, use a five-level fallback when the model is absent (despite the 'all levels' comment), and show seven named enum cases through max without ultra. Their descriptive budgets differ from TS. The code creates maxVisible10 without setting the current selection, despite comments promising preselection; the callback spawns lane.set_thinking_level, ignores its result, immediately updates footer and closes (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/selectors.rs:746-876`). The settings variant additionally persists defaultThinkingLevel and also does not preselect (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/settings.rs:1770-1852`). Native images Yes/No mark the current choice in descriptions but do not preselect it, update state without settings persistence and close (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/selectors.rs:978-1034`). These existing choices are partial counterparts, not missing selectors.
entries.port: Add the fixed/automatic preview state machine and explicit cancellation rollback to native theme selection, using TUI-007 for detection. Align thinking/image current selection, descriptions and supported levels while preserving native capability filtering. Keep standalone reusable components separate from caller persistence. Surface async lane failures before reporting successful application; preserve this as a recommended improvement over the observed native fire-and-forget callback.
entries.priority_reason: Theme preview/automatic pairing and accurate current-choice selection are missing from existing native selectors.

entries.title: User message formatting, width budgets and OSC 133 zones
entries.what: Renders the user's original prompt as styled Markdown with appearance-controlled format, padding, borders and optional compact width, and marks the resulting rows as a terminal prompt zone.
entries.mechanism:
The component retains original text separately from formatted display text, builds a background Box around Markdown and applies appearance styling without mutating the prompt. Rendering recomputes the width budget and rebuilds the box, then adds optional borders and OSC133 markers to the emitted rows.

Constructor defaults are Markdown theme from the global theme, outputPad1, no transformers and no appearance. getText returns the original text; setOutputPad/setAppearance rebuild immediately. With appearance, every `{message}` occurrence in format is replaced through split/join, the shared resolver supplies exact foreground/background/border colors and configured text styles, and appearance padding overrides outputPad. Without appearance, background is userMessageBg, foreground userMessageText and vertical padding 0. Markdown is configured with preserveOrderedListMarkers:true and preserveBackslashEscapes:true, plus the user/false transformer context (TUI-028). Box padding is clamped nonnegative at construction (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/user-message.ts:31-102`).

render floors the requested width and clamps it to at least 1. Side borders reserve 2 columns except none/top-bottom styles. Horizontal padding is limited to max(0, floor((safeWidth-sideWidth)/2)); vertical padding is used unchanged. The full-width branch renders the Box at safeWidth, clips/pads rows, wraps each row with side borders when present and finally clips/pads every returned row back to safeWidth. It therefore fits the final rows, but the Box is initially rendered at outer width rather than the reduced side-border content width; adding side borders clips the rendered rows instead of reflowing text at that smaller width. This source behavior is distinct from the comment claiming content is budgeted before borders (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/user-message.ts:104-145`).

fitToContent chooses min(maxWidth, longest visible source line+2*paddingX+sideWidth), using formatted raw source rather than rendered Markdown row widths. It renders at that outer target, slices side-border content to max(1, outerTarget-sideWidth), adds top/bottom and returns without the full-width branch's final clamp. For a one-column target with side borders, the helper still supplies two side glyphs and contentTarget remains 1; this branch has an untested narrow-width overflow risk. The existing width 1/2/3/10/30/80 matrix uses the default fitToContent:false; the fit-to-content test uses width 80. No runtime tests were executed (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/user-message.ts:122-135`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/appearance/user-message-presentation.ts:145-161`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/appearance-user-message-layout.test.ts:20-100`).

fitLineToWidth pads with spaces or slices by visible columns while preserving ANSI; zero requested width is allowed in this helper. fitTargetWidth measures each unwrapped source line. Exported fitLinesToContent measures already-rendered lines, clamps target to maxWidth-sideWidth and pads/truncates each, but the component's render path uses fitTargetWidth instead. The border helper supports none/single/double/round/bold/classic/single-double/double-single/top-bottom-single/top-bottom-double/top-bottom-bold; its mixed styles fall through to default horizontal/vertical glyphs, with the supplied mixed-style corner table, unlike the assistant helper's explicit mixed glyphs.

markOsc133Zone mutates the rows array. Empty rows remain empty; a single row begins A+B+C in order; multiple rows begin with A on the first and B+C on the last, never suffixing the line. Exact bytes are ESC]133;A BEL, ESC]133;B BEL and ESC]133;C BEL. User-message tests assert one-row compact output, marker order, background reset at line end and transformer context/invalidation; appearance tests cover format/style/color/width, not preservation of all text through side-border clipping.
entries.dependency_text: Uses shared Box/Markdown and ANSI-aware width/slicing. Main interactive stamping and later appearance updates are TUI-024.
entries.rust: Native UserMessageComponent already wraps Markdown in a theme.surface background and OSC133, defaults horizontal padding 1, permits with_pad, and rebuilds its cached Box only on invalidation/padding/theme revision (`rust:crates/ice-tui/src/user_message.rs:25-115`). Its vertical padding is always 1, unlike TS default 0; the comment claiming output_pad controls both is inaccurate. It has no user appearance format/styles/borders/fit-to-content or user transformer hook. Marker insertion would produce B+C before A for a single returned row, but the fixed vertical padding normally makes standard messages multi-row; scope that as the helper path, not an observed current one-row regression. Native inline tests check nonempty output, marker presence and CJK no-panic, without marker-order or exact layout assertions (`rust:crates/ice-tui/src/user_message.rs:122-154`). The native cache optimization is an existing capability to retain; its comment that TS builds only once does not describe the frozen TS render method.
entries.port: Add typed user appearance and original/display text separation to native UserMessageComponent, preserving its cache and rebuilding only when text/theme/appearance/width requires it. Budget the actual inner width before Markdown layout and explicitly decide whether to fix the TS clipping and narrow fit branch while retaining intended appearance behavior. Implement shared OSC133 order handling for one and multiple rows, exact per-role colors and width-aware user transformer context. Test content preservation as well as line width.
entries.priority_reason: Core prompt presentation differs in default spacing and lacks the appearance/transformer contract.

entries.title: Assistant content ordering, reasoning visibility, bullets and display transforms
entries.what: Renders assistant text and consecutive reasoning blocks in order, controls hidden reasoning labels and stop notices, and adds optional bullets, appearance borders and context-aware Markdown transforms.
entries.mechanism:
updateContent retains the last message and streaming flag, rebuilds text/thinking children in content order, and appends stop notices according to whether tool calls are present. Rendering then wraps that content in optional assistant appearance geometry and marks non-tool messages with OSC133 zones.

A leading Spacer 1 is added only if some text or thinking content is non-whitespace. Text blocks are trimmed and rendered as Markdown; adjacent thinking blocks are individually trimmed, empty blocks skipped and the remaining run joined with two newlines. A thinking run gets one following spacer only if another visible text/thinking block occurs later, so a separate tool-call block does not force extra space. Hidden reasoning emits one static label per nonempty run; appearance.hiddenLabel overrides constructor hiddenThinkingLabel, and a blank label suppresses the run entirely. Visible reasoning uses thinking appearance foreground/styles or default thinkingText plus italic. The final all-Spacer container is cleared (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/assistant-message.ts:164-263`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/assistant-message.ts:290-293`).

A length stop always adds `Response was truncated before completion.`, including messages containing tool calls. Without tool calls, aborted uses a supplied errorMessage unless it is exactly `Request was aborted`, otherwise `Operation aborted`; error uses `Error: ` plus errorMessage or `Unknown error`. Partial content remains before those notices. Other content kinds are not rendered by this component. hasToolCalls suppresses all OSC133 markers; otherwise shared A/B/C zone order applies (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/assistant-message.ts:160-161`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/assistant-message.ts:265-288`).

setHideThinkingBlock/setHiddenThinkingLabel/setThinkingAppearance/setOutputPad rebuild the retained message; setBulletText does so only on a value change. setAssistantAppearance clones its input but geometry is applied during render rather than rebuilding content. Default padding 0/border none/background terminal-default is a fast path with no extra wrapper. Otherwise inner width=max(1, width-borderColumns-2*paddingX), body is clipped there and padded onto the chosen background, paddingY adds rows, and exact single/double/round/bold/classic/mixed/top-bottom borders are drawn. Unlike the user helper, assistant mixed styles use ╓╖╙╜ with horizontal─/vertical║ and ╒╕╘╛ with horizontal═/vertical│. There is no final width clamp or padding clamp against very narrow render widths, so the source does not establish a universal width invariant. Read border tests exercise ordinary widths, not that boundary (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/assistant-message.ts:91-162`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/assistant-message.ts:315-343`).

BulletBlock renders its child at max(1, width-2), prefixes the first row with current theme.text(sym(bullet)) plus one space and prefixes continuations with two spaces. It uses a fixed two-column budget rather than measuring the glyph. Text Markdown has padding 0 in bullet mode; thinking retains outputPad. A width below 3 can therefore still produce a three-column row. The interactive host enables bullets through TUI-024; the standalone component default is false.

createMarkdownTransform closes over messageType/isStreaming and passes each render-time availableWidth to the chain. Transformers run in registration order; a string result replaces current Markdown, non-string results are ignored, and a thrown error preserves current text and continues. User is user/false, assistant text assistant/current-streaming, and reasoning assistant-thinking/current-streaming. Transforms alter display source only, not the original message. entries.title: Default custom-message cards, completion summaries and renderer precedence
entries.source: `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/custom-message.ts:1-239`; `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/custom-entry.ts:1-63`; tests `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/custom-message.test.ts:1-114`. Extension registration/renderer contracts are EXT-037/038.
entries.what: Provides the default system-card shell for displayed custom messages, specialized compact shell/subagent completion summaries, and a spacing/error facade around persistent entry renderers.
entries.mechanism:
A custom renderer gets first opportunity to produce the message component; the default card is used only when it returns no component or throws. Specialized completion rows and appearance controls apply to the host's fallback presentation, leaving successful custom renderer output responsible for its own styling.

Every CustomMessageComponent starts with Spacer 1. Renderer calls receive message, {expanded, outputPad} and live theme; rebuild removes the previous component and default box, and a truthy renderer result is installed directly. Exceptions are swallowed into fallback. Merely supplying a renderer also disables getToggleId, even if that renderer later fails, so bash completions then use the generic fallback card. Existing replaced components are removed but no disposer is invoked in this class (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/custom-message.ts:63-109`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/custom-message.ts:142-178`).

For bash_background_completed without a renderer, toggle identity is `bash-completed:<taskId-or-empty>:<timestamp>`. The status label uses description ?? command ?? taskId ?? 'command'; stoppedByUser takes precedence over isError, and statuses are `was stopped`, `failed` or `completed`. An exit code suffix is included for failed/completed when exitCode is not undefined; optional duration is formatted by the existing shell runtime formatter. Symbols/colors are muted separator for stopped, error/error for failure and success/toolSuccess otherwise. Collapsed content is one clickable toggle line; expanded adds plain dim message text with padding 2. It bypasses card background, border and label appearance. Output content uses only text blocks joined with newline, or the original string (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/custom-message.ts:20-45`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/custom-message.ts:169-178`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/custom-message.ts:223-228`).

Generic fallback is initially Box(1,1, customMessageBg), a bold [customType] label, Spacer 1 and Markdown colored customMessageText. SystemCardAppearance overrides box padding/background, label/body presentation and an outer chrome border, excluding the initial spacer. When appearance is removed after a previous appearance-built box, rebuild only recreates the box if the new appearance is non-null; therefore the previous structural padding/background can remain even though label/body revert. outputPad is passed to custom renderers but does not replace default box padding.

Only subagent_completed belongs to COLLAPSIBLE_CUSTOM_TYPES. Collapsed source with more than 8 lines shows first 4 and last 3, inserting `... N more lines (<current expand key> to expand)` where N=sourceLineCount-7; at 8 or fewer it shows all. The budget is source lines, not rendered/wrapped rows. Expanded shows all Markdown. Tests assert a 20-line body hides 13, preserves head/tail, and expands, plus exact shell completion output/absence of card background and renderer outputPad updates (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/custom-message.ts:181-236`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/custom-message.test.ts:11-112`).

CustomEntryComponent is the TUI facade for EXT-038: renderer(entry,{expanded}, theme) controls content; undefined produces no rows, while a thrown error produces a Box 1/1 with `[customType] renderer failed: <message>`. Only a present component gets Spacer 1; hasContent reports that presence. Expansion/invalidation clears and re-renders. This entry does not change hidden-by-default entry selection or extension registration rules.
entries.interfaces: CustomMessageComponent(message, customRenderer?, markdownTheme?, outputPad=1, cardAppearance=null): getToggleId(), setExpanded(), setOutputPad(), setCardAppearance(), invalidate(), render(width). Bash details: optional taskId, command, description, isError, exitCode, durationMs, stoppedByUser. CustomEntryComponent(entry, renderer): hasContent(), setExpanded(), invalidate(). tool-toggle link encoding is reviewed with tool rows.

entries.title: Branch, compaction and skill summary cards
entries.what: Shows branch summaries, compaction records and parsed skill invocations as collapsible custom-background cards with the current expand-key hint.
entries.mechanism:
Each wrapper uses Box(1,1, customMessageBg), starts collapsed and rebuilds its contents on expansion or invalidation. The wrappers display already-produced session/skill data; they do not perform summarization, skill loading or session mutation.

Branch cards always show a bold customMessageLabel [branch] and Spacer 1. Expanded body is Markdown `**Branch Summary**` followed by the supplied summary; collapsed body is `Branch summary (<current app.tools.expand key> to expand)` in customMessageText/dim. Compaction cards similarly show [compaction], with expanded header `**Compacted from <tokenStr> tokens**` and summary, or the collapsed `Compacted from <tokenStr> tokens (...)` label. The connector redacted the tokenStr assignment at source line 35, so its exact formatting expression was not read and is explicitly unverified; no alternative route was used to recover it. All other lines of that file were visible.

SkillInvocationMessageComponent renders only ParsedSkillBlock, leaving the user's accompanying message to its caller. Collapsed output is one `[skill] <name> (<expand key> to expand)` Text. Expanded output is [skill], then Markdown of `**<name>**\n\n<content>` with customMessageText base color; unlike branch/compaction it adds no separate spacer before this Markdown. None of these three wrappers invokes display Markdown transformers or SystemCardAppearance in the read implementation; each captures a MarkdownTheme argument, defaults it at construction and uses current global colors for rebuilt text.
entries.interfaces: BranchSummaryMessageComponent(message, markdownTheme?), CompactionSummaryMessageComponent(message, markdownTheme?), SkillInvocationMessageComponent(parsedSkillBlock, markdownTheme?): each exposes setExpanded(boolean) and invalidate(). Required display data are summary, compaction token label source, and skill name/content respectively. Session compaction/tree mechanisms and parseSkillBlock remain session-owned.

It is a mode of a tool execution rather than a reusable ParsedSkillBlock wrapper, and the hard-coded hint does not track rebinding. Full tool-mode identification/caller behavior is reviewed with tool rendering, so no broader missing-skill claim is made here.

Share a reusable skill card for parsed invocation data and update hints from the keybinding registry. entries.title: Tool renderer composition, execution context, images and live result binding
entries.what: Combines built-in and extension call/result renderers, retains per-call rendering state across streamed arguments/results, and displays supported images without losing live completion bindings after transcript rebuilds.
entries.mechanism:
The component resolves the built-in tool definition for its cwd, then independently prefers the registered definition's renderCall, renderResult and renderShell properties. It retains argument, result, execution, expansion and image state and projects them into either a default boxed shell, a renderer-owned shell or the compact presentation described in TUI-032.

Options default showImages=true, imageWidthCells=60, compact=false and no toolsAppearance. Unknown tools have no built-in definition and use the default shell unless an extension requests self. The default tree has a leading Spacer 1 and Box 1/1 with pending background; call and result Component references are retained separately for renderer reuse. A shared mutable state object survives both renderers. Context includes args, toolCallId, invalidate, lastComponent, state, cwd, executionStarted, argsComplete, isPartial, expanded, showImages and isError; invalidate clears component/render caches and requests a UI render. isPartial initially true. markExecutionStarted and setArgsComplete update display, while argument/result setters retain new values and clear display caches. updateResult defaults isPartial=false and replaces the result rather than appending text (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/tool-execution.ts:40-238`).

Renderer exceptions fall back to generic call/result rendering. A result renderer receives content and details, with error state in context. The fallback call prints the tool name and JSON arguments; fallback results join textual blocks. Call and result renderer selection is independent, so a custom call renderer can retain built-in results and vice versa. Self shell omits generic box framing and can render no rows when its content is empty; it still uses the component's image children. Appearance affects state background/title/output styling but does not automatically impose all appearance-model geometry on an extension-owned component. Extension registration and transport remain EXT-owned.

Images are extracted from the latest result only when terminal image capability and showImages are true and both data/MIME exist. Each image gets maxWidthCells; the setter floors and clamps its value to at least 1. Kitty skips non-PNG images until asynchronous convertToPng completes; converted entries are cached by image ordinal, followed by updateDisplay and requestRender. The ordinal cache is neither cleared when a different result arrives nor guarded by a result generation, and there is no in-flight deduplication in this component. Thus the source permits a prior or late conversion at the same ordinal to be reused for a later result. This is a TS state-lifetime limitation, not a contract to reproduce. Default/self shells include images when supported; compact rows include them only when expanded. Component rendering caches settled output by width, while partial output is recomputed, and setters/invalidate clear that cache (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/tool-execution.ts:243-285`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/tool-execution.ts:462-631`).

Interactive message_update creates missing tool components by ID and updates arguments on existing ones. Successful assistant message_end marks pending arguments complete; aborted/error completion turns all pending calls into error results and clears the map. tool_execution_start creates a missing component and marks execution started; updates replace partial result with isError=false; end applies the final error flag and removes the ID. Transcript reconstruction builds a temporary map, consumes matching historical results, and re-registers only unresolved calls into live pendingTools. The regression asserts that a subsequent live completion still updates a reconstructed call, and that completed history does not remain pending (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:4230-4343`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:4771-4816`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/suite/regressions/4167-thinking-toggle-pending-tool-render.test.ts:162-198`).

Tool component tests exercise partial arguments, renderer reuse/context, exception fallback, self shells, expansion, built-in resource/skill/doc read renderers and line-range labels. These source assertions were read, not executed. Actual read-tool resource recognition belongs to TOOLS; this entry owns composing those renderers into the transcript.
entries.dependency_text: EXT owns tool registration and renderer host transport; SESSION-023 owns runtime registry/control integration. TUI image encoding/terminal placement is terminal-owned. TOOLS owns built-in tool-specific call/result definitions.
entries.rust: Native ToolExecutionComponent already retains args/result, Pending/Running/Completed/Failed status, elapsed timing, expansion, display titles, skill mode, diff rows and optional Markdown results. Running invalidates on each render; settled output is cached against width, component revision and theme revision. ToolPanel clamps horizontal padding to preserve a content column and clips/pads rows to the target width (`rust:crates/ice-tui/src/tool_execution.rs:24-265`, `rust:crates/ice-tui/src/tool_execution.rs:361-626`, `rust:crates/ice-tui/src/tool_panel.rs:1-42`). Native results are stored as strings and this component has no equivalent independent extension call/result Component callbacks, persistent renderer context/state or image-result projection. It additionally supplies structured plan and todo displays, which should be retained. Native host extension renderer routing is separately credited in EXT; its existence is not evidence that this component implements the TS context contract. Inline tests through 1682 cover wrapping, narrow widths, state presentation, caching, plan/todo and skill modes (`rust:crates/ice-tui/src/tool_execution.rs:1180-1682`).

Preserve native timers, plan/todo projections, theme-aware caching and safe ToolPanel geometry. Introduce generation-aware image conversion/cache ownership; maintain unresolved-ID bindings across rebuilds and explicit args-complete/start/partial/end phases.

entries.title: Compact tool rows, result precedence and bounded summaries
entries.what: Presents compact tool cells with state markers, operation-specific headers, bounded collapsed output and explicit expansion hints.
entries.mechanism:
Compact rendering separates a title from indented result rows and chooses preview content by a strict state/tool precedence. Completed rows are cached by width until component state changes; pending rows are recomputed, so streaming titles and partial output remain live.

Collapsed content width is capped at 100 columns; expanded content uses the supplied width. A leading blank row is optional, title budget is max(1, width-2), and body budget max(1, width-4). The first body row uses two spaces plus the theme gutter and a space; continuation rows use four spaces. Body rows are clipped with a dim ellipsis, not wrapped by this layer. The first nonblank row and applicable more hints can carry the internal toggle URL (TUI-034). Fixed prefixes and max 1 content budgets mean this layer does not establish a universal width invariant for widths below its indentation.

Edit with a string path uses Edit/Edit failed/Edited according to partial/error/success and includes added/removed counts when details.diff is a string. Diff counts count every leading '+'/'-' line. Bash with a nonblank command uses Running only when partial and executionStarted, otherwise Ran, including a call whose execution has not started. Collapsed command displays its first logical line plus an ellipsis when multiline; expanded displays the complete command wrapped by the header renderer. Other titles use renderCall output and fall back to toolName if it renders no lines. Path/title accents use global theme colors where coded, even when toolsAppearance supplies other text styles (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/tool-execution.ts:287-391`).

Collapsed-result precedence is: no result → no rows; partial → last 3 normalized textual lines and a hidden-prefix hint; error → first 5 error-styled lines plus more; successful edit with diff → rendered diff trimmed of blank ANSI rows and capped 14; any own backgroundTaskId property in details → one summary line; a non-Bash result component → its rendered preview, capped 14 for edit/write and 5 otherwise; no textual lines → summarizer; other text → first 3 dim lines plus more. Text joins text blocks, removes carriage returns and trims the end before splitting. An empty trailing-only output is distinct from missing result. The background preview branch tests property presence, whereas summarizeToolResult requires backgroundTaskId to be a string, so malformed metadata can fall through to a normal line-count summary. Expanded successful edits show the entire rendered diff without this height cap. Expanded non-edit calls use the full result renderer or styled raw text; edit errors or edits without a successful diff still take the collapsed body path even while expanded (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/tool-execution.ts:392-460`).

summarizeToolResult first recognizes a string backgroundTaskId and reports started vs moved to background according to origin. Next an edit diff produces literal added/removed counts; otherwise it returns textual line count, 'image' for empty text with an image block, or 'no output'. It does not execute or classify tool safety. Read description accepts nonblank path, appends offset and offset+limit-1 or 1-limit when values are numbers, and imposes no finite/positive validation here; tool input validation belongs to TOOLS. grep/find and ls descriptions use their corresponding pattern/path fields. Tests assert pending/completed/error snapshots, partial tail behavior, diff counts, long commands, width 100 capping, edit expansion and current theme colors (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/tool-summary.ts:96-146`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/compact-tool-rows.test.ts:1-228`).
entries.dependency_text: TUI-033 owns grouping and display-only shell classification; TUI-034 owns links/expansion application state. Tool execution/truncation correctness remains TOOLS-owned.
entries.rust: Native ToolExecutionComponent has a different unified panel: a wrapped header with status marker, display name, argument summary, elapsed time and chevron; expanded args are a flattened k=v summary. Text results show first 12 wrapped visual rows collapsed and all rows expanded. Diff rows are additionally capped 6 collapsed and 40 expanded, with fixed Ctrl+O hints. It does not implement the TS100-column compact layout, exact partial/error/edit/background/result-renderer precedence or per-tool 3/5/14 limits (`rust:crates/ice-tui/src/tool_execution.rs:361-536`). Its hand-written argument display parser has builtin path/pattern/command formatting and incomplete-JSON fallbacks, which are presentation-only rather than execution validation (`rust:crates/ice-tui/src/tool_execution.rs:769-1177`). Native todo/plan/skill views remain useful separate capabilities; inline tests assert safe narrow widths and content preservation. Native completed output should not be labeled missing merely because its layout differs.
entries.port: Add compact row mode alongside the native panel, using typed args/results and the existing theme symbols. Make preview precedence explicit and independently test partial, failed, edit, background and renderer-owned results. Preserve native safe width budgets and unlimited expanded textual output; decide deliberately whether to retain the TS edit-error and expanded 40-row native limitations.
