entries.title: Exploration grouping and display-only shell summaries
entries.what: Groups adjacent read/search/list calls into one expandable exploration cell, while leaving execution and permission policy unchanged.
entries.mechanism:
createToolComponent groups a call only when tool style is compact, describeExploration returns a description, and the component does not render its own shell. It scans the existing transcript backward to find a trailing open group, skipping spacers and components whose render(80) has no nonblank visible text; a visible item or a group containing an error ends the run.

The group owns the actual member components, so they retain live updates. Its toggle ID is the first member ID. Adding a member suppresses its leading spacer, assigns that shared toggle ID, applies the group's expansion flag and invalidates the group cache. isOpen means no member is in error; pending and successful members remain eligible. Expanded mode renders the members with the shared group identity. Collapsed mode starts with a blank row, caps content width 100, displays Exploring while any member is pending and Explored otherwise, and gives the marker error precedence. Up to 6 descriptions are displayed; longer runs show the first 5 and one '+N more' row. Failed members additionally render their own error rows below the descriptions, indented 2. The hidden-count hint itself is not clipped to a very narrow width. Settled groups cache by width; partial groups recompute. Direct changes to an already settled member do not themselves notify a parent cache, so callers must invalidate or change group state for such a nonstandard update. Normal live completion occurs while the group is pending and is not evidence of that stale-cache condition (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/tool-group.ts:14-114`).

The lexical Bash classifier rejects commands containing '>', a backtick, '$(' or '<(', splits on &&, ||, semicolon, pipe or newline, then whitespace-splits each part. Empty parts and cd are skipped. cat/head/tail/wc/nl/file/stat count as read; sed requires an exact -n word and no word beginning -i; git status/log/diff/show/blame count as read. rg/grep/egrep/fgrep/ag/find/fd count as search unless a word is exactly -exec or -delete. ls/tree/pwd count as list; any unknown command makes the whole command shell. Search takes precedence over read, then list; only cd yields shell. It does not parse quoting or enforce safety, and '<' redirection is not rejected except '<('. Classification affects grouping/labels only and must never be reused for authorization (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/tool-summary.ts:12-69`).

describeExploration maps read→Read with path/range, grep/find→Search with pattern/path, ls→List with path or'.', and classified Bash→the corresponding label with the first trimmed command line. Unknown tools or ordinary shell commands are ungrouped. Tests cover read/search/list grouping, errors closing the group while remaining visible, expanded member output, width 100 truncation, settled cache reuse and runs longer than 6 (`ice:packages/coding-agent/test/compact-tool-rows.test.ts:230-339`).
entries.dependency_text: Grouping consumes live component state and uses internal expansion links. TOOLS owns actual read/search/list/Bash behavior and policy.
entries.rust: The fully read native tool component supports individual panels, plan/todo and skill projections, but no exploration aggregate. A behavior search for Exploring/Explored, describeExploration, ToolGroup, ice-action and tool toggle identifiers across crates/ice-tui and crates/ice-cli found Bash/visual-truncate counterparts but no grouping/classifier implementation; the native tool component's complete 1682-line body was independently checked. Native CLI has global panel expansion instead (`rust:crates/ice-tui/src/tool_execution.rs:269-536`, `rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui.rs:2282-2298`). This missing claim is scoped to the grouped exploration presentation, not the underlying tools.
entries.port: Introduce a transcript group component that retains member identity/state, exact run boundaries and error visibility. Keep the lexical classifier private to presentation. Use explicit child-revision propagation and width-safe hidden hints instead of inheriting the TS settled-cache and narrow-width limitations.
entries.priority_reason: Grouping improves long tool-heavy transcripts but does not block execution or individual result access.

entries.title: Application action links and incremental tool expansion
entries.what: Routes fullscreen transcript action links and expands tool output in newest-first batches, with per-cell overrides and shared group identity.
entries.mechanism:
The interactive composition root enables tool-toggle links only for fullscreen mode and supplies the fullscreen renderer an internal-action predicate plus URL callback. That callback first offers the URL to the application; a false result delegates to openBrowser. The main-screen renderer does not enable these click routes.

A process-global flag starts false. linkIceAction wraps text in OSC8 only when enabled; tool URLs are 'ice-action:toggle-tool/' plus encodeURIComponent(id). linkToolToggle copies the rendered row array and wraps only its first nonblank ANSI-stripped row, preserving the original array when disabled or empty. parseToolToggleUrl requires the exact prefix and catches malformed percent decoding; an empty suffix decodes to an empty ID. isIceActionUrl recognizes the broader 'ice-action:' prefix. More hints use current keybinding text, adding 'click or' only when links are enabled. Changing the global flag does not itself invalidate component caches (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/tool-toggle-link.ts:1-64`).

A ToolCell is a ToolExecutionComponent, ToolGroupComponent or a CustomMessageComponent with a toggle ID; other expandable cards are handled separately. The group ID is its first member, standalone tools use toolCallId and eligible custom completions use their custom toggle ID. toolExpandFrom is undefined for all collapsed, 'all' for all expanded, or a cell ID marking the first expanded tail cell. A missing anchor resolves to index 0. Per-ID overrides take precedence over the tail rule. Each normal expand action moves the anchor backward 3 cells, newest first; after reaching index 0, the next action collapses everything. No cells still selects 'all' and emits the all-expanded status. A separate newest action toggles only the newest cell and reports 'No tool output yet' when absent. Explicit all-expanded/collapsed uses the same anchor mechanism. Changing the anchor clears overrides; when its overall boolean changes it also updates the active header and non-tool expandable children in loaded resources/chat. Applying cell expansion requests a render (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:5578-5654`).

handleUiAction recognizes exact bottom, shells, agents and prompt URLs; bottom scrolls to end, shells opens the shell view, agents opens the hub, and prompt scrolls to the sticky prompt target when available. A valid tool URL with an unknown ID is consumed without browser fallback. A known ID toggles its override and reapplies expansion. Unknown or malformed actions return false and therefore reach the URL opener configured at composition. The application does not implement an additional unknown-internal-URL rejection. Primitive hit testing, selection and hyperlink activation are TUI-224; this entry owns destination routing and state mutation (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:5656-5687`). Tests assert no links by default, title and more links for a standalone cell, and shared group links before/after expansion.

entries.title: User Bash streaming display, visual tail and completion presentation
entries.what: Shows user-invoked Bash progress and bounded visible output, including deferred placement, cancellation/exit notices and full-output references.
entries.mechanism:
The TS component creates a leading spacer, dim-or-Bash-colored dynamic borders, a command header and an animated Running loader with the current cancel-key hint. It accumulates incoming output deltas, then projects a context-limited tail into a 20-visual-row collapsed preview or an expanded view.

appendOutput strips ANSI, normalizes CRLF and CR to LF, joins the first segment onto the previous last line and appends the remaining segments. The raw line array is not memory-capped here. updateDisplay calls the shared truncateTail with DEFAULT_MAX_LINES/DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES before presentation; expanded output therefore still excludes content removed by that context limit. Collapsed mode first keeps the last 20 logical lines and then uses visual truncation at render width with a leading newline. Its hidden count is based on logical lines before the 20-line slice, not all visual rows omitted by wrapping. Text rendering is cached per width until invalidate/rebuild. getOutput returns accumulated normalized output, not the displayed truncation (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/bash-execution.ts:95-163`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/bash-execution.ts:204-273`).

setComplete saves exitCode/cancelled/truncation/fullOutputPath, stops the loader and rebuilds. Cancelled takes status precedence; a defined nonzero exit code is error, while absent/null/zero is complete. Collapsed hidden output shows an expand hint; expanded shows collapse only when the logical hidden count was nonzero. Cancellation and nonzero-exit notices are separate lines. A full-output warning is emitted only when returned or local context truncation is true and a fullOutputPath is truthy. dispose stops the loader. The constructor uses dim command/borders when excluded from context, but updateDisplay uses Bash color for the header in the default appearance path, so exclusion's dim header is not retained after an update. Borders retain their initial color. Appearance replaces the border wrapper with applyChromeBorder and custom background/text/paddingX; the source does not automatically apply every stored appearance property (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/bash-execution.ts:32-94`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/bash-execution.ts:164-239`).

truncateToVisualLines renders Text(text, paddingX,0) at the requested width and takes the last maxLines rendered rows. Empty text returns zero rows; maxLines=0 is not specially handled in TS, so slice(-0) returns all rows while skipped reports the full length. Width and maxLines validation are not part of this helper. Native Text actually wraps, so the old native visual_truncate comment describing logical-line-only truncation is stale, not the runtime behavior (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/visual-truncate.ts:1-51`, `rust:crates/ice-tui/src/text.rs:78-94`).

The UI first emits the extension user_bash hook and reports hook failures without host-execution fallback. A hook's complete result is displayed and recorded directly. Otherwise it creates the panel, places it in pendingMessages when the session is streaming or chat when idle, feeds executeBash deltas through appendOutput, and applies completion metadata. Execution failure completes the panel with undefined exit and separately shows an error. The component reference is cleared afterward. Historical Bash messages restore saved output/exit/cancel/truncation/path; this branch does not apply global expansion before insertion (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:4625-4644`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:8128-8229`). Hook/session execution mechanics are EXT and TOOLS/SESSION-owned.
entries.dependency_text: TOOLS owns actual Bash process/capture/truncation semantics; EXT owns user_bash dispatch. TUI-205 supplies wrapping Text and the terminal worker owns Loader. This entry owns display accumulation/projection and the UI callback protocol.
entries.rust:
Native BashExecutionComponent already shows wrapped commands, state backgrounds, safe ToolPanel padding, elapsed duration, cancel/error and full-output notices,20-row visual tails and expanded output. append_output intentionally replaces a complete snapshot; the native primary caller passes get_progress().output snapshots, so the difference from TS delta accumulation is consistent, not a corruption bug (`rust:crates/ice-tui/src/bash_execution.rs:23-416`, `rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui.rs:559-630`). It normalizes tabs to 4 spaces, has no independent context cap, uses a static running marker plus elapsed time, and preserves excluded command color. Expanded mode passes hidden=0, so its conditional collapse hint is not emitted; a truncation flag prints a full-output notice even without a nonempty path. Native visual_truncate explicitly returns empty for max_lines=0 and otherwise renders wrapping Text before slicing (`rust:crates/ice-tui/src/visual_truncate.rs:1-108`). All native Bash inline tests were read through 710.

A separate native transcript finalizer synthesizes exit_code as 1/0 from is_error, forces cancelled=false and reads details.full_output_path plus details.truncation.truncated, so that event path does not preserve arbitrary exit codes/cancelled metadata even though the direct user-Bash caller does (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/transcript_view.rs:952-978`). This is scoped to that caller; process semantics are not inferred from UI flags.
entries.port: Preserve the native snapshot protocol and elapsed/width-safe rendering. Add the desired TS loader/key hints, appearance projection and context-limited preview semantics with clearly named delta vs snapshot methods. Carry real exit/cancel/path metadata through the generic transcript finalizer, and make expanded collapse hints and zero-line behavior explicit.
entries.priority_reason: Bash display exists, but metadata loss in one native caller and differing preview/appearance contracts affect result interpretation.

entries.title: Diff row parsing, word emphasis and appearance-sensitive tinting
entries.what: Formats numbered edit diffs with theme or custom appearance, single-line replacement word emphasis and width-sensitive background rows.
entries.mechanism:
renderDiff parses numbered changed/context rows and coalesces consecutive removals followed by additions. Exactly one removed and one added row receive a word-level comparison; larger hunks retain whole-row coloring. The result is newline-joined text whose height is controlled by the caller.

The TS parser requires a leading '+', '-' or whitespace, optional whitespace/digits, then one whitespace separator and the remaining content. Unparsed rows stay context text. Tabs become 3 spaces only in parsed content. Line-number text is retained, then rendered before the sign. diffWords marks changed chunks; leading whitespace is excluded from emphasis only for the first removed/added chunk. The normal theme path uses added/removed/context foregrounds and, for changed rows, a background chosen by theme.getDiffBgAnsi. Stronger word background is used only when both row/word tints exist, otherwise inverse video emphasizes changed words. A customized appearance is detected by JSON.stringify inequality against the default model, so property order can affect that decision; custom text presentation disables automatic row tinting (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/diff.ts:13-98`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/diff.ts:117-207`).

Only tinted changed rows apply width clipping with ellipsis, right padding to width and a background reset. Custom-styled rows and untinted/context rows do not apply that width bound in this helper; the compact tool caller clips the returned rows separately. The optional filePath argument is accepted but unused, so it does not supply syntax highlighting. setDiffAppearance clones its argument into module-global state and reset(undefined) restores defaults. No height cap exists in renderDiff itself; TUI-032 applies 14 collapsed rows and all rows for an expanded successful edit.
entries.dependency_text: TOOLS owns edit diff production and atomic file changes; this entry owns display parsing and tint/word styling. Terminal TUI-203 provides clipping/style continuation primitives.
entries.rust: Native render_diff already parses changed/context rows, uses TextDiff::from_unicode_words for a single replacement pair, highlights changed words by inverse video and clips positive-width rows. Its layout places sign before a right-aligned line-number gutter and '│'; TS places the retained number before the sign. Native accepts only '+','-' or literal-space leading signs, does not require the TS separator after digits, and width 0 returns content unchanged. It has no appearance override or adaptive changed-row/word background. Tabs become 3 spaces. Its changed-word loop strips leading whitespace from every changed chunk but re-adds it only for the first chunk, so later changed chunks can lose their leading whitespace; this is a bounded source-level formatting limitation. Native inline tests verify inverse emphasis, context foreground and clipping but do not cover that later-chunk case (`rust:crates/ice-tui/src/diff.rs:1-311`, `rust:crates/ice-tui/src/diff.rs:313-358`). Native tool panels then impose their own 6/40 diff-row caps, separately from this renderer (`rust:crates/ice-tui/src/tool_execution.rs:465-505`).
entries.port: Align the numbered-row grammar and row order where compatibility is desired, add shared diff appearance and theme-derived row/word tinting, and preserve whitespace across all word chunks. Keep explicit clipping at both renderer and consumer boundaries so appearance changes cannot produce unbounded rows.
entries.priority_reason: Native diff rendering is usable, but appearance, grammar, layout and a whitespace edge case differ.

entries.title: Footer Git metadata, asynchronous refresh and extension status data
entries.what: Supplies branch/worktree metadata, throttled ahead/behind/dirty counts and extension status values to footer consumers, with watcher retries and explicit disposal.
entries.mechanism:
FooterDataProvider discovers Git metadata from its cwd and caches branch/status values separately. Branch changes are watched and debounced, while working-tree counts refresh only when requested by a footer consumer.

findGitPaths walks upward for .git. A directory uses .git/HEAD; a file beginning exactly 'gitdir: ' resolves its remainder relative to that directory, then resolves an optional commondir relative to the Git directory. Missing HEAD or a filesystem exception returns null immediately. An unrecognized .git file allows the walk to continue. The returned repoDir is the worktree/root used for Git subprocesses, commonGitDir locates shared reftable files, and headPath locates this worktree's HEAD. A regular 'ref: refs/heads/' HEAD preserves the full branch suffix. '.invalid' asks git --no-optional-locks symbolic-ref --quiet --short HEAD, synchronously on first getGitBranch and asynchronously during refresh; failure maps to 'detached'. Other readable HEAD contents also map to 'detached'; missing/read errors map to null. The symbolic-ref subprocess helpers do not set a timeout here (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/footer-data-provider.ts:16-81`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/footer-data-provider.ts:303-331`).

The branch watcher watches HEAD's parent directory to survive atomic replacement and reacts to missing filenames or exactly HEAD. On Linux with WSL_DISTRO_NAME/WSL_INTEROP and a /mnt/<drive> repo it additionally watchFiles HEAD every 1000 ms, comparing mtime/ctime/size. If a shared reftable directory exists, it watches that directory and, when tables.list exists, watches that file plus 250 ms metadata polling. Events schedule one 500 ms refresh; an event during an in-flight refresh marks a pending rerun. Callback notification occurs only when a previously known cached branch changes. Initial refresh can fill an undefined cache without notification. Watch errors close all watchers and schedule a 5000 ms retry; watch construction errors use the same error callback. Cleanup cancels normal/retry timers and unregisters polling. Filesystem close errors are ignored (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/footer-data-provider.ts:265-445`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/fs-watch.ts:1-31`).

getGitStatus returns the last cached result while starting a background git --no-optional-locks status --porcelain=v2 --branch, at most once per 2000 ms and only one in flight. It uses timeout 2000 ms and maxBuffer8MiB. Parser defaults ahead/behind/dirty to 0, recognizes '# branch.ab +N -N', and counts lines beginning 1/2/u/? plus a space; ignored paths do not count. Failure retains prior counts. Successful results are discarded after disposal or when repoDir differs from the captured request; a changed JSON result notifies the same branch listeners. There is no timer polling working-tree status in the background without calls (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/footer-data-provider.ts:83-118`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/footer-data-provider.ts:164-194`).

setCwd is a no-op for the same string; otherwise it cancels debounce/watchers, clears branch/status caches and status timestamp, rediscovers metadata, reinstalls watches and notifies listeners. It does not cancel subprocesses or attach a generation guard to the asynchronous '.invalid' branch resolution, so an old branch request can settle after a cwd change and overwrite the new cache. That is a source limitation; status requests have the repoDir check described above. dispose prevents asynchronous cache updates, closes watchers/timers and clears listeners. Listener callbacks are invoked synchronously without per-listener exception isolation.

Extension statuses are a live Map keyed by string; undefined deletes, an empty string remains, clear removes all. Setters do not notify listeners themselves; the UI setExtensionStatus caller requests a render. Available provider count is a stored number with no validation. ReadonlyFooterDataProvider exposes getGitBranch/getExtensionStatuses/getAvailableProviderCount/onBranchChange plus optional getGitStatus, excluding mutations/dispose. Tests cover regular nested repos, '.invalid' plain/worktree reftable lookup, detached fallback, debounce, unchanged-branch silence, retry after async watcher error and preserving counts on status failure; they were read only.
entries.dependency_text: EXT owns the public extension footer-data and setStatus bridge. SET owns general resource watcher use; this entry owns footer-specific Git discovery and refresh.
entries.rust: Native footer has a git_branch field and a working primary CLI startup watcher. find_git_head_path/git_branch_for walk parents for a literal .git/HEAD and watch that path through the native fs watcher; they do not resolve .git files/commondir/reftable. git_branch_for takes only the final slash-separated ref segment and uses the first 7 characters of any other nonempty HEAD. Thus feature/name becomes name and reftable '.invalid' is displayed literally. Native scoped behavior search found no porcelain-v2 status provider or ahead/behind/dirty consumer; the native footer's complete body confirms those fields are absent (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/sessions.rs:628-667`, `rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui.rs:1119-1134`, `rust:crates/ice-cli/src/fs_watch.rs:1-162`, `rust:crates/ice-tui/src/footer.rs:91-127`). Native extension status is synchronized through a separate registry revision into the footer and excludes pet/voice presentation where appropriate, so extension statuses are already implemented at host level (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/state.rs:1032-1053`).
entries.port: Retain native watcher lifecycle and extension registry synchronization, then add worktree/common-dir discovery, full branch names, reftable fallback and an on-demand status cache with bounded subprocess execution. Guard all asynchronous resolutions with a cwd generation and keep failed status refreshes from erasing useful counts.
entries.priority_reason: Current native branch display is wrong for common slash names and worktree/reftable repositories, and working-tree counts are absent.

entries.title: Legacy and customized footer usage, cost and context projection
entries.what: Displays cumulative usage/cost alongside current context and model information, with legacy and configurable field layouts.
entries.mechanism:
FooterComponent receives a session and read-only data provider and computes its projection fresh on every render; invalidate and dispose are compatibility no-ops because the provider owns caching/watchers. setSession/setDataProvider replace dependencies, and setAppearance clones the supplied model.

formatTokens returns raw counts below 1000, one-decimal k below 10000, rounded k below 1 million, one-decimal M below 10 million and rounded M thereafter. formatCwdForFooter resolves cwd/home and uses path-relative containment, so a sibling merely sharing the home prefix is not abbreviated. It returns '~' for home itself and '~'+platform separator+relative path for descendants. sanitizeStatusText replaces CR/LF/tab with spaces, collapses literal spaces and trims; despite its broad comment it does not remove every other control sequence (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/footer.ts:25-70`).

Legacy rendering aggregates all session entries on each render, including persisted subagent_usage, assistant usage, tool-result usage and branch/compaction usage. The latest assistant determines cache hit rate as cacheRead/(input+cacheRead+cacheWrite); subagent totals add cost/tokens but do not alter the session's current context estimate. Usage fields appear only for truthy counts; cache-hit percentage appears when cumulative read/write cache use exists and latest rate is known. Cost is fixed 3 decimals and also shown at zero for OAuth-backed providers or kimi-coding, with '(sub)'. A child-cost hint is inserted beside total cost before the subscription marker only when estimated width also leaves room for the model. Current context uses session.getContextUsage separately, falls back to model contextWindow, marks explicit percent:null as '?', and otherwise defaults missing percent to 0.0. Thresholds strictly above 70 and 90 use warning/error, and auto compaction appends '(auto)'. Experimental mode adds xp (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/footer.ts:305-406`).

The first legacy row is cwd, optional branch in parentheses and optional session name; it is width-truncated. The second puts usage/context left and model plus reasoning level right, with at least 2 spaces. A provider prefix is attempted only when availableProviderCount>1 and dropped first if it does not fit. Left stats are clipped before the right side gets its remaining budget; if no room remains, the model disappears. Extension status values sorted by localeCompare(key) form an optional third row. A combined subagent/notices badge may replace the right side of row 1 via placeRight; if the badge plus 2 exceeds width it is omitted rather than overflowing.

Appearance differs from the default only when JSON.stringify differs. A color-only override retains compact layout when compact style is selected; changes in order, visible or separator force customized multirow layout. Customized primary fields are cwd/branch/session; secondary fields are usage/cache/cost/context/provider/model/thinking; extension values have their own row. Within each group appearance.order and visible select fields, then trailing fields are popped until one or more fit and the final string is clipped. The groups remain separate even if the order interleaves their IDs. Context always uses strict numeric-percent detection ('?' otherwise), with threshold colors overriding appearance colors; other fields use primary/secondary text presentation. Experimental xp joins usage. Extension styling is independent, and the subagent/notices overlay still applies after layout (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/footer.ts:482-591`).

Read tests cover wide names/model/provider text, all-entry cost totals, subagent cost without context inflation, hint omission at narrow widths, subscription marker placement, cache-hit rate, safety colors and badge clipping. They do not turn the comments about native unknown context into an implementation guarantee.
entries.interfaces: FooterComponent(session, footerData); setSession, setDataProvider, setAutoCompactEnabled, setAppearance, setStyle, setNoticeSource, setCapabilitySource, setBackgroundTaskSource, setWatchSource, setSubagentSource, render. FooterStyle='compact'|'legacy'; default legacy. formatTokens and formatCwdForFooter are exported.
entries.dependency_text: SESSION owns context/usage semantics and SUB owns subagent_usage record production. AUTH owns OAuth classification. This entry owns which data is displayed, precision, field order and width handling.
entries.rust: Native FooterComponent already renders cwd/branch/session, cumulative usage, cache-hit rate, cost, context thresholds and auto marker, model/thinking and separate run/extension statuses. Values are pushed by callers rather than derived from a session inside the component; native cost appears only when positive and lacks subscription/child-cost annotations. Its home-relative helper is lexical and does not resolve paths. Native extension status shares the stats row instead of a separate sorted row, with registry joining handled by its host (`rust:crates/ice-tui/src/footer.rs:29-289`, `rust:crates/ice-tui/src/footer.rs:301-503`). Critically, comments say unknown context renders '?', but stats_line renders 0.0% when percent is None and window>0; inline tests explicitly expect 0.0% initially and after set_context_tokens(None). This is an observed source/test agreement against the comment, and differs from TS explicit-null unknown context (`rust:crates/ice-tui/src/footer.rs:356-364`, `rust:crates/ice-tui/src/footer.rs:620-641`). Native lacks customized footer field order/visibility/text presentation in the complete 663-line source.
entries.port: Add the shared footer appearance model and exact cumulative/child/subscription projection without replacing existing native usage and model updates. Represent unknown context distinctly from measured zero, decide a consistent absent/null policy, and preserve display width under wide Unicode field values.
entries.priority_reason: Native usage display works but unknown context currently communicates a measured zero, and customization/subscription/child-cost details are missing.

entries.title: Compact footer priorities, runtime badges and status-line allocation
entries.what: Fits execution mode, cwd/Git, model/context and actionable runtime badges into one prioritized status row, with required information retained across narrow layouts.
entries.mechanism:
Compact footer builds left/right StatusSegment arrays, assigns priorities and delegates width allocation to layoutStatusLine. Color-only footer appearance overrides preserve this compact route; structural field customization selects TUI-038's multirow layout instead.

Left segments are execution mode 'ice-mode' plus elevated capabilities at required priority 100, cwd priority 60 with middle shrink/min 16, branch priority 65 with shrink/min 12 plus unchanged counts, session name 30 and other extension statuses 20. Capabilities use error color and abbreviate external→ext; other status keys are sorted, sanitized and blank values removed. Git ahead uses success, behind/dirty warning and zero counts disappear. Branch shrinking cuts its label while retaining the count suffix. Right segments are model/thinking 70, context 90, active shells 95, subagent segment variable priority and notices 100. Context appears only for a positive window, rounds a numeric percent to an integer and otherwise shows '?', and uses strict >70/>90 warning/error thresholds (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/footer.ts:177-265`).

The shell segment appears only when background count>0, pluralizes shells and optional watches, and links to OPEN_SHELLS_URL. The subagent segment exists whenever an overview exists: 'agents running/max' or 'agents off', then nonzero queued count and the count of children whose state is idle. Pending approvals append a warning label. Activity uses primary color, idle uses secondary. Priority is 100 with approvals,96 with running/queued activity and 65 otherwise; the segment links to OPEN_AGENTS_URL. Notices count warning+error, ignore informational/update counts, and use error color when any error exists. These are display callbacks, not lifecycle or policy implementations (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/footer.ts:247-303`).

layoutStatusLine copies segments and uses a 2-column gap. While overflow remains it chooses the lowest-priority eligible segment, scanning left then right with stable ties. A shrink callback is attempted once toward the minimum width needed, clamped to minWidth(default 1), and then removed even if it failed to shorten. Before dropping a previously shortened target it tries another available shrink candidate. Segments at priority>=100 are never dropped, though they may shrink. Nonrequired targets are removed until the row fits or only required content remains. A fitting row fills intervening spaces to width; if required content still overflows, left and right are clipped separately onto two rows, right-aligned on its row, and blank rows removed. No segment mutation leaks back to the caller. A callback that returns an oversized minimum can still be dropped or clipped by the final path (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/status-line.ts:13-84`).

The middleTruncate helper used for cwd budgets visible cells but slices JS UTF-16 code units, so a wide-character path can exceed the requested cell budget or split a surrogate pair; this is documented in TUI-040 and should be corrected rather than copied. Tests cover count preservation beside long paths, normal 120-column badge combinations, widths 40/60/80, color-only customization, required approvals and disabled agents. They do not establish correctness for every Unicode shrink callback.
entries.interfaces: StatusSegment{text, priority, shrink?(maxWidth), minWidth?}; REQUIRED_PRIORITY=100; layoutStatusLine(left, right, width):string[]. Footer's callback sources read current counts on each render; OPEN_SHELLS_URL/OPEN_AGENTS_URL feed TUI-034.
entries.dependency_text: SUB owns capacity/approvals data and TOOLS owns background shell/watch registries. Later notices entry owns warning aggregation. This entry owns their compact display and allocation priorities.
entries.rust: Native footer's complete source implements the legacy-like two-row projection and fixed left/right truncation, without priority segments, compact layout, runtime shell/subagent/notices badges or shrink callbacks (`rust:crates/ice-tui/src/footer.rs:301-503`). Native tool/child/status capabilities are credited elsewhere; this missing claim concerns their integrated compact footer projection only. Generic terminal layout exists but does not implement this application-specific priority contract.
entries.port: Add a provider-free status-segment allocator and wire exact badge callbacks from existing native runtime data. Preserve required approvals/capabilities across narrow widths, maintain link identity through clipping and use grapheme/cell-safe middle truncation.
entries.priority_reason: The compact status view is absent even though several underlying native runtime facts already exist.

entries.title: Responsive session header and live startup resource summary
entries.what: Shows a responsive mascot/header beside current model, mode, capabilities, cwd and resource counts, with optional expanded startup help.
entries.mechanism:
SessionHeaderComponent obtains fresh SessionHeaderData on every render and chooses a fixed ASCII or block mascot according to the symbol preset. It lays the text block beside the mascot only when at least 24 columns remain after the art width and 2-column gap, centering shorter text vertically against the art.

The block art rows are '█▄  ▄▄▄  ▄█', '▀██▀███▀██▀', ' ██▄▀█▀▄██', '  ▀█████▀', '   █▄▀▄█'; ASCII rows are ' (o>', '//\\\\', 'V_/_'. The title uppercases appName and adds dim v<version>. Model and optional thinking appear first; mode and capabilities are appended only when mode is truthy, with capabilities in error color when the whole row fits. If the session row is too wide it truncates the plain combined string and styles it uniformly muted, losing individual capability color. Location includes cwd plus loaded summary when both fit; otherwise it drops the entire loaded summary and middle-truncates cwd. Optional startupStatus adds a fourth text row. Hint is always appended; expanded nonempty help adds a blank row and each help line prefixed by one space and clipped (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/session-header.ts:27-135`).

middleTruncate first measures visible width, computes remaining budget after the current ellipsis, and splits the retained count into floor-head/ceil-tail. It then uses String.slice with those counts instead of cell/grapheme slicing. This makes its implied width guarantee unsafe for wide/combining/surrogate text, and no final clip is applied to the resulting location row. Tiny budgets<=ellipsis+1 use ordinary truncation instead.

The host builds the header with verbose||toolOutputExpanded, or an empty Text when startup is silenced. Resource initialization/rebinding occurs before initial messages; loaded context count includes explicit system source, base template, append sources and AGENTS files. Other counts include loaded skills, promptTemplates, nonhidden extensions and themes with sourcePath. Zero counts disappear and pluralization is count-sensitive. Model/thinking come from current session state, cwd is home-relative, mode is the ice-mode extension status, elevated capabilities are derived from known safety-notice IDs, and startup:* status values join in insertion order. Dynamic data is not cached in the header. Global expansion can update it through TUI-034 (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:1125-1193`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:1473-1475`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:1595-1653`).

entries.title: Live working, retry and compaction indicators with countdown disposal
entries.what: Displays working facts and operation-specific status labels, updates retry countdowns, and disposes replaced timers while preserving compaction visibility.
entries.mechanism:
StatusIndicator extends the terminal Loader, carries kind working/retry/compaction/branchSummary and disposes by stopping it. Working uses render-time detail callbacks; retry owns an additional countdown, while compaction and branch summary supply distinct reason-specific messages.

WorkingStatusIndicator keeps a mutable appearance holder so constructor-captured color functions observe later appearance updates without recreating its Loader timer. Spinner color uses indicator.color with label styles; label uses label presentation. setAppearance changes colors only in this subclass, not the frame cadence; frames are supplied separately by the host's effective working indicator. With details and at least 2 Loader rows, it appends elapsed time, positive output-token count (optional '~'), reasoning level except off, and a current app.interrupt hint unless interruptible=false. It clips the resulting second row and optional gutter detail to width. formatElapsed clamps negative milliseconds to 0, floors seconds, uses seconds below 60, unpadded m/s below 1 hour and h plus two-digit minutes thereafter. Without details the Loader output is unchanged (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/status-indicator.ts:40-130`).

Retry's initial seconds are ceil(delayMs/1000). CountdownTimer immediately invokes onTick with that value, then every 1000 ms decrements, ticks, requests a render, and at <=0 disposes and invokes onExpire. Even zero/negative initial durations wait for the first interval before expiry. It counts intervals rather than measuring a deadline, so delayed callbacks extend elapsed wall time. dispose clears the interval idempotently; Retry dispose clears both countdown and Loader. Retry text includes attempt/max and cancel-key hint. Retry/Compaction/BranchSummary setAppearance updates colors plus frame/interval options. Manual compaction says Compacting context; threshold says Auto-compacting; overflow prepends Context overflow detected. IdleStatus returns two space-filled rows at width (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/status-indicator.ts:132-258`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/countdown-timer.ts:1-40`).

The host replaces a status by cancelling any compaction hold, disposing the prior indicator and mounting the new one. Kind-filtered clear leaves a different indicator untouched; otherwise it disposes and clears, adding IdleStatus only after a prior indicator in regular mode with clearOnShrink. Successful compaction remains visible for at least 1000 ms from its shown timestamp, changing its label to Context compacted, then hands off to working only if still the same indicator and streaming/visible. The timeout has an identity check and is cancelled by replacement/clear. setWorkingVisible(false) clears only working; true while streaming can replace another current kind. Extension options are applied to an active working Loader directly (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:2873-2937`).

Preparing prompts skip registered extension slash commands, echo only plain parent-view prompts, and display an uninterruptible Preparing indicator showing the active extension path/event or Sending prompt. End preparation removes the echo and only clears its own still-active indicator. Working details add finalized output usage to ceil(current text+thinking+serialized tool-args JS length/4), explicitly flag the estimate, select the last pending tool's first title row at width 200, and prioritize blocking child wait over tool detail over a rotating six-tip list (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:1524-1578`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:5462-5515`).

Compaction/retry events install and restore Escape handlers, set terminal progress, manage summary/error rows and hide transient retry-attempt errors. Summarization retries show retry then restore compaction/branch status per event source. SESSION owns the actual cancellation/retry state machine; this entry owns indicator mounting, feedback and timer lifetime. Tests assert elapsed formatting, detail rows, width 30 clipping, frame updates and that dispose stops further render requests.
entries.interfaces:
WorkingDetails{startedAt, outputTokens, outputTokensEstimated, thinking?, detail?, interruptible?}; StatusIndicator kind/dispose/setAppearance; WorkingStatusIndicator setDetails; RetryStatusIndicator(attempt, maxAttempts, delayMs); CompactionStatusReason manual|threshold|overflow. CountdownTimer(timeoutMs, tui|undefined, onTick, onExpire), dispose.

Exported supporting type (verbatim):
```ts
export type StatusIndicatorKind = "working" | "retry" | "compaction" | "branchSummary";
```
Source: `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/status-indicator.ts:11-11`.
entries.dependency_text: Terminal Loader cadence/cancellation primitives are terminal-owned; SESSION-015–018 owns compaction/retry semantics and EXT owns working-indicator overrides. TUI owns their presentation and disposal.
entries.rust: Native StatusIndicator supports all four kinds, fixed themed spinner, elapsed time and a deadline-based retry countdown; it advances the spinner per render and emits one row rather than Loader's two-row shape. The fixed prefix is not clipped when width is smaller than it. It uses a literal Ctrl+C hint, lacks configurable appearance/frames and WorkingDetails, and its separate CountdownTimer has no callback/dispose thread to leak (`rust:crates/ice-tui/src/status_indicator.rs:23-265`, `rust:crates/ice-tui/src/countdown_timer.rs:15-48`). Primary native working and compaction feedback is actually an editor WorkingState, gated by show_terminal_progress, rather than calls to the library working/compaction constructors. Native retry mounts StatusIndicator in the status container and is driven by the host render loop; remote TUI retry has its own retained slot. These working paths are credited, while TS detail/tip/estimate/hold contracts are absent (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/state.rs:987-1029`, `rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/state.rs:1210-1239`, `rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui.rs:1254-1282`, `rust:crates/ice-cli/src/tui_shell.rs:361-407`).
entries.port: Keep native deadline countdown and existing editor/status integration, then add typed working facts, configurable indicator appearance, real keybinding hints and explicit replacement lifetime. Separate terminal progress output from visibility policy where intended, and preserve successful compaction long enough to be seen without allowing stale timers to replace newer status.
entries.priority_reason: Native progress exists but lacks detailed live facts, configurable presentation and the exact operation handoff/visibility behavior.

entries.title: Bordered extension loader cancellation facade
entries.what: Wraps a loader in themed borders and exposes cancellation, input and disposal through a reusable extension-facing component.
entries.mechanism:
BorderedLoader chooses CancellableLoader by default or a plain Loader when cancellable=false, then builds top border, loader, optional spacer/cancel hint, final spacer and bottom border. It captures the supplied Theme in border/spinner/message closures.

The cancellable variant forwards signal, onAbort assignment and handleInput to its loader. The noncancellable variant creates a separate AbortController, returns its signal and ignores onAbort/input; this wrapper never aborts that controller. The fallback signal getter can create a fresh signal if the stored controller is absent, although normal construction supplies it. The cancel hint remains in the component tree regardless of loader running state. dispose calls the inner dispose when present, otherwise stop. It does not itself remove the wrapper from a parent or add a disposal-time abort policy (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/bordered-loader.ts:12-67`).
entries.interfaces: BorderedLoader(tui, theme, message,{cancellable?:boolean}); readonly signal:AbortSignal; onAbort setter; handleInput(data);dispose. Default cancellable=true.
entries.dependency_text: Terminal CancellableLoader/Loader owns its signal, key matching and frame behavior. EXT owns UI host transport; this entry owns this exported border/cancellation adapter.
entries.rust: Native BorderedLoader already wraps Arc<Loader> or Arc<CancellableLoader>, uses dynamic borders and an optional cancel hint. Its hint appears only while the cancellable loader is running; the wrapper has no input, signal/callback or dispose forwarding, and explicitly leaves lifetime with the caller. It supports a border-color override and invalidates the inner component. This is a partial facade, not a missing visual component (`rust:crates/ice-tui/src/bordered_loader.rs:19-111`). Inline tests 119–139 verify border rendering and a running cancel hint.
entries.port: Attach an explicit cancellation/input/disposal adapter to the native wrapper while retaining caller ownership options. Clarify whether cancel hints disappear after completion and whether disposal aborts outstanding work, rather than relying on the TS noncancellable signal's never-fired controller.
entries.priority_reason: The visual wrapper is present but its public lifecycle/cancellation facade is incomplete.

entries.title: Live model picker, favorites, scoped view and selection persistence
entries.what: Shows cached available models immediately, refreshes them with bounded cancellation, supports favorites and a scoped view, and applies the selected model to the current session.
entries.mechanism:
The component builds its border/title/search/list/details/hints synchronously from getAvailableSnapshot, requests a render, then begins a 15,000 ms refresh. It starts in scoped mode only when scopedModels is nonempty. Refreshed scoped entries are rebound through runtime.getModel(provider, id) when possible and retain their previous Model when unavailable. All-model ordering first prioritizes the current provider/id pair, then provider.localeCompare; a stable favorites-first pass subsequently places every favorite ahead of every nonfavorite, even the current model. Scoped ordering begins with configured order, with favorites affecting presentation only. Favorites are exact provider/id strings loaded into a Set (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/model-selector.ts:1-211`).

Search uses getModelSelectorSearchText: provider, provider/id, provider, id and optional name, with provider deliberately first for fuzzy scoring. The generic getModelSearchText used by the scoped editor starts with id instead. Nonempty filtering resets the selected index to zero; empty filtering clamps its prior index. Favorites-first sorting is applied after fuzzyFilter, so favorites can outrank a stronger fuzzy match. Toggle-favorite writes SettingsManager immediately, reapplies the filter and restores the selected model by identity. Toggling the scoped/all view is available only when scoped entries exist; changing favorites does not reorder the actual runtime scope. Up/down wrap, the favorite action is handled before Tab/view switching, and confirm/cancel are checked before passing data to Input (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/model-search.ts:1-22`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/model-selector.ts:212-406`).

The list renders at most ten rows centered around the selected index, using Text rather than single-line truncation. It marks current and favorite models, displays a scroll counter when needed and exposes the selected display name below. A catalog error replaces model details. Refresh shows muted progress, warning on timeout/abort or provider errors, and a success message otherwise. One provider error names that provider; multiple errors list provider keys. A closed selector ignores refresh completions; dispose is idempotent, clears the timer and aborts the controller. Filtering is reapplied after the refreshed snapshot, preserving the user's query but resetting a nonempty-query selection to its first result (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/model-selector.ts:103-340`).

Confirmation disposes the selector, persists defaultProvider/defaultModel, then invokes onSelect. The component does not await that callback. Its interactive caller awaits session.setModel, refreshes autocomplete/footer/border state, closes the selector, reports the selected model and invokes provider warnings/easter-egg checks. Failure closes the selector and reports the error; the already persisted default is not rolled back. This write-before-live-apply behavior is the observed TS contract, not an atomic operation (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/model-selector.ts:346-406`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:6472-6503`).

Read-only tests cover favorite ordering/toggling and selection retention, name/provider search, catalog errors and resetting filtered selection in both all/scoped modes. They were inspected, not executed. AUTH owns model resolution, refresh implementation and cycling; this entry owns picker state and its live-selection caller.
entries.dependency_text: Uses generic input/fuzzy/keybinding primitives and theme adapters. AUTH-024 owns scoped model matching and cycling; Settings owns persisted favorites/default fields. Session model transitions are SESSION-036.
entries.rust: The native live picker is present: model_selector_items deduplicates by API, lowercase provider and lowercase ID, emits provider-qualified values with display name fallback and provider-prefixed search text, and marks current by bare ID case-insensitively (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/settings.rs:530-575`). The live selector uses a snapshot, SearchableSelectList and ten-row SelectList; it does not explicitly preselect current, expose favorites/scoped mode, or run this owned refresh. It persists defaults only when the inferred current provider differs or is unknown, updates TuiState immediately, spawns lane.set_model while discarding its Result, reports success and closes before acknowledgement (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/selectors.rs:121-214`). `/model` uses the cached catalog for direct matching before opening the picker (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/commands.rs:117-174`). Native tests expressly cover qualified values, deduplication, provider/name search and ambiguous/package IDs (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/tests.rs:1816-1921`, `rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/tests.rs:2468-2497`). Native catalog refresh elsewhere remains credited to AUTH; this is a caller-specific gap.
entries.port: Extend the existing native picker with identity-preserving cached/refresh state, favorites, scoped presentation and owned cancellation. Make live-apply failure and persistent-default sequencing explicit; matching TS write-before-apply is separate from a proposed transactional improvement. Preserve native qualified-ID/ambiguity handling and test the same-provider persistence difference.
entries.priority_reason: Model choice is a core interactive path; omitted refresh and differing acknowledgement/persistence can make visible state or future defaults diverge from the actual lane.

entries.title: Scoped-model editor, unavailable entries and session-only versus saved order
entries.what: Edits the ordered model scope used for cycling, preserves unavailable configured entries, and distinguishes immediate session changes from an explicit save.
entries.mechanism:
EnabledIds is null for all models or an explicit ordered string array. Toggling from null produces only the chosen ID; it does not disable one item from an implicit full set. Explicit toggle removes the first matching occurrence or appends. enableAll appends absent target IDs and collapses to null only when the resulting length and membership match allIds. clearAll from null returns allIds minus targeted IDs, or [] for an unfiltered clear. move swaps adjacent positions only in an explicit enabled array. getSortedIds places explicit enabled IDs, including unavailable IDs and retained duplicates, ahead of other catalog IDs. The catalog Map is last-wins by provider/id while allIds can retain duplicates (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/scoped-models-selector.ts:18-127`).

The component propagates focus to Input, uses eight centered rows, fuzzy-filters available entries by ID/provider/name and unavailable entries by full ID, and shows unavailable rows instead of discarding them. In null/all mode available rows omit checkmarks; explicit mode shows enabled/disabled marks, while unavailable rows always display unavailable/disabled presentation. The footer counts available enabled IDs separately from unavailable IDs, lists toggle/all/clear/provider/reorder/save hints and marks unsaved edits. updateModels preserves selected identity when it remains visible and optionally replaces enabledIds only when its second argument is supplied. A refresh-status Text is created only if the constructor received a truthy status; later setRefreshStatus is a no-op otherwise (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/scoped-models-selector.ts:129-279`).

Navigation wraps. Toggle, enable/clear filtered results, provider-wide toggle and reorder mutate session state through onChange with a cloned array/null. Mutating shortcuts mark dirty even when their helper returns an unchanged value. Reorder applies to the full enabled array, while selectedIndex is adjusted by the same delta in the filtered list. refresh clamps only the upper bound, not zero: when the first filtered row is an enabled item later in full order, reordering up can leave selectedIndex=-1 and updateList dereferences the missing selected row. This is a source-derived TS defect, not a behavior a port should intentionally reproduce. onChange/onPersist allow Promise returns but are neither awaited nor caught. Save clears dirty immediately. Ctrl+C is hardcoded to clear a nonempty query or cancel; Escape is hardcoded cancel. Cancel does not revert previous onChange calls (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/scoped-models-selector.ts:211-227`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/scoped-models-selector.ts:269-404`).

The host seeds from current session scope when nonempty, otherwise resolves configured patterns while retaining no-match diagnostics as unavailable IDs. A change resolves available ordered selections into session.setScopedModels; null, explicit empty, all available selected, or an explicit set containing only unavailable models maps to runtime [] (unrestricted cycling), even though the UI distinguishes these states. Saving null or the exact complete available set clears the stored setting; otherwise it saves the explicit array, including []. These UI/runtime distinctions must not be collapsed into an assertion that clearing every checkbox disables every model (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:6505-6577`).

The host starts a 15,000 ms owned refresh, aborts on dispose and ignores closed completions. If the user has not edited and the initial session scope was empty, refreshed models are reconciled from original configured patterns; after an edit the current enabled IDs are retained. updateModels preserves selection/unavailable entries, and a non-null current scope is reapplied to the runtime. Timeout/provider-error/success messages are shown and the timer is cleared. Shared AUTH source review records full reads of regressions 3217,6949 and 7153; those test bodies are credited to the AUTH worker, not claimed as independent TUI reads (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:6578-6626`).
entries.interfaces: ModelsConfig{allModels, enabledModelIds:string[]|null, refreshStatus?}; ModelsCallbacks{onChange, onPersist, onCancel}, where change/persist may return void|Promise<void>. ScopedModelsSelectorComponent.updateModels(models, enabledModelIds?), setRefreshStatus(message, kind); session-only edits and explicit persistence are separate callbacks.
entries.dependency_text: AUTH-024 supplies configured-pattern resolution, current scope and cycling behavior. Settings owns storage accessors. TUI-044 is the related model selection view, not the scope editor.
entries.rust: The native `/scoped-models` selector reads saved settings, constructs a ten-row SelectList from catalog bare IDs, and toggles the first case-insensitive matching ID on Enter. It reports added/removed state as notes. Escape persists the accumulated list (None when empty) and closes, including on a save error; there is no distinct save action, search, provider-wide/filtered batch operations, reorder controls, unavailable configured rows or live AgentSession scope update in this callback (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/settings.rs:1858-1944`). AUTH-024 separately documents native bare-ID matching and startup/current cycling wiring. Existing native scope storage and the interactive toggle/save path are real partial counterparts.
entries.port: Build the ordered scope editor over existing native scope storage and AUTH resolution. Preserve unavailable explicit IDs and distinguish display selection, runtime unrestricted scope and saved configuration. Add live change plus explicit save/cancel semantics, refresh reconciliation and identity-based filtered reorder. Treat fixing the TS negative-index case and awaiting persistence errors as deliberate robustness decisions.
entries.priority_reason: This controls model cycling and saved order; native Escape-save and lack of live scope update materially differ from the TS session-only editing contract.

entries.title: Authentication option picker, configured-status labels and method routing
entries.what: Lists provider authentication options with method and configured-source status, filters them, and routes login/logout to the chosen method.
entries.mechanism:
Each AuthSelectorProvider carries id, name, authType oauth|api_key, optional method metadata and configured status. The picker decides once from the initial list whether to display auth-type labels (only if more than one auth type exists). Search includes name, ID, raw auth type and method name; status/source labels are not search keys. Filtering preserves/clamps the previous index rather than resetting to zero. Eight centered rows use TruncatedText with selected accent arrow, plus a scroll counter. Up/down clamp at the endpoints rather than wrap; confirm invokes onSelect(id, authType), cancel invokes onCancel and remaining input goes to Input. Focus propagates to Input (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/oauth-selector.ts:1-164`).

Unconfigured rows use a muted label. A configured credential of the other auth type shows a warning identifying subscription or API key. Same-type status with no source, OAuth, or stored credential is rendered as configured; an uppercase environment-name list is prefixed env:, while another source string is displayed verbatim. Login and logout have distinct titles/empty-list text, and an empty filtered result is distinct from having no available providers. Callbacks are synchronous from the component's perspective; it owns no refresh/disposal controller. The test at line 54 was redacted by the connector; visible ranges 1–53 and 55–148 were read, and no claim depends on the hidden line (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/oauth-selector.ts:165-215`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/oauth-selector.test.ts:1-53`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/oauth-selector.test.ts:55-148`).

The login host enumerates modelRuntime providers and makes an option for each supported OAuth/API-key method, attaching the same configured type/source status and sorting by provider name. A direct trimmed case-insensitive provider ID/name match with one option starts immediately; multiple methods open a method selector; a nonexact input becomes the provider search query. OAuth routes to showLoginDialog; API key with a login callback routes to showApiKeyLoginDialog; a method configured externally routes to ambient information. Method selection uses displayed labels and maps the chosen label by comparison, rather than carrying an opaque option ID. The exact API-key label assignment at interactive-mode.ts7027 was redacted and remains unverified (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:6933-7026`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:7028-7124`).

Logout enumerates stored credentials with a 15,000 ms AbortSignal timeout, labels them from current provider metadata with an ID fallback, and sorts by provider name. After selection the UI closes before asynchronous logout. It resolves the stored record by provider ID, invokes runtime.logout with the same bounded timeout, updates provider counts and reports success or a synchronization-specific error. Returning from a method-specific picker can reopen the all-method provider picker; a general cancel closes the selector. AUTH owns credential enumeration/storage/logout semantics and method implementations (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:6933-6975`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:7080-7181`).

entries.title: Provider authentication dialogs, prompt callbacks and editor restoration
entries.what: Replaces the editor during provider authentication, displays links/device codes/progress, resolves text or choice prompts and restores the editor after completion or cancellation.
entries.mechanism:
LoginDialogComponent is a bordered Container with an overrideable provider/title, dynamic content and a reusable Input. Focus propagates to Input. Its AbortController signal is passed to provider login. Submitting while a resolver exists reads the raw input, replaces each mounted reference to Input with plain Text prefixed '> ', resolves and clears the resolver/rejecter. There is no masking option in this dialog and the same path is used for API-key prompts, so submitted text can be echoed visibly. Cancellation aborts the signal, rejects a pending prompt with 'Login cancelled', clears it and invokes onComplete(false,...); it has no idempotence guard or separate dispose method (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/login-dialog.ts:11-91`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:7278-7325`).

showAuth clears content, shows an OSC8 URL and platform-specific Cmd/Ctrl click hint, appends optional warning instructions and calls openBrowser. showDeviceCode clears content and shows verification URI plus user code but does not automatically open a browser. showManualInput resets Input then appends prompt/input/cancel hint; showPrompt appends message/optional example/input/cancel+submit hints without clearing prior auth links. Each installs one new resolver pair: a concurrent second prompt would overwrite the first, and these methods do not check already-aborted signal. showDetails clears and replaces content, while showInfo/showWaiting/showProgress append messages and optional links/hints without a history cap. Every display method requests a render. handleInput checks the configured cancel binding first and otherwise forwards to Input even if it is currently unmounted (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/login-dialog.ts:93-234`).

The host mounts the dialog and restores the main editor/focus on both success and error. Ambient methods show external-configuration information without a provider login callback. API-key login can show Bedrock-specific alternative-auth documentation; otherwise API-key and OAuth both call modelRuntime.login with dialog.signal and the prompt/notify adapter. Prompt types map to a choice selector, manual-code input, or ordinary text input. Choice labels are displayed and the first matching label resolves its option ID, so duplicate labels are ambiguous. A supplied prompt.signal races the response against abort and removes its listener in finally; an already-aborted signal is checked after creating/displaying the response UI. It does not explicitly clear the dialog's pending resolver when the external signal wins (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:7255-7407`).

Auth notifications map auth_url to showAuth, device_code to showDeviceCode plus waiting text, info to showInfo and other messages to showProgress. Login cancellation suppresses the generic error notice; CredentialSynchronizationError produces a saved-credentials-but-local-state-failed message. Successful login restores the editor before completeProviderAuthentication. That completion helper uses the cached provider catalog to select the configured provider default only when the previous model was unknown, reports missing default/model/live-selection failures, updates provider count/footer/border, and reports credentials saved. It then starts a nonblocking provider-scoped 15,000 ms refresh whose failure produces a warning while preserving cached models. Thus login UI completion does not wait for the later catalog refresh (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:7183-7253`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:7384-7439`).

Shared AUTH evidence records full reads of regressions 5433 (prompt input) and 7027 (login completion before refresh timeout), plus 7443 for cached model-command resolution. This TUI entry independently reads the actual TS/native callers; provider credential persistence, callback execution and refresh internals stay with AUTH.
entries.interfaces: LoginDialogComponent(tui, providerId, onComplete, providerNameOverride?, titleOverride?); signal:AbortSignal; showAuth(url, instructions?), showDeviceCode(info), showManualInput(prompt):Promise<string>, showPrompt(message, placeholder?):Promise<string>, showDetails(lines), showInfo(message, links?, showCloseHint?), showWaiting, showProgress, handleInput. Host adapters use AuthPrompt and AuthEvent through modelRuntime.login.
entries.dependency_text: AUTH-015 owns the generic provider authentication host/runtime; other AUTH entries own provider-specific methods and credentials. TUI owns mounted component state, prompt display and editor restoration. Native browser-opening capability is not inferred from the separate CLI auth path.
entries.rust: Native TUI has masked API-key input with trim/nonempty validation, save/error handling, ReloadExtensions and editor restoration (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/settings.rs:821-895`). Generic OAuth creates a generation/flow ID, shows a waiting frame, renders returned title/URL/instruction strings and accepts an unmasked, trimmed, nonempty response for exchange. Credential and logout results are validated/saved/removed and restore the editor (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/settings.rs:897-1186`). Input callbacks are invoked after releasing the shared input-slot mutex; native tests cover this and API-key save/cancel restoration (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/settings.rs:788-797`, `rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/tests.rs:1958-2061`). The main caller consumes paste while waiting, routes active inputs before chat, and lets plain Escape restore the editor and reset the flow ID even during a worker action. request_oauth runs on spawn_blocking with an extension snapshot/keepalive; the result is ignored if its flow ID is stale. No abort token interrupts the blocking provider callback in this path (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui.rs:1863-1885`, `rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui.rs:2011-2037`, `rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui.rs:3148-3221`). The returned generic interaction UI lacks the full TS typed select/manual/device/info/progress callback presentation and automatic auth-URL browser opening. Native masked API-key input and stale-result rejection are capabilities to retain.
entries.port: Adapt the native auth protocol to the typed prompt/notification UI, preserving masking, nonempty validation, released-lock callbacks and stale-flow guards. Supply cancellation to cooperative provider work where supported and keep UI cancellation distinct from callback termination. Retain native API-key masking instead of deliberately copying the TS plaintext echo. Preserve editor restoration and nonblocking post-login refresh/error reporting.
entries.priority_reason: Provider authentication is interactive and failure-sensitive; missing prompt forms and incomplete cancellation semantics can strand a login or display incorrect completion state.

entries.title: Application keybinding catalog, legacy migration and configuration loading
entries.what: Adds the coding-agent action namespace and defaults to generic TUI keybindings, loads keybindings.json and translates legacy action names deterministically.
entries.mechanism:
KEYBINDINGS spreads TUI_KEYBINDINGS and adds 68 app actions; module augmentation exposes those IDs to generic keybinding consumers. The exact declaration/default/description catalog, source spans and four platform-sensitive expressions are preserved in tui-keybindings-catalog.json. Important defaults include Escape interrupt, Ctrl+C clear, Ctrl+D empty-editor exit, Shift+Tab thinking, Ctrl+P/Shift+Ctrl+P model cycling, Ctrl+L picker, Shift+F favorite, Ctrl+O/Alt+O/Shift+Alt+O tool expansion, F2 notices, ? shortcuts, Ctrl+B background, Down shells and contextual Agent Hub/view actions. Message send-now is Ctrl+Enter, follow-up Alt+Enter and dequeue Alt+Up. New/tree/fork/resume actions are defined with no default key. Panel/session/tree/model actions can intentionally share keys because their consumers supply context (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/keybindings.ts:13-297`).

Only suspend, clipboard paste and the order of the two tree fold/unfold alternatives vary here by platform. Suspend is unbound on Windows and Ctrl+Z elsewhere. Paste image is Alt+V on Windows and Ctrl+V elsewhere. Darwin prefers Alt+Left/Right before Ctrl+Left/Right for tree fold/unfold; other platforms reverse that order. TS backward model cycle, follow-up and dequeue are not Windows-specific in this frozen source. Native comments claiming their alternative Windows defaults match upstream are therefore stale for this baseline.

The 60-entry legacy map covers editor navigation/deletion/yank/undo, generic input/selection and older app/session/tree names. migrateKeybindingsConfig iterates raw object insertion order, maps a legacy key unless its namespaced target is already an own property, and marks migrated whenever a rename or shadowed legacy key is encountered. Namespaced values win independent of input order, including malformed values. Known IDs are output in catalog order, then unknown extras sorted lexicographically. Values are preserved by migration; toKeybindingsConfig later retains only strings or arrays composed entirely of strings. Empty arrays disable an action; null and mixed arrays are dropped at this stage. isLegacyKeybindingName uses the JavaScript in operator rather than an own-property test, an upstream edge case for inherited Object names that a robust port should handle deliberately (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/keybindings.ts:299-418`).

loadRawConfig returns undefined for missing files, parse/read errors, null or nonobject JSON, but accepts arrays as objects. KeybindingsManager.create resolves agentDir/keybindings.json, migrates and filters it in memory, then passes definitions and user bindings to the generic manager. It does not rewrite the file in this loader. reload is a no-op without configPath; otherwise it replaces user bindings from the same file, so an unreadable/invalid file resets to defaults. getEffectiveConfig delegates to resolved bindings. The independent migration runner owns disk rewriting; read-only tests cover that caller, namespaced precedence and loading old names before rewrite (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/keybindings.ts:420-462`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/keybindings-migration.test.ts:25-87`).
entries.interfaces: AppKeybinding=keyof 68 AppKeybindings; KEYBINDINGS includes inherited generic definitions; migrateKeybindingsConfig(raw):{config, migrated}; KeybindingsManager(userBindings={}, configPath?), static create(agentDir?), reload(), getEffectiveConfig(). Complete literal catalog and 60 migration pairs are in owned evidence/tui-keybindings-catalog.json.
entries.dependency_text: TUI-210 owns generic definition resolution/conflicts/matching. This entry owns application defaults, migration and the configuration-file/host bridge. CLI owns the migration runner's write invocation; Settings owns native storage fields.
entries.rust: The native generic registry defines 15 app actions, with 53 of these TS app IDs absent from that registry. This is a registry statement, not a blanket assertion that hardcoded controller actions are absent (`rust:crates/ice-tui/src/keybindings.rs:147-296`, `rust:crates/ice-tui/src/keybindings.rs:297-684`). Native Windows backward cycle uses Alt+P, dequeue Alt+Q, follow-up additionally Ctrl+Q and paste additionally Ctrl+V; these differ from the current TS defaults. Its real configured_keybindings bridge reads settings.keybindings, recognizes 11 app plus 4 viewport IDs, silently defaults on settings-read failure, accepts string/string-subset arrays/null, disables empty arrays/null, ignores a wholly invalid nonempty string list and applies partial valid lists. It installs a global clone plus an Arc for the host; it does not load separate keybindings.json or migrate legacy names (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/state.rs:407-472`). parse_configured_key lowercases/trims, accepts modifier aliases and F1–F12, takes the last nonmodifier token as the key and normalizes Shift+Tab to BackTab; keybinding_matches separately handles received BackTab (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/state.rs:350-405`, `rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/state.rs:474-491`).
entries.port: Extend the existing native registry/loader with the full application catalog and legacy mapping, and choose explicit compatibility for keybindings.json versus settings.keybindings. Preserve native working overrides and platform extras where intentional. Add reload/effective views through TUI-210 and preserve deterministic precedence/ordering without copying the inherited-property migration edge case.
entries.priority_reason: Missing configuration names and differing file/default semantics make copied user bindings silently ineffective on core interactive actions.
