entries.title: Custom editor action precedence, shell gutter and completed-mention decoration
entries.what: Wraps the generic editor with contextual app shortcuts, literal shell mode and visual chips for autocomplete-selected file/skill mentions without changing submitted text.
entries.mechanism:
Input routing first offers the raw packet to the extension shortcut callback. Next, conditional actions are checked in Map insertion order and claim only when both binding and canHandle match; false predicates fall through to editing. Clipboard-paste-image always consumes its matching key even if no callback is installed. Interrupt goes to the dynamic onEscape or registered interrupt handler only when autocomplete is closed; otherwise the generic editor handles menu cancellation. Exit invokes dynamic onCtrlD/registered exit only when getText().length===0, consumes that empty-editor key even without a callback, and otherwise falls through to editing. Other actions are checked in insertion order before the parent editor. Exceptions/async callback results are not handled by this wrapper (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/custom-editor.ts:108-172`).

The shell prefix is the first line's leading spaces/tabs plus one or two exclamation marks. It is displayed in the prompt gutter with one following space, while the source text retains its original prefix. Autocomplete is disabled whenever the whole text after trimStart begins with !, including later command lines; this differs from the first-line-only gutter detector for leading newline input. Ordinary embedded exclamation marks do not switch modes. Tests cover bang/double-bang commands, history/paste, home/backspace/undo and width/cursor mapping, as well as preventing an in-flight normal-mode completion from reopening a shell-mode menu. Those lower-level stale-request guards belong to TUI-255 (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/custom-editor.ts:34-46`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/custom-editor-shell-autocomplete.test.ts:23-82`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/custom-editor-shell-prompt.test.ts:17-105`).

setAutocompleteProvider forwards triggerCharacters, suggestions and application, with a default true for absent shouldTriggerFileCompletion. After applying a completion, it remembers item.value.trimEnd only when the query prefix and item value begin with @ or $, and the label does not end in /. The Set retains at most 256 tokens, evicting the earliest inserted distinct token; duplicate additions do not refresh insertion order. It is not cleared by this wrapper's setText/history changes or provider replacement. Unselected arbitrary variables, emails and unfinished queries are not styled.

Decorations begin with the parent spans and are disabled in shell mode. Each remembered token is found at whitespace/string boundaries, including all repeated occurrences. A mention normally conceals its one-character trigger; only a cursor exactly at its start on the matching logical line reveals that trigger. It uses selectedBg, accent for skills or syntaxString for files, bold, then explicit intensity/foreground/background resets. Parent decorations overlapping a mention are split into surrounding pieces; resulting mention and remaining spans are sorted by source start. Source text and expanded submission retain @/$ syntax. Tests cover quoted paths, trailing completion space, wide wrapping, caret mapping, undo/history and overlapping ordinary highlighters (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/custom-editor.ts:48-103`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/custom-editor-mentions.test.ts:37-173`).
entries.interfaces: CustomEditor extends Editor; actionHandlers Map<AppKeybinding,()=>void>; onAction, onConditionalAction(action, canHandle, handler); onEscape/onCtrlD/onPasteImage/onExtensionShortcut; overridden prompt prefix, autocomplete eligibility/provider, decoration and input routing.
entries.dependency_text: Terminal entries own generic editor decoration/conceal/caret and asynchronous completion mechanics. This entry owns the app wrapper, its selected-token registry and routing order; EXT owns extension shortcut registration/dispatch semantics.
entries.rust: Native Editor has a static EditorStyle prompt, state/undo/paste/working fields and submit/change callbacks, without an application action Map, completed-mention registry or decoration/conceal hooks in the inspected component state/API (`rust:crates/ice-tui/src/editor.rs:20-84`, `rust:crates/ice-tui/src/editor.rs:249-367`). Application dispatch is nevertheless real in the primary CLI: extension shortcuts are offered before release filtering, preparation cancellation and modal routing; active provider/dialog inputs take precedence, and later branches handle app actions such as interrupt/external editor/tool expansion (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui.rs:1937-2045`, `rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui.rs:2240-2290`). Native host autocomplete is separately retained by TUI-241/255. The remaining gap is a comparable reusable wrapper/conditional-action contract and shell/selected-mention presentation, not native keyboard handling generally.
entries.port: Layer contextual application actions on the native editor without breaking host modal/release/preparation routing. Add shell gutter/autocomplete suppression and a bounded selected-mention registry through the generic decoration/caret interface. Keep submission text literal and preserve nonclaiming key fallthrough; treat callback failures and retained mention lifetime explicitly.
entries.priority_reason: Core editing works natively, but contextual shortcuts and visual source-to-display mapping differ in common shell and attachment workflows.

entries.title: External-editor process lifecycle, terminal handoff and draft replacement
entries.what: Temporarily yields the terminal to an external editor and replaces the draft only after successful completion.
entries.mechanism:
editInExternalEditor creates a private mkdtemp directory under tmpdir with prefix ice-editor-, writes prompt.md as UTF-8, splits the supplied command on literal spaces and passes the temporary path after those arguments. Quoting and repeated spaces are not parsed as shell words. It logs the command and asynchronously spawns with inherited stdio, using shell:true only on Windows. Spawn error resolves a null exit code; any nonzero/null code returns failed. Exit 0 reads UTF-8 and removes exactly one trailing LF. Filesystem creation/write/read errors propagate instead of becoming failed. The directory is removed recursively/force in finally after creation, and cleanup errors are ignored (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/external-editor.ts:13-44`).

The interactive caller gets the settings-resolved editor command, expands folded pastes when supported, stops the TUI before launching, replaces text only for status complete, and restarts the TUI with a forced redraw in finally. Failed child exit leaves the existing draft unchanged; thrown helper errors still restore the UI and propagate. There is no helper timeout or abort signal. Tests and the inert fixture were read rather than executed; they cover original content, temporary directory privacy/cleanup, child failure and intentionally empty edited content (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:5707-5723`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/external-editor.test.ts:35-63`).
entries.interfaces: ExternalEditorOptions{command, content}; ExternalEditorResult={status:'complete', content}|{status:'failed'}; editInExternalEditor(options):Promise<ExternalEditorResult>. Host owns terminal stop/start and settings-based command resolution.
entries.dependency_text: Settings owns external-editor command resolution; terminal entries own start/stop behavior, and the application must call that handoff around this process.
entries.rust: Native launch_external_editor uses a worker thread, a NamedTempFile with ice-draft- prefix/.md suffix, writes the expanded draft and chooses ICERS_EXTERNAL_EDITOR (nonblank), then VISUAL, EDITOR, or notepad/nano. Command::new receives the whole environment string as one executable with no argument parsing. Successful exit reads the file without stripping a trailing newline; errors are returned through TuiMessage (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/run.rs:72-118`). The key caller launches and immediately continues with no terminal stop/start or exclusive editor-operation state in this path; result handling unconditionally replaces the current draft. A late result can therefore overwrite edits made while the child was open. It sets cursor row 0 and col=text.chars().count, but Editor.set_cursor interprets col as a byte offset in that row, giving incorrect multiline/non-ASCII positioning (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui.rs:2271-2280`, `rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui.rs:2901-2912`, `rust:crates/ice-tui/src/editor.rs:548-562`). Existing native temp-file cleanup and explicit error messages remain credited.
entries.port: Add terminal/input ownership around the native child and restore it on every exit/error path. Resolve editor command configuration consistently, choose explicit argv parsing compatibility, apply a successful result to the intended draft generation and place the cursor using row plus byte offsets. Preserve native error details while matching intentional empty content and trailing-LF behavior where required.
entries.priority_reason: Without terminal handoff a terminal editor can compete with the running TUI; unguarded completion can overwrite a newer draft.

entries.title: Responsive shortcut overview and effective hotkey transcript
entries.what: Shows a compact responsive shortcut overview from an empty prompt and a longer transcript block using current bindings and extension shortcuts.
entries.mechanism:
ShortcutsViewComponent removes empty sections and builds a title, section columns and footer. It measures rendered cell widths and uses a three-column gap plus two leading spaces; if the total fits, rows from all sections are padded side by side, otherwise sections stack with blank separators. Every output row is finally truncated to width. Section key alignment measures visible width but uses String.padEnd for padding, so ANSI/wide public input keys can be misaligned. invalidate is a no-op because rendering rebuilds from stored sections/current theme. Any input packet closes and is consumed (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/shortcuts-view.ts:15-67`).

The ? app action is conditional on an empty default editor and no autocomplete. showShortcutsView resolves current app/editor key labels, builds Compose, Session and Transcript sections, removes rows whose binding display is empty and mounts the overview in the selector/editor slot. The fixed slash/bang rows and mapped message/model/tool/notices/subagent actions are explicit; this is not an automatic enumeration of all catalog definitions. Tests assert side-by-side, narrow stacking, width bounds and any-key closure (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:3687-3692`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:7877-7923`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/shortcuts-view.test.ts:18-47`).

The separate /hotkeys command obtains effective navigation/editing/core app key displays, interpolates Markdown tables, appends extensionRunner.getShortcuts(getEffectiveConfig()) with description or extensionPath fallback, and adds the bordered Markdown block to the transcript. Its fixed core rows do not enumerate all 68 app actions, despite the compact overview footer saying /hotkeys lists every shortcut. Extension descriptions are interpolated directly into Markdown. The display is generated when invoked rather than subscribed for later binding changes (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:7945-8059`).

Shared key-label helpers resolve current bindings every time they are called. formatKeyText splits alternatives by '/' and each chord by '+', maps any case spelling of alt to option only on Darwin, optionally capitalizes the first character of each displayed part, and rejoins without trimming or reordering. keyText returns current getKeys joined by '/', or an empty string for no bindings; keyDisplayText enables capitalization. keyHint styles the key as dim and a leading-space description as muted, so an unbound key still leaves the styled description; rawKeyHint formats a supplied key string instead of looking up a binding (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/keybinding-hints.ts:1-49`).
entries.dependency_text: Uses application effective bindings, generic width/truncation and Markdown rendering; EXT owns shortcut resolution/conflicts, while this entry owns help presentation.
entries.rust: Native /hotkeys is registered and adds a themed static table of key labels/descriptions to the transcript (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/commands.rs:104-114`, `rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/rendering.rs:317-359`). It does not derive those strings from configured_keybindings, append extension shortcuts or provide the empty-editor ? responsive modal. Existing native help is retained as a partial counterpart; stale help after user overrides is a concrete consequence of its literal key table.
entries.port: Build the compact overview from effective bindings and add native extension shortcuts to /hotkeys. Preserve the existing transcript help path, use cell-aware key padding, and make the footer's scope match the actual list.
entries.priority_reason: Discoverability and accuracy of configured shortcuts matter, but the underlying actions have independent implementations.

entries.title: Notice store, badge counts, sticky state and derived-group dismissal
entries.what: Keeps a session-local diagnostic history with stable identities, repeat counts, active badges, derived groups and dismissals.
entries.mechanism:
Notice records carry id, four kinds, twelve ordered categories (extensions, mcp, tools, skills, prompts, themes, compaction, subagents, model, session, console, updates), source/title/detail, sticky/quiet/group flags, createdAt/updatedAt and count. add globally replaces by id, keeps first creation time, increments repeats, refreshes update time, trims and emits even for identical content. list returns a new array containing the stored mutable objects. orderNotices sorts nonquiet before quiet, error→warning→update→info, then newest update. counts counts records rather than repeats and excludes info and quiet records (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/notice-center.ts:7-101`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/notice-center.ts:158-198`).

replaceGroup deletes missing current group entries, remembers dismissed group/id pairs while that identity continues to appear, and forgets a tombstone once the incoming group no longer contains its id. Surviving entries retain creation time and count. Its unchanged check compares group, kind, title, detail only: changes solely to source/category/sticky/quiet are ignored. Identities are globally keyed even across groups. dismiss/dismissWhere refuse sticky records, add group tombstones and emit only on removal. Trimming above 500 evicts nonsticky quiet records first, then oldest updates; all-sticky records can exceed 500 and eviction does not create dismissal tombstones. Subscribers receive no initial callback and exceptions are not isolated (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/notice-center.ts:104-198`).

Tests cover deduplication, badge exclusions, sticky protection, subscriber counts, group disappearance/reappearance and quiet/old eviction. They do not establish a strict 500 maximum for all-sticky data or updates to the fields omitted from group equality (`ice:packages/coding-agent/test/notice-center.test.ts:35-123`).
entries.interfaces: NoticeKind; NoticeCategory; NOTICE_CATEGORIES; Notice, NoticeInput, NoticeCounts; SAFETY_NOTICE_CAPABILITIES{safety:bash:bash, safety:external:external}; orderNotices; MAX_NOTICES=500; NoticeCenter(now=Date.now):add, replaceGroup, dismiss, dismissWhere, list, counts, subscribe.

entries.title: Diagnostic reducers, console capture and notices attached to prompts
entries.what: Turns tool/model/compaction/resource/subagent events into notices, routes extension and console diagnostics, and can attach a diagnostic snapshot to a model prompt.
entries.mechanism:
The event reducer ignores successful tools and creates quiet tool failures keyed by call id with JSON arguments and text output; MCP names match a nonletter-bounded case-insensitive mcp, then exact agent/subagent classify children. Assistant error messages use provider/model plus first error line as identity; retries become quiet warnings until terminal failure. Compaction cancellation/success become quiet info, retryable failure quiet warning and terminal failure error; summary-retry events are quiet warnings. Details use a 6000 UTF-16-character cap plus an omitted-count suffix; arguments/summary use 2000. IDs built with Date.now can collide within one millisecond (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/notice-sources.ts:11-164`).

Subagent overview derivation emits configuration errors, pending-approval warnings, blocked-child warnings, failed/abandoned last-turn errors and quiet completed outcomes; blocked state wins, while a failed last turn can remain visible for a running child. Facts include agent/state/turns/tokens/patch. Resource notices identify category/type/path/message, display formatted source paths, retain collision winner/loser paths and mark collisions quiet. Reports reuse notice ordering, show active counts and logged entries, prefix details as diagnostic data and include age/repeats/sticky state. They stop after 40 entries or an approximate 20000-character body budget and cap each detail at 1500; separators and the omitted footer are appended outside the budget check, and titles/sources are uncapped. Tests assert <=21000 for their bounded fixture rather than a universal exact limit (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/notice-sources.ts:167-321`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/notice-sources.test.ts:116-249`).

The host retains tool arguments from start until end, records parent-session notices before child-view display filtering, replaces resource and subagent groups, and feeds counts/capabilities to the footer. Extension warning/error with id goes only to the store (safety: prefix selects session category); without id it goes both to chat and store. Info stays chat-only in notify. Extension-console records key by path+text and are not quiet; runtime log/info are quiet, warning/error active, keyed by full formatted text. Global console methods pass through while stopped/shutting down and are restored explicitly. Text-bearing IDs and tool-argument retention have no independent byte/count cap. Slow handlers, model-catalog failures and available release/package updates add notices (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:675-740`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:1477-1609`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:1995-2022`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:3494-3532`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:4038-4125`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:5756-5795`).

/notices <prompt> rejects while compacting before editor mutation, then clears the editor, records the complete command in history and creates a displayed customType:notices report with count metadata. Streaming delivery sends report as steer then prompt with streamingBehavior:steer; idle delivery queues report for nextTurn, flushes pending Bash components and starts/enqueues the user prompt. Report/send errors are not rolled back after editor clearing. Tests cover notification routing, runtime console pass-through/restoration and both prompt delivery orders (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:1493-1521`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/notice-center.test.ts:125-235`).

The separately exported deprecation utility has module-local exact-message deduplication: warnDeprecation(message) returns if its Set already contains the string; otherwise it adds the string before console.warn(chalk.yellow(`Deprecation warning: ${message}`)). clearDeprecationWarningsForTests() clears that Set. The recorded bounded production-source search found only the definitions, so this is a dormant utility contract, not evidence that an active runtime path emits these warnings (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/deprecation.ts:1-15`).
entries.dependency_text: Consumes session events and custom-message delivery, resource diagnostics and subagent overview; those producers retain their own ownership. Extension callback ABI is already audited in EXT, while this entry owns the interactive diagnostic consumer.
entries.rust: Native error and neutral-note rendering remains available (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/rendering.rs:416-487`), as do extension status mailboxes (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/state.rs:178-192`). Independent native search found no notice reducer/store or /notices attachment command. The native UI components and event state were inspected directly; a visible transcript error is credited but does not supply grouped history, badges or report delivery.
entries.port: Route existing native session/resource/extension/subagent diagnostics into the notice store and implement the report command using native custom-message delivery. Preserve bounded detail, diagnostic-data labeling, parent-view collection and console restoration. Choose explicit byte limits for IDs/reports and cleanup for unmatched tool starts rather than inheriting accidental unbounded state.
entries.priority_reason: A consolidated diagnostic view and model-visible report are central to recovering from silent extension, model and background-task failures.

entries.title: Responsive notices inspector, filters, copy and dismissal
entries.what: Replaces the editor with a live notices list and detail inspector while the transcript remains visible.
entries.mechanism:
The panel starts on Problems when any nonquiet warning/error exists; Problems itself includes quiet errors/warnings. Tabs contain All, Problems and only categories present, in declared order. Up/down clamp selection; left/right wrap filters and reset selection; page keys scroll details by 16; dismiss respects sticky state; clear applies to the current filter; copy asynchronously sends title/category/source/detail and shows success/error. Escape or the notices-show action closes. Selected identity is kept where possible; a render fallback after its removal assigns a new id without resetting detailOffset. Subscription requests redraw without a timer, so age text advances only on another render; dispose unsubscribes, but outstanding copy callbacks have no disposal guard (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/notices-view.ts:88-194`).

The list shows 14 rows centered around selection with above/below indicators, kind symbols, repeat count and age. Detail wraps title, category/source/seen data, sticky explanation and a 16-row body window. At width>=110 list and detail sit in roughly equal columns separated by a border; narrower terminals stack them. Filters are a clipped single row rather than a scrolling tab strip. Most rows are cell-truncated, but the header is emitted without a final width clamp and wrapped title height is unrestricted. oneRow removes CR/LF but is not a general control-sequence sanitizer. Tests establish category filtering, quiet Problem inclusion, sticky/dismiss/copy/close actions, detail scrolling, width 60 for their fixture and unsubscribe-on-dispose (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/notices-view.ts:196-312`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/notice-center.test.ts:257-335`).

The host binds app.notices.show and mounts the panel via showSelector with focus and explicit disposal, retaining the transcript above it (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:3687-3692`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:7936-7942`).
entries.interfaces: NoticeFilter; NoticesViewComponent(center, keybindings, onClose,{requestRender?, copy?, now?}); handleInput, invalidate, render, dispose; exported formatAge.
entries.dependency_text: Uses the notice store, configured app actions, width/wrapping primitives and clipboard helper. Generic selector focus/lifecycle is audited at the controller boundary.
entries.rust: Native SelectorKind enumerates model/thinking/tools/images/session/theme/provider/scoped/settings/tree/extension, without notices (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/state.rs:42-95`). Native error/note output remains transcript-only (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/rendering.rs:416-487`). Scoped native search found no notice panel or filter/dismiss implementation; generic selectable lists do not implement this two-pane diagnostic contract.
entries.port: Add the notice inspector using existing native focus/layout/clipboard facilities. Preserve stable selection, filtered dismissal and sticky notices; explicitly bound header/title output and ignore asynchronous copy completion after disposal.
entries.priority_reason: Without the inspector, accumulated diagnostics cannot be filtered, copied or dismissed through the terminal UI.

entries.title: Live background-shell list, details, foreground follow and stop controls
entries.what: Lets users inspect and stop background shells from a live editor-slot panel.
entries.mechanism:
The panel subscribes to registry changes with one 100 ms coalescing timer and a 1 s runtime ticker (disableable for tests). It initially selects the newest running snapshot, honors an optional initial id and opens details directly when exactly one shell is running. The list includes only running shells; details/follow retain the selected completed/killed shell until returning to the list. Selection clamps. Enter/right opens details, f enters follow, left moves follow→details→list, Enter in details closes, Escape always closes, and stop calls registry.kill(id,{notify:true}) and reports the result. dispose unsubscribes and clears both timers (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/shells-panel.ts:73-168`).

The ten-row list displays id, runtime, first command line and status markers. Detail shows status/origin, elapsed time, at most three wrapped command rows, optional log path and eight wrapped tail rows; follow uses 24 tail rows. Running output comes from the current snapshot; finished output prefers finalText, while killed output adds final status to accumulated output. ANSI/OSC escapes and most controls are removed, each CR-redrawn line keeps only its final segment, text is trimmed, empty output gets a state-specific placeholder, and every final row is width-clamped. Hidden earlier output is indicated; this panel tails rather than scrolls arbitrary historical output (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/shells-panel.ts:31-71`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/shells-panel.ts:170-289`).

Host Down opens shells only with an empty default editor, no autocomplete and at least one running shell; otherwise normal editor movement remains available. The panel occupies the selector/editor slot with disposal callback. Tests cover newest selection, live output/CR normalization, stop notification, terminal-state retention until back, direct single-shell details, width 40 and repaint after output (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:3703-3711`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:7926-7933`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/shells-panel.test.ts:42-153`).
entries.interfaces: ShellsPanelComponent(registry, keybindings, onClose,{requestRender?, now?, tick?, initialShellId?}); handleInput, invalidate, render, dispose. Views:list/details/follow; consumes BackgroundShellSnapshot and registry onChange/list/kill.
entries.dependency_text: TOOLS owns native/background process snapshots, retention, stopping and output semantics. This entry owns only the interactive list/detail/follow consumer.
entries.rust: Native direct Bash execution already has an elapsed/streaming transcript component and cancellation token, these user-Bash capabilities are retained under TUI-035 (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui.rs:559-630`, `rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/state.rs:202-209`). Native SelectorKind has no shell view (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/state.rs:42-95`), and an independent crates-wide search for ShellsPanel,/shells, shells_panel and shell-panel equivalents found none. No absence of background process support is inferred. Native user-Bash streaming/cancellation does not by itself establish the model-facing background registry/control contract.
entries.port: Build the live panel over the background-shell registry and stop contract owned by TOOLS, wire the conditional editor action and dispose all timers/subscriptions on close or session replacement. Preserve finished selection during follow and explicit model notification when stopped; retain the already-working native user-Bash streaming/cancellation path.
entries.priority_reason: Users need direct visibility and stop controls for work moved out of the foreground.

entries.title: Transcript prompt-row indexing and sticky prompt navigation
entries.what: Identifies which user prompt owns the answer currently visible while browsing older fullscreen transcript output.
entries.mechanism:
TranscriptDocument flattens only its designated chat container's direct children while rendering the document once; direct UserMessageComponent children record their starting rendered row and raw message text. Other nested containers are rendered normally, without recursively indexing prompts. prompts exposes the most recent render's array. StickyPromptHeader resets its target each render, hides outside fullscreen, while following the end, at nonpositive width or when no earlier prompt exists, then searches backward for the last prompt row<=scrollTop. It also hides when that prompt starts exactly at the viewport top. The one-line label uses the first nonblank prompt line, trims/collapses whitespace, truncates with ellipsis, fills the row with user-message colors and wraps the full row in an internal scroll-prompt OSC8 link (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/sticky-prompt.ts:18-96`).

The host places the sticky header above the primary transcript scroll view and routes its internal URL to the currently exposed targetRow, requesting render even if the target vanished. This uses prompt rows from the last document render rather than performing a second source-message scan. Tests establish actual rendered row positions, latest preceding prompt selection, same-row/follow-end hiding, OSC8 target, fullscreen visibility and width 20 clipping (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:1051-1096`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:5671-5675`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/sticky-prompt.test.ts:27-79`).
entries.interfaces: TranscriptDocument(chat):prompts, render; StickyPromptHeader(document, scrollView, theme, isVisible):targetRow, invalidate, render; JUMP_TO_PROMPT_URL=ice-action:scroll-prompt via shared prefix.
entries.dependency_text: Uses user-message rendering, internal action routing and primary scroll geometry. Primitive mouse/link behavior is separate from application prompt identity.
entries.rust: Native transcript navigation installs a generic jump-to-latest indicator and handles top/bottom/page keys (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/transcript_navigation.rs:7-59`). Its jump helper composites a button into the bottom transcript row and does not index user-message ownership (`rust:crates/ice-tui/src/jump_to_end.rs:22-100`). An independent untruncated crates search for sticky prompt, promptRows/prompt_rows and scroll-prompt counterparts found none. Native scrolling is retained; the missing contract is prompt-aware sticky context and return navigation.
entries.port: Track native user prompt positions during transcript layout, expose the most recent layout identity and render a clickable sticky header. Keep geometry synchronized across width/theme changes and ensure hidden/replaced transcripts cannot leave a stale target.
entries.priority_reason: Browsing long answers loses their initiating prompt without a persistent context header.

entries.title: New assistant-message counts and jump-to-bottom dock pill
entries.what: Shows new assistant response groups received while the user is scrolled away from the end and provides a direct jump back.
entries.mechanism:
NewMessagesPill snapshots the message-array length on the first visible render away from the end, resets on transcript-id change or shrinking message count, and clears its snapshot while hidden or following. It scans only later entries: a nonblank text assistant starts one count until a user or toolResult resets the group; tool-only/blank assistant entries are skipped without resetting, and other roles also leave grouping unchanged. It does not count newly added text within an assistant already included in the snapshot. The label shows count/pluralization or Jump to bottom, current configured Bottom key and a down arrow. It truncates to nonnegative width, centers by visible cells and wraps the selected-background label in an internal OSC8 link (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/new-messages-pill.ts:10-63`).

The host supplies the displayed session's messages plus the streaming message, and a transcript id combining displayed view/session. The pill is fullscreen-only, positioned after queued/status/above-editor widgets and immediately before the editor. Click calls scrollToEnd. Tests cover grouping, ignored tool-only messages, reset on bottom/view switch, keys and widths 0/1/5/20/80, click dispatch, End before editor handling, and exact dock placement at 80×24 and 40×12 even after activity rows are removed (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:1064-1096`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:5657-5662`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/new-messages-pill.test.ts:20-231`).

entries.title: Context occupancy grid, proportional bar, category details and largest entries
entries.what: Renders a context-window breakdown as category-colored grid/bar, usage provenance, free/reserved capacity and detailed sources.
entries.mechanism:
The view holds a supplied breakdown snapshot and model label. Ten categories map to fixed theme tokens: systemPrompt→syntaxType, contextFiles→syntaxString, skills→syntaxFunction, tools→syntaxKeyword, promptAdditions→syntaxNumber, conversation→accent, toolResults→warning, extensionMessages→customMessageLabel, summaries→success, shell→syntaxOperator. ASCII uses #/./o and =/-/.; other symbol presets use round dot/free/reserve and line glyphs. Allocation clamps negative category tokens to zero, targets the rounded measured share with a minimum cell per positive category when possible, distributes largest remainders, removes excess from largest allocations and finally drops smallest categories if categories outnumber cells (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/context-usage.ts:8-97`).

The grid is 20×10 cells separated by spaces; the bar is at most 72 columns. Used category estimates are scaled to measured total for allocation, while legend/part labels retain their supplied unscaled estimates. Free and auto-compact reserve have separate glyphs. Width>=92 places legend beside grid; narrower output stacks it. The header reports used/window, percentage (<0.1 for a positive sub 0.1 share) and estimated/provider-reported provenance. Details show per-category parts and supplied largest entries; a simple startsWith(homedir) replaces the home prefix without a path-boundary test. Footnotes explain approximate four-character tokens and compaction threshold/off state. Output rows are clipped to max(1, width), so public width 0 is not a strict zero-column contract (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/context-usage.ts:103-265`).

/context obtains the session breakdown and model, warns if either is unavailable, then inserts a snapshot component into chat. It does not subscribe that old component to future usage. Tests cover rendering at 140/70 columns, source/category content, dot glyphs and allocation's many-small-category/minimum/total bounds (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:7830-7840`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/context-breakdown.test.ts:159-213`).
entries.interfaces: allocateCells(categories, scale, window, total):number[]; ContextUsageComponent(breakdown, modelLabel):invalidate, render. ContextBreakdown values are supplied by the session computation, not recomputed from rendered text.
entries.dependency_text: SESSION-037 owns occupancy/tool-source computation; SESSION-027 owns all-history usage and uncertainty. This entry owns allocation/presentation and /context caller behavior.
entries.rust: Native /context is hidden from autocomplete, prints discovered context files/skills/templates and requests ShowUsage. The async native handler appends message/token/cache/cost totals, cumulative input/output, lane/leaf and active operation. It is a genuine text report, but not occupancy by system/tool/conversation category, a reserve-aware grid or largest-entry view (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/commands.rs:738-773`, `rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/rendering.rs:489-564`, `rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui.rs:3086-3135`). Native footer percentage remains separate and does not establish breakdown parity.
entries.port: Add the proportional category view using native occupancy data once SESSION-037 is satisfied. Retain discovered-resource and native lane/operation information, and distinguish estimates from measured totals without implying unscaled legend values sum exactly to the measured total.
entries.priority_reason: Context pressure is hard to diagnose without identifying which sources consume the window.

entries.title: Saved versus current project trust selector and restart semantics
entries.what: Shows project trust choices with inherited saved decisions and the current session's separate effective state.
entries.mechanism:
The component obtains getProjectTrustOptions(cwd), starts on the first option whose savedPath and trusted value exactly match the saved decision, or index 0. It renders cwd, saved decision (none, trusted/untrusted path, or inherited ancestor), current-session trust and each option with saved checkmark/current selection. Up/down and literal k/j clamp; confirm or LF emits only trusted and updates; cancel invokes the callback. All option rows render, with no separate viewport. The selection is based on the stored decision rather than effective current-session trust (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/trust-selector.ts:21-133`).

The host reads the store before opening the selector, writes all selected updates synchronously, closes and reports that restart is required. It does not immediately toggle the live runtime/resources. A store exception before done leaves the selector unresolved; no local error catch exists. Tests assert saved markers, default confirmation, inherited labels and parent-trust updates that clear a more-specific child decision (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:6447-6470`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/trust-selector.test.ts:17-86`).
entries.interfaces: TrustSelection=Pick<ProjectTrustOption, trusted|updates>; TrustSelectorOptions{cwd, savedDecision, projectTrusted, onSelect, onCancel}; TrustSelectorComponent.handleInput. SET-003 defines the choices, inheritance and transactional store semantics.
entries.dependency_text: Core trust resolution/storage and extension project_trust hooks remain SET-003/EXT ownership; this entry owns interactive selection and explicit deferred effect.
entries.rust: Native /trust parses empty/yes/y/true as true, no/n/false as false, clear/reset/none as removal; invalid values print usage. It calls config::set_project_trust and reports success/failure with redraw. There is no selector or display of saved ancestor/current effective trust, and the empty command immediately writes trusted. The handler also does not reload live runtime state, while its success text omits the TS restart guidance (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/commands.rs:590-631`). Preserve the implemented persistence command; SET-003 compares store/inheritance behavior.
entries.port: Add an interactive no-argument trust selector with saved/current-state labels and parent options, retaining explicit argument commands. Report the actual activation timing and surface failed writes while leaving the user's selection recoverable.
entries.priority_reason: A trust change must clearly distinguish persistence from the state of the already-running session.

entries.title: Subagent footer projection, resident counts, bounded activity and attention status
entries.what: Projects the live/historical agent view bridge into a compact footer with stable child identity, actual resident work/queue counts and advisory attention.
entries.mechanism:
The snapshot includes all non-parent views. Labels use role or label plus taskId or the first eight runId characters, replace C0/DEL controls with spaces, collapse spaces and clip to 128 cells. It takes the last three activities before filtering stale running activities from terminal views, then projects only bounded toolName (64 cells), optional path (96) and outcome. It freezes the outer snapshot, children, entries and activity projection; checkIn is retained by reference, so this is not a deep freeze of every nested supplied value. A displayed parent deliberately has no selected child fallback. Retained counts include reusable views; live attention includes finalization, defined repeat-failure count and due/queued/consumed/owner-unavailable check-ins (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/subagent-view-switcher.ts:60-199`).

Terminal statuses normalize underscores/hyphens, while a live finalization phase with absent/working control becomes FINALIZING. Advisory check-in state changes attention and detail text without replacing a working control state. The component subscribes to bridge events and replaces stale sampled view work counts with resident runtime-overview running/queued counts; liveCount remains the bridge count and only positive idle counts render. Elapsed time is supplied state, not advanced by a component timer. Dispose unsubscribes once (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/subagent-view-switcher.ts:113-148`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/subagent-view-switcher.ts:244-295`).

No children produces no rows. Width below 44 gives count-only text; 44–71 gives one identity/status row; at least 72 gives a second row only when selected-child detail exists. Detail includes outcome markers, safe activity, floored elapsed seconds, check-in status/ISO due time and repeat failures. Main view omits navigation hints; child view shows interrupt-to-main and previous/next bindings. Rows are cell-clipped/padded; customized appearance selects attention/running/muted presentation and may add a chrome border at width at least eight. Tests cover frozen bounded projections, terminal stale activity suppression, advisory owner-unavailable state, parent selection, overview precedence and 20/43/60/71/72/120-column output (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/subagent-view-switcher.ts:298-350`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/subagent-footer.test.ts:81-384`).
entries.dependency_text: SUB-016/036 own view lifetime, live/historical projection and input controls; SUB-037 owns the Hub. This entry owns the footer projection and presentation, not child execution or management.
entries.rust: The independently read native child host has plugin-owned jobs, cancellation, bounded text deltas and destructive polling that exposes running/done/failed and delays terminal results until queued deltas drain. entries.title: User-message fork picker and asynchronous fork result handoff
entries.what: Lets the user choose a prior user message as the fork point and restores that selected text into the editor after a successful runtime fork.
entries.mechanism:
The list preserves caller order, starts at the requested entry ID or the last message, and renders ten centered items. Each item has a newline-normalized, trimmed, width-minus-two clipped text row, a Message i of N metadata row and a blank row. Timestamp is accepted but unused. Metadata, empty-state and scroll-indicator rows are not independently width-clipped. Up/down wrap; selection is guarded when empty. The wrapper adds a heading/explanation/borders and exposes the inner list for focus. Empty input schedules onCancel after 100 ms without storing a cancellation handle (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/user-message-selector.ts:14-154`).

The interactive host prechecks an empty message list, selects the newest available entry initially and closes the selector before awaiting runtimeHost.fork(entryId). Cancellation only redraws; success sets selectedText or empty text and posts status; errors are reported. Because the picker closes before the await, this caller has no late-draft ownership guard when it writes the returned text (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:6628-6664`).
entries.interfaces: UserMessageItem{id:string, text:string, timestamp?:string}; UserMessageList.onSelect/onCancel; UserMessageSelectorComponent(messages, initialSelectedId), getMessageList. The callback carries the durable entry ID, not a visual row index.
entries.dependency_text: SESSION-021 owns fork/runtime replacement effects and cancellation. This entry owns the user-message choice, focus and editor result handoff.
entries.rust: The native fork command obtains current metadata and calls fork_typed with ForkOptions::default(), then installs the fork and rebuilds history. Its active command route invokes that default fork directly; it does not present a user-message fork-point list or return selected text into a protected editor draft (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/sessions.rs:198-264`, `rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui.rs:3137-3147`). Native session tree navigation is a separate implemented picker, not proof of selected-message fork parity.
entries.port: Add an entry-ID user-message picker and route the selected point to the native fork API. Preserve cancellation/error feedback and protect text typed after the picker closes from late fork completion; clip all ancillary rows and give empty-state timers explicit lifetime ownership.
entries.priority_reason: Forking from a chosen user turn is a distinct workflow from duplicating the current leaf.

entries.title: Session fuzzy, quoted-phrase and regular-expression search with ordering modes
entries.what: Searches session identity, name, conversation text and cwd using composable fuzzy/phrase tokens or an explicit regular expression.
entries.mechanism:
The searchable text concatenates id, optional name, allMessagesText and cwd; path is not included. Only the lowercase prefix re: selects regex mode; the trimmed pattern compiles with i, and empty/invalid expressions produce no results. Otherwise quote toggling extracts phrases and outside-quote whitespace splits fuzzy tokens. There is no quote escape syntax. An unmatched quote falls back to whitespace tokens from the original query, retaining the quote character (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/session-selector-search.ts:17-114`).

Every token must match. Fuzzy tokens use the TUI fuzzy score; phrases match lowercased, whitespace-collapsed text and cost 0.1 times the match position. Regex also costs 0.1 times its first match position. Named-only uses a trimmed nonempty name. Empty queries preserve incoming order and may return the same array; recent mode filters without independently sorting by modified. Relevance and nonempty threaded queries sort total score ascending, then modified descending. Invalid regex has no separate error object in the filtering result (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/session-selector-search.ts:116-194`).

Tests assert phrase whitespace/case behavior, regex handling, stable recent order, relevance ties, invalid patterns and the named-only filter. These are source-read assertions, not executed test results (`ice:packages/coding-agent/test/session-selector-search.test.ts:1-196`).
entries.interfaces: SortMode=threaded|recent|relevance; NameFilter=all|named; ParsedSearchQuery{mode:tokens|regex, tokens:{kind:fuzzy|phrase, value:string}[], regex:RegExp|null, error?:string}; MatchResult{matches:boolean, score:number}; parseSearchQuery(query), matchSession(session, parsed), hasSessionName(session), filterAndSortSessions(sessions, query, sortMode, nameFilter). getSessionSearchText is private.
entries.dependency_text: TUI-235 owns the generic fuzzy matcher. This entry owns session corpus, query parsing, filtering and session-specific ordering.
entries.rust: The native picker builds search text from display label, short ID and file stem, then wraps a generic searchable selector. It lists only the current cwd session directory. Its caller does not include allMessagesText or cwd, parse phrase/regex modes, implement named-only filtering, or expose the three session sort modes (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/selectors.rs:265-347`). Generic fuzzy filtering is retained; it does not establish the richer session search contract.
entries.port: Add the session-specific corpus and parser, retaining explicit query modes and deterministic tie ordering. Decide how invalid regex errors are displayed, and document that recent ordering comes from the session loader rather than silently adding a conflicting sort.
entries.priority_reason: Finding a conversation by its text, directory or exact phrase matters once the session list grows.

entries.title: Session list hierarchy, scope/sort/name controls and path-aware rendering
entries.what: Presents saved sessions with a threaded family view, current-session marker, relative age and keyboard-controlled scope/search/display modes.
entries.mechanism:
The three-row header shows current/all-project scope, threaded/recent/Fuzzy ordering, named/all filtering, progress/status and action/query hints. Relative ages progress through now/minutes/hours/days/weeks/months/years. Home shortening is a simple prefix test. A canonical-path map attaches a session to an available parent, computes each subtree's newest modification and sorts roots/children by that value before flattening branch gutters. It has no cycle guard; a closed parent cycle with no root can disappear from the root traversal. Named filtering happens before tree construction and can promote a named child to a root when its parent is filtered out (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/session-selector.ts:31-274`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/session-selector.ts:350-400`).

Threaded hierarchy is used only for an empty query; other views are flat search results. Ten centered visible rows combine a sanitized name or first message with count, age and optional cwd/path metadata. The allocator keeps at least ten message columns, then clips the final row, which can sacrifice metadata on narrow widths. Current session, saved name, selection and pending deletion use distinct styles. Search edits preserve/clamp the numeric index rather than preserving the selected session's identity. Down on an empty list can create index -1, and later filtering can retain that negative index. Up/down and page steps of ten clamp; confirm checks the selected row (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/session-selector.ts:280-517`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/session-selector.ts:519-635`).

Scope, sort, named filter and path display have explicit keybindings. Most actions read the global manager while named filtering uses the supplied manager. Current-session deletion is rejected using canonical path identity. Tests independently exercise canonical parent aliases, newest-child ordering and active-session aliases (`ice:packages/coding-agent/test/session-selector-path-delete.test.ts:249-352`).
entries.interfaces: SortMode=threaded|recent|relevance; SessionScope=current|all; NameFilter=all|named; SessionSelectorComponent; private SessionList and SessionSelectorHeader. Current identity is a canonical file path.
entries.dependency_text: The session storage layer supplies SessionInfo and parent paths; this entry owns list organization, visual metadata and control state.
entries.rust: The native current-directory list uses display labels, byte-size/short-ID descriptions and ten SelectList items, with primary column bounds 56–72. It closes before sending SwitchSession and supports generic searching/cancel. It does not build a parent hierarchy or expose all-project/named/sort/path controls and TS current-session styling (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/selectors.rs:265-347`). Native session storage and hot-switch behavior remain separate preserved capabilities.
entries.port: Build the richer list over native metadata while retaining the existing asynchronous switch request. Use identity-preserving selection, cycle-safe hierarchy construction and explicit empty-list state; allocate metadata within the actual row budget.
entries.priority_reason: A flat current-directory list loses session families and makes large multi-project histories difficult to navigate.

entries.title: Session selector loading, scope caches, delete confirmation and rename lifetime
entries.what: Coordinates asynchronous current/all-project lists and in-picker delete/rename operations while preserving the displayed scope.
entries.mechanism:
Construction immediately loads current scope. Each scope has a nullable cache and loading flag; only all-scope requests have a sequence counter. Progress and visible success/error application check current scope and, for all, sequence. However success assigns caches and clears loading before checking stale sequence/scope, so an old all result can overwrite its cache while being kept off screen. Current loads have no generation token. Switching to a cached all list does not refresh it; an already running all request is not duplicated. Refresh reloads only the current scope. There is no abort/dispose generation for the component (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/session-selector.ts:642-776`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/session-selector.ts:879-986`).

Delete first enters a confirmation state that consumes every key except confirm/cancel. The noninvasive delete alias is enabled only for an empty query; query editing otherwise retains input behavior. Current-session canonical identity is protected. Confirm clears that state before firing an unawaited deletion callback. Successful trash/permanent deletion removes exact path matches from both caches, posts a two-second status and refreshes; failures post a three-second error. There is no busy flag against repeated operations or closed-view guard. Header status timers are cleared by select/cancel/onExit callbacks, but SessionList never invokes its onExit callback (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/session-selector.ts:519-635`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/session-selector.ts:778-820`).

Rename is offered only with a callback and outside loading. It replaces the list with a focused Input initialized to the existing name; a trimmed empty submission stays in the view. Submission awaits the callback and refresh, then restores the list in finally. It has no local catch, pending-submit lock or late-result ownership guard; Enter can start concurrent submissions. The callback's second parameter is the next name despite its currentName declaration label. Tests prove late all-scope completion cannot visibly switch back, all loading is not duplicated, query/delete alias separation, active-path safety and rename hint/input behavior; they do not establish stale-cache or disposal safety (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/session-selector.ts:822-877`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/session-selector-path-delete.test.ts:108-247`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/session-selector-rename.test.ts:1-112`).

The interactive caller uses SessionManager.list(cwd, sessionDir) for current scope and chooses default listAll or an explicit sessionDir for all scope. It closes before handleResumeSession, passes the current file path separately, and implements rename by opening the selected session and appending a nonempty trimmed session-info name. Its onExit callback requests shutdown, but the list has no corresponding dispatch (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:6858-6893`).
entries.interfaces: SessionsLoader(onProgress?)=>Promise<SessionInfo[]>; SessionSelectorComponent(currentSessionsLoader, allSessionsLoader, onSelect, onCancel, onExit, requestRender, options?, currentSessionFilePath?); options={renameSession?:(sessionPath, currentName)=>Promise<void>, showRenameHint?:boolean, keybindings?:KeybindingsManager}. Callback completion mutates selector state after await.
entries.dependency_text: Core listing/rename/delete storage operations remain session ownership. This entry owns loading/caches, interactive confirmation, operation feedback and component lifetime.
entries.rust: The native selector synchronously enumerates and summarizes current-directory files before opening the searchable list, then delegates selected-session switching to the async message loop. It has no dual-scope caches/progress callbacks, per-row deletion confirmation or rename input in that picker (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/selectors.rs:265-347`). This comparison credits native listing/switching and does not infer that underlying file operations are absent.
entries.port: Add asynchronous metadata loading and picker operations with per-request generation and component cancellation. Validate generation before all state/cache writes, serialize destructive submissions, handle errors locally and keep focus restoration tied to the owning view.
entries.priority_reason: Session selection and deletion need reliable scope, identity and late-result ownership while users continue interacting.

entries.title: Session tree topology, filtered ancestors, branch folding and selection preservation
entries.source: `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/tree-selector.ts:1-336`; `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/tree-selector.ts:338-661`; `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/tree-selector.ts:996-1153`; `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/tree-selector.test.ts:128-250`; `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/tree-selector.test.ts:328-701`. Line 337 is connector-redacted and is not claimed read.
entries.what: Turns the session DAG projection into a navigable visual tree with active-path priority, meaningful filters and foldable branch segments.
entries.mechanism:
The list flattens supplied SessionTreeNode roots using iterative traversal, prioritizes children/roots whose subtree contains the current leaf, records assistant tool-call metadata and marks the active ancestor path. Single-child chains stay flat; branch children and the first following generation indent, while multiple roots use a suppressed virtual-root connector. Initial selection targets the explicit ID or leaf, walks to the nearest visible ancestor, then falls back to the last visible row. Parent walks lack cycle detection and assume valid session topology (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/tree-selector.ts:96-327`).

Default hides label/custom/model-change/thinking-change/session-info bookkeeping; no-tools additionally hides tool results; user-only and labeled-only restrict by role or defined label; all enables those entry types. Before every mode, an assistant with no text and a normal stop/toolUse outcome is hidden unless it is the current leaf, so all is not literally every entry. Search AND-matches tokens against lowercased node text; the exact query-normalization expression at line 337 is unavailable. The visible corpus contains labels, role, the first 200 UTF-16 units of message text, shell command, custom type/text, branch summary, model/thinking/title metadata; compaction contributes its type label, not its summary. Folding excludes descendants by the full parent chain, then visual structure attaches remaining rows to their nearest visible ancestor (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/tree-selector.ts:338-615`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/tree-selector.ts:879-893`).

Filtering preserves the last valid selected ID even through empty results and otherwise walks to a visible ancestor. Up/down wrap; left/right or page keys move maxVisibleLines. Fold/up collapses a root or branch-segment start with visible children, otherwise walks upward to a segment start; unfold/down opens an existing fold or follows first-child segments toward the next branch/leaf. Nested folds survive parent unfold, but any query edit/filter change clears all folds. Escape first clears a nonempty query and folds, otherwise cancels. Text input rejects C0/DEL/C1 controls; backspace removes one UTF-16 unit, not a grapheme. Tests specify ancestor selection, empty-filter preservation, active/non-active branches, multiple roots, hidden intermediates and fold-reset rules (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/tree-selector.ts:996-1153`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/tree-selector.test.ts:128-250`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/tree-selector.test.ts:328-701`).
entries.interfaces: FilterMode=default|no-tools|user-only|labeled-only|all; TreeList.getSearchQuery, getSelectedNode, handleInput; app.tree.foldOrUp/unfoldOrDown/filter.default/filter.noTools/filter.userOnly/filter.labeledOnly/filter.all/filter.cycleBackward/filter.cycleForward; tui.select.* and tui.editor.cursorLeft/cursorRight/deleteCharBackward.
entries.dependency_text: SESSION-026 owns durable navigation and branch-summary effects; this entry owns the supplied tree's filtered topology and cursor/fold state.
entries.rust: The native tree selector loads oldest-first entries, labels them by type/sequence with a current marker and short ID, and uses a 12-item searchable list over type/sequence/ID. It sends NavigateTree for the selected durable ID. It has no hierarchy, active-ancestor path, branch folding, nearest-visible-ancestor selection or TS filter modes. An independent scoped crates search found no corresponding fold/label-filter controller (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/selectors.rs:372-447`).
entries.port: Build a topology-aware native tree component over the session view while retaining the existing entry-ID navigation route. Preserve empty-filter identity and hidden-ancestor folding, add cycle guards, and resolve the redacted query expression before promising byte-for-byte search parity.
entries.priority_reason: Branch structure and stable selection are central to safely choosing a point in a non-linear conversation.

entries.title: Tree row viewport, entry formatting, full copy and inline labels
entries.what: Keeps deep tree content readable, shows meaningful message/tool summaries and lets users copy complete text or label a selected entry.
entries.mechanism:
Rows use a fixed two-cell cursor gutter, three-cell indentation steps, connectors/fold symbols, active-path bullet, optional warning-colored label and local-time label timestamp. Selection bolds content and applies selectedBg to both gutter and body. A shared horizontal offset is calculated from the selected row's content anchor, a bounded 4–20-cell anchor budget and 2–12-cell left context budget; every visible row uses that offset while retaining its cursor gutter. ANSI-aware slicing adds a reset and clips the final width. The list centers at most max(5, floor(terminalHeight/2)) entries, then shows position/filter state. Help groups semantic action chunks and wraps them instead of simply truncating key hints (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/tree-selector.ts:62-92`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/tree-selector.ts:664-765`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/tree-selector.ts:1177-1268`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/tree-selector.ts:1349-1389`).

Message previews concatenate text blocks and truncate to 200 UTF-16 units before normalizing newline/tab; assistant emptiness distinguishes aborted/error/no-content. Tool results resolve stored assistant call metadata and format read ranges, write/edit paths, bash command (50 units), grep/find/ls or 40-unit JSON custom arguments. Custom messages, compactions, branch summaries and bookkeeping have separate labels; unknown entry types render blank. Path shortening is a home-prefix test. Labels are not control-normalized. Label times show HH:mm today, month/day this year or two-digit year/month/day otherwise. Copy deliberately uses full text rather than the preview: message text/error, shell command, custom text or summary; blank/unsupported returns undefined (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/tree-selector.ts:768-994`).

Label editing swaps the tree body for a focused Input, trims submission and uses undefined to remove a label. It mutates the supplied node and timestamp before synchronously invoking the persistence callback, then restores the list. A throwing callback can leave the edit view after local mutation; no rollback is present. updateNodeLabel does not reapply active filtering, so a removed label can remain in labeled-only until another filter pass. The host appends label changes and uses copyToClipboard with explicit empty/error/status feedback. Tests assert narrow help, full long-message copy and timestamp toggling (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/tree-selector.ts:632-640`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/tree-selector.ts:1270-1426`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:6835-6853`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/tree-selector.test.ts:252-326`).
entries.interfaces: TreeSelectorComponent(tree, currentLeafId, terminalHeight, onSelect, onCancel, onLabelChange?, initialSelectedId?, initialFilterMode?); onCopy(text|undefined), focused, getTreeList; app.message.copy, app.tree.editLabel, app.tree.toggleLabelTimestamp. Labels persist through the supplied callback, not directly in the widget.
entries.dependency_text: Generic text width/wrapping and Input behavior remain terminal-fragment contracts; session storage owns durable label events. This entry owns the tree-specific viewport, formatting and UI handoff.
entries.rust: The native picker exposes type/sequence/current and a 12-byte ID prefix, using a generic searchable SelectList. It has no message/tool preview formatting, shared horizontal tree viewport, selected-entry copy callback or label editor/timestamp toggle. Its error and empty-session feedback are implemented (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/selectors.rs:381-447`). Native transcript copy and session metadata APIs are separate and are not treated as absent.
entries.port: Add tree row formatting and bounded horizontal panning, preserving full text for explicit copy. entries.priority_reason: Deep branches need readable content and labels, and copy must not silently return a truncated preview.

entries.title: Tree navigation chooser, optional summary cancellation and editor preservation
entries.what: Coordinates selection of a historical point with optional branch summarization, cancellation, transcript rebuild and safe editor restoration.
entries.mechanism:
The host obtains the current tree/leaf and configured filter, rejects an empty tree and treats selecting the current leaf as a no-op status. It closes the tree before optionally asking No summary/Summarize/Custom instructions; canceling that chooser reopens the same tree selection, while canceling custom instructions loops back to the choice. The configured skip-summary setting bypasses the chooser. If streaming, it restores pending messages into the editor and awaits session abort before navigation (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:6712-6782`).

For summary requests, the host temporarily replaces Escape with abortBranchSummary, installs a branch-summary status indicator and passes summarize/customInstructions to navigateTree. An aborted summary reopens the tree at the chosen entry; a canceled navigation posts status without rebuilding. Success clears/rebuilds chat, fills result.editorText only when nonempty and the current editor is still whitespace-empty, posts status and asynchronously flushes the compaction queue. Errors are displayed, and finally always clears the summary indicator if installed and restores the earlier Escape callback (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:6783-6829`).

The empty-editor check protects a later draft in this path, unlike the fork picker's unconditional returned-text assignment. Durable navigation, summary generation and cancellation semantics are supplied by SESSION-026; this contract is the interactive coordinator.
entries.interfaces: showTreeSelector(initialSelectedId?); session.navigateTree(entryId,{summarize, customInstructions}); result.aborted/cancelled/editorText; defaultEditor.onEscape override; branchSummary status indicator; configured treeFilterMode and skip-summary choice.
entries.dependency_text: SESSION-026 owns actual branch navigation/summary; SESSION-020 supplies queued editor delivery. The TUI owns chooser state, input restoration and visible completion behavior.
entries.rust: The native selector sends NavigateTree and closes. The message loop calls lane.navigate_tree(Some(entry_id), false, None, None), so it always requests no summary and has no custom instructions or summary-cancel interaction. It rebuilds history on Completed, prints the structured failure message on Failed, uses a generic note for other outcomes and redraws. It does not check current leaf as a UI no-op, expose the summary chooser, restore pending editor input before abort, or use a returned editorText field (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/selectors.rs:420-447`, `rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui.rs:2962-2995`). The native navigation implementation is compared separately under SESSION-026.
entries.port: Extend the native navigation message to carry summary choice/instructions and own cancellation/status lifetime. Retain structured native errors and transcript rebuild, protect drafts against asynchronous completion and restore input bindings on every exit path.
entries.priority_reason: Changing conversation history must make summary/cancellation choices visible and preserve input entered while navigation is pending.

entries.title: Resource config picker grouping, scope switching and inherited-state display
entries.what: Shows package and loose-file resources in a searchable global/project configuration picker with clear inherited and overridden states.
entries.mechanism:
Users can inspect extensions, skills, prompts and themes by their source package or directory. Global mode toggles a resource on or off; project mode shows whether it inherits the global choice or explicitly loads/unloads it.

Groups are keyed by origin, scope, source and baseDir, with package groups before top-level groups, user before project and source/name locale sorting. Subgroups have fixed extensions/skills/prompts/themes order. Extension names include their parent folder unless already under extensions; SKILL.md displays its parent name. Search is one lowercase substring over displayName, resource type or full path, retaining only matching items and their headers. Every search/mode rebuild selects the first item. Up/down skip headers and clamp; page movement uses visible row count, also skipping headers (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/config-selector.ts:26-179`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/config-selector.ts:255-394`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/config-selector.ts:460-520`).

The viewport is max(5,(terminalHeight or 24)-8), despite additional search/scroll rows outside that nominal eight-row chrome budget. Global enabled state uses [x]/[ ]; project overrides use [+]/[-], and inherited global resources are dimmed with a suffix. Header reports the settings path and available scope toggle. Item/header rows clip to width, while no-resources and scroll-indicator rows are not explicitly clipped. Enter/space toggles the selected permitted item; Tab requests scope change; configured cancel closes; literal Ctrl+C invokes exit. entries.title: Resource enable filters and project inherit/load/unload mutation semantics
entries.what: Writes targeted resource selection patterns while keeping global package choices and project overrides distinct.
entries.mechanism:
The picker saves resource choices directly through SettingsManager. Project changes cycle among inheritance, forced loading and forced unloading, using the inherited enabled state to choose the next step.

Global top-level toggles derive a path relative to the source base directory, remove exact existing bare/!/+/− targets and append +pattern or -pattern to the relevant resource array. Package toggles find the exact source string, convert string entries to objects and update a package-relative resource array. A missing package index returns without writing, but toggleResource still returns the optimistic new enabled state, so the view can change without a matching persisted package. Setter errors propagate without local recovery. The view updates only the current scope's item collection (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/config-selector.ts:382-394`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/config-selector.ts:522-643`).

For project top-level overrides, equivalent target forms include scope-relative, absolute, base-relative and metadata-base-relative paths. Signed matching entries are removed; inherited global files gain a bare absolute inclusion plus a signed override, and returning to inherit removes that injected absolute target. Package source matching first accepts exact strings, otherwise compares locally resolved paths across their scope bases; it does not canonicalize package source aliases. New project overrides use {source, autoload:false}, converting local sources to a project-relative spelling. Their selected type filter is replaced with +/−package-relative-path; returning to inherit removes that filter and deletes an empty autoload:false package override, otherwise collapses an empty filter object to its source string (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/config-selector.ts:671-735`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/config-selector.ts:791-869`).

Inherited enabled defaults come from a constructor-time resourceType+canonicalPath map, falling back to user item.enabled or true for project-origin resources. For inherited-enabled resources the cycle is inherit→unload→load→inherit; disabled inheritance uses inherit→load→unload→inherit. Exact matching filter entries are last-wins; ! and - mean unload, bare/+ mean load. Empty package arrays mean unload only when autoload is not false. The inherited map is not refreshed after global toggles, so changing global mode then switching to project mode in the same picker can use stale inherited state. The source-read test specifies an inherited package's -filter→+filter→removed override sequence (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/config-selector.ts:287-296`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/config-selector.ts:737-789`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/package-command-paths.test.ts:430-459`).

Exact signed target rewrite semantics live in the picker; package-manager resolution of those patterns remains CLI ownership.
