entries.title: Embedded portrait Easter eggs, animation timing and cleanup
entries.what: Displays two embedded decorative portraits using terminal block graphics, with a command-triggered random reveal and a model-specific scanline tribute.
entries.mechanism:
The Armin command adds a monochrome animated portrait, while selecting the matching OpenCode Kimi model adds the color Daxnuts portrait. Both request redraws as their reveal progresses and expose dispose to stop their timer.

Armin decodes a fixed 31×36 LSB-first XBM bitmap (zero is foreground) into 31×18 half-block cells. It randomly chooses typewriter/scanline/rain/fade/crt/glitch/dissolve, runs at 30 fps except glitch 60, and caches width+gridVersion. Typewriter reveals three cells/frame; scanline one row/frame; shuffled fade 15 and dissolve 20 cells/frame; CRT expands from the middle; glitch corrupts eight frames then restores the image. Rain tracks drops per column and settles onto nonspace cells. Static analysis of the read 144-byte bitmap finds columns 0 and 30 entirely background; those columns never settle in tickRain, leaving its completion condition false until disposal. This is a source/data derivation, not an executed animation test (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/armin.ts:8-57`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/armin.ts:116-380`).

Armin clips image rows to width-minus-one then adds one leading space, but its ARMIN SAYS HI footer is not clipped; nonpositive widths are not robustly bounded. Daxnuts decodes a fixed 32×32 RGB hex asset into 32×16 half blocks with foreground=bottom/background=top pixels. An 80 ms timer stops after 25 ticks, revealing rows progressively and adding text after 60% progress. Its center helper strips SGR then uses string length, and it does not clip fixed-width artwork or the displayed URL on narrow terminals. Both cache rendered rows and clear their interval on dispose. The Daxnuts trigger requires provider exactly opencode and a lowercased model ID containing kimi-k2.5; there is no once-per-session latch. Its displayed Try OpenCode URL is the source's mistral.ai news URL, not an inferred corrected destination (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/armin.ts:60-109`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/daxnuts.ts:10-163`, `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:8110-8125`).
entries.interfaces: ArminComponent(ui), DaxnutsComponent(ui):render, invalidate, dispose; /arminsayshi; OpenCode provider/model selection trigger. Assets are embedded literals; no runtime network fetch is required.
entries.dependency_text: The host must dispose removed components for timer ownership. These are decorative components, independent of native terminal image-protocol support.
entries.rust: A scoped native source search found no Armin/Daxnuts component, trigger or matching first-run artwork. The nearest built-in decorative host behavior is a static welcome banner using native DynamicBorder/Text (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/extras.rs:35-65`). Native image and animation primitives are retained under terminal entries; these two specific bundled components are absent.
entries.port: If retained, implement the embedded assets as optional native components with bounded rendering and explicit animation lifetime. Fix rain completion for blank columns and clip both art and text to the viewport; retain exact source assets/labels only if product policy still wants them.
entries.priority_reason: These are low-priority decorative behaviors, but exhaustive parity accounting must record them and their source lifetime defect.

entries.title: Startup changelog baselines, collapsed notices and explicit history display
entries.what: Show new release notes once for an eligible fresh session, remember the display baseline, and expose the full local changelog on request.
entries.mechanism:
Startup computes release notes before mounting the interactive interface. Resumed sessions with messages skip this calculation, while a first recorded installation establishes the current version without showing historical entries. With an existing baseline, only parsed entries newer than that baseline are joined after line-ending normalization; a nonempty result advances the stored version and triggers the optional install report. An empty result leaves the baseline unchanged (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:1386-1411`).

The one-shot startup-notice flag is set before the empty-content check. The notice gets a spacer when needed and dynamic borders; expanded mode shows a What's New heading and Markdown, while collapsed mode extracts the first three-part version with a regular expression, falls back to the application version, and offers /changelog. The settings and extension rebind sequence calls this after resource diagnostics, before initial history is rendered (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:923-951; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:2269-2341`).

The explicit /changelog command parses all local entries, reverses their parsed order, normalizes each section, joins them, and shows a fallback when there are none. It renders a bordered heading and Markdown with horizontal and vertical padding one, then requests render. It does not accept a special all argument in this handler (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:7842-7861`).

Install reporting is skipped for any truthy ICE_OFFLINE value or disabled telemetry. Otherwise it starts a best-effort fetch to https://ice.dev/api/report-install?version=<encoded version>, with the application User-Agent and a 5,000 ms AbortSignal timeout; rejection and non-success response have no UI effect. This is the source's request construction, not evidence of any server behavior (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:1413-1430`).

entries.title: Extension selector, input and multiline editor presentation contracts
entries.what: Present extension-owned choices and text prompts with focus, cancellation, optional countdowns and external editing.
entries.mechanism:
A selector displays every option in a nonshrinking list and starts at the first index. It can also show a separately scrollable Markdown content pane, while an input dialog forwards focus to its single-line input. Both selector and input install a countdown only when timeout is truthy, positive and accompanied by a TUI; expiration invokes cancellation, title text shows remaining seconds, and dispose clears the countdown (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/extension-selector.ts:12-129`; `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/extension-input.ts:11-90`).

Selector input first consumes the tools-expand action, calling the optional expansion callback. Page actions scroll the content pane by at least one row and otherwise viewport height minus two. Configured selection arrows or literal k/j clamp without wrapping; confirm or LF chooses only a truthy option, so an empty string is not selectable. Cancel invokes the caller. The selector allocates all option rows rather than imposing a ten-item menu window. The input widget ignores its _placeholder parameter, applies any provided initialValue including an empty string, accepts confirm or LF with the raw value including empty, and otherwise delegates input editing.

The multiline dialog embeds the shared editor with the editor theme/options, forwards focus, applies only a truthy prefill, and shows effective confirm/newline/cancel/external-editor hints. Cancel precedes the external-editor action. The external command comes from an explicit truthy option, then VISUAL, EDITOR, and finally notepad on Windows or nano elsewhere. It passes the editor's ordinary text to the external helper, stops the TUI before entering the try block, replaces text only for a completed edit, and always restarts and forces render from finally. The widget does not add its own timeout, signal or error catch around that edit (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/components/extension-editor.ts:12-133`).

The host facade owns the Promise, AbortSignal, resolution and editor-slot lifetime; widget disposal alone is not that cancellation protocol. These presentation differences therefore supplement EXT-040 rather than counting its bridge again. The complete widget bodies and documented Component/Focusable contracts were read; no interactive dialog was opened.
entries.dependency_text: EXT-040 owns extension request/response semantics and cleanup; TUI owns these three concrete widgets. MISC-024 may consume this presentation contract without a second widget estimate.
entries.rust: The native extension host has functioning input, choice and editor dialogs, plus the UiDialog mailbox and ask-user bridge. Input uses a real placeholder, selectors use SelectList with ten visible rows, and results retain structured values/kinds rather than only TS strings (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/extensions.rs:77-495; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/extensions.rs:529-939`; accepted EXT-040 source review). Native presentation has no corresponding TS content pane/countdown/timeout and scalar return contract. Preserve actual input placeholders, structured permission metadata, live mailbox lifecycle and native multiline editing; do not infer a missing dialog system from the component names.
entries.port: Add a small presentation adapter over the native dialog host for content scrolling, configured key hints, timed cancellation and source-compatible prefill/selection rules. Keep structured native results at the bridge boundary and decide whether empty-string selection and ignored-placeholder behavior should be intentionally improved. Ensure terminal restart and disposal remain guaranteed when external editing fails.

entries.title: Prompt admission, compaction queues, follow-up and send-now ownership
entries.what: Route user drafts to the correct local command, active run or pending queue and restore queued work predictably across interruptions and compaction.
entries.mechanism:
Submission trims the draft and routes built-in commands before normal prompts. Child-view routing and direct Bash routing also precede compaction and streaming admission, so those inputs do not automatically become model steering. A controlled child receives non-slash input through its bridge; a read-only child warns and clears it. Direct ! or !! Bash rejects an overlapping user shell before clearing the draft, while extension commands can execute immediately during compaction (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:3784-4029`).

Compacting normal input is stored in a local array with steer or followUp mode, added to editor history, cleared and shown in the pending display. Streaming ordinary submission calls session.prompt with steer; the follow-up action uses expanded text and followUp while streaming, but forwards to the normal submit callback when idle. Idle ordinary input is delivered to a waiting input callback or appended to pendingUserInputs, then added to history. Background-shell/watch subscriptions repaint footer counts only when counts change and are disposed together with the session event subscription (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:4030-4063; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:5160-5189; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:5856-5862`).

Send-now joins all steering messages, all follow-up messages and the new expanded draft with blank lines. During a live run it first releases background shells and blocking child waits, yields through setImmediate, clears both runtime and local compaction queues, clears the editor and repaints pending work, awaits abort, then submits the combined text. Idle, compacting and extension-command cases use the ordinary submit path instead. The read test asserts this release/yield/clear/abort/submit order (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:5197-5219`; `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/interactive-mode-send-now.test.ts:1-72`).

Dequeue merges runtime queue items before matching local compaction items, clears both stores, and restores steering followed by follow-up and any current ordinary editor text. Empty restore still clears pending display and can abort; nonempty restore returns the number of queue items. The display lists separate truncated Steering and Follow-up rows and an effective dequeue hint. The local queue has no explicit length cap (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:5801-5862`).

Compaction flush snapshots and clears its local queue. With willRetry it enqueues each non-command by its original mode; otherwise leading extension commands run first, the first ordinary message starts a prompt, and remaining messages are queued by mode. Both synchronous failure and rejection of that first prompt clear the runtime queue and restore the entire original local snapshot with an error notice. This is a source-level recovery policy, not evidence that partial earlier side effects are rolled back (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:5874-5952`).

The shared built-in display catalog BUILTIN_SLASH_COMMANDS declares 29 command names: fast, settings, customize, model, scoped-models, export, import, share, copy, name, session, context, changelog, hotkeys, notices, tasks, shells, resources, fork, clone, tree, trust, login, logout, new, compact, resume, reload, quit. It is a ReadonlyArray<BuiltinSlashCommand>. Argument hints are [on|off|status] for fast, <provider/model> for model and <provider> for login; the other records omit argumentHint. The tasks description refers to the shells view first and Agent Hub when no shell is active, and quit interpolates APP_NAME. This catalog supplies names/descriptions; runtime admission and command execution remain the explicit host branches described above (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/slash-commands.ts:14-56`).
entries.dependency_text: Runtime owners retain queue/process/session semantics. This estimate covers TUI admission, draft lifetime, compaction-local storage and ordering around those APIs.
entries.rust: Native submit routes slash commands and user Bash before prompts, and busy steering/follow-up/dequeue use separately spawned lane operations while the main loop can await a run (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui.rs:1398-1497`; `rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui.rs:2617-2695`). The generic editor expands and history-stores submitted text, clears undo/redo, invokes on_submit and then clears the draft (`rust:crates/ice-tui/src/editor.rs:1186-1204`). Busy steering failure restores images and reports the error but does not restore text into the editor or queue; the internal Editor history retains the submission (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui.rs:1425-1460`). Follow-up explicitly clears the draft before the status/reservation check; its busy failure likewise restores only images, and this branch does not add the text to history (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui.rs:2655-2692`). In the idle follow-up branch a failed try_start_working reservation leaves the cleared draft unsubmitted, and UserInput send failure is ignored; ordinary submit at least resets Idle after its channel-send failure (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui.rs:2661-2672`; `rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui.rs:1487-1495`). Normal bare Up/Down is intercepted by the host and reads a separate TuiState history, so the internal Editor record does not prove ordinary recall restores a failed busy submission (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui.rs:2600-2613`; `rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/state.rs:833-864`). Follow-up bypasses generic submit/history entirely. These are exact source-visible recovery differences. Separately, native dequeue correctly materializes expanded draft text before replacement, restores images and places the caret at the UTF-8 end; preserve that behavior (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/events.rs:15-148`). No equivalent send-now release-and-recombine action or TS compaction-local queue contract appears in the full native host.
entries.port: Keep native image-aware queue restoration and concurrent lane access. Add explicit draft/queue ownership for each admission branch and a send-now transaction that detaches background work, snapshots queues, aborts and submits in the intended order. Define recovery for partially admitted work so a failed queue operation does not silently discard text or duplicate previously delivered commands.
entries.priority_reason: Incorrect admission or recovery can lose a user's draft, reorder work or send a command to the wrong run.

entries.title: Session rebind and reload presentation ordering
entries.source: `ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:2269-2407; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:2770-2818; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:7445-7539`; resource and extension lifecycle owners `EXT-020` and `SESSION-021`.
entries.what: Keep editor focus, resource diagnostics, completion and visible messages aligned when a session or extension generation changes.
entries.mechanism:
Rebinding captures the current runtime session before awaiting extension setup. It replaces subscriptions and can render and subscribe before extension binding, then checks that the captured session is still current before applying later work. Autocomplete is installed before slow extension initialization and rebuilt after registration; the UI context supplies session actions, queue-restoring abort and shutdown scheduling (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:2269-2407`).

Runtime settings apply the HTTP dispatcher, scrollbar, provider/cwd footer data, thinking and output padding, hardware cursor, shrink policy and editor padding/completion limits. Current and custom editors receive the relevant settings; status and title are refreshed as the bound session becomes ready. Extension errors and resource diagnostics flow to their existing notice owners rather than becoming an independent modal subsystem.

/reload rejects while streaming or compacting. It resets extension UI, replaces the editor with a loading view, moves focus and forces a render, then yields a tick. A guarded beforeSessionStart callback refreshes thinking/output settings and rebuilds history before extension startup notifications; after reload it ensures that callback ran, reloads keybindings, reapplies themes/runtime appearance and autocomplete/shortcuts/resources, handles implicit trust persistence and model diagnostics, and restores the current editor. This entry covers host ordering and stale-session guards only. Discovery, extension generation invalidation, session replacement and settings persistence remain with their respective owners; no reload or extension code was executed during this audit.

entries.title: Signal, crash, suspend and normal shutdown sequencing
entries.what: Restore terminal state and dispose the runtime in the intended order for ordinary exits, operating-system signals, terminal loss and suspension.
entries.mechanism:
The clear action first clears a draft and a second invocation strictly within 500 ms requests shutdown. The empty-editor exit action also requests shutdown, while the shutdown flag prevents reentry. Normal interactive shutdown clears compaction status and console capture, disables automatic theme synchronization, drains terminal input for up to the requested 1,000 ms, stops the TUI, then disposes the runtime and prints an eligible resume command before exit zero (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:4871-5072`).

Signal shutdown reverses the critical runtime/terminal order: it disposes the runtime before disabling theme synchronization, draining and stopping the terminal, and does not print the interactive resume hint. SIGTERM and non-Windows SIGHUP handlers are prepended, kill tracked detached children and start this path; handlers remain registered until terminal stop. Neither ordinary path wraps every awaited cleanup in a timeout/finally, so disposal or drain failure can prevent later steps. The dedicated regression source asserts extension cleanup before terminal restoration for a signal-triggered exit (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:4871-5159`; `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/suite/regressions/5080-signal-shutdown-extension-cleanup.test.ts:1-186`).

Terminal stream EIO, EPIPE and ENOTCONN errors take an emergency path that unregisters handlers, kills tracked detached processes and exits 129 without normal cleanup. Other terminal errors are thrown. The prepended uncaught-exception handler exits one immediately if already shutting down, otherwise unregisters signals, kills children and stops the UI independently on a best-effort basis, prints the error and exits one. These paths deliberately have different cleanup guarantees.

Suspend on Windows only reports that it is unsupported. On other platforms a long keepalive interval prevents natural process exit, a temporary SIGINT listener absorbs interruption, and one SIGCONT callback clears those resources, restarts and forces redraw; the UI stops before sending SIGTSTP to the process group. A synchronous stop/kill failure clears the interval and SIGINT listener and rethrows, without the same restart cleanup as SIGCONT (`ice:packages/coding-agent/test/interactive-mode-suspend.test.ts:1-150`).

Resume formatting requires a TTY stdout, persisted session and an existing session file. It emits the application name, a custom session-directory argument when applicable and the session ID; simple shell-safe characters remain literal and other values use single-quote escaping. It does not generate a hint for an in-memory or missing file. The formatter tests were read in full, together with the source-only SIGTERM regression credited by the tools owner; no signals were sent.
entries.interfaces: app.clear/app.exit/app.suspend; SIGTERM/SIGHUP/SIGCONT/SIGTSTP/SIGINT; uncaughtException; stdout/stderr error listeners; drainInput(1000); runtimeHost.dispose; formatResumeCommand; exits 0/1/129 in the TS paths.
entries.dependency_text: Terminal protocol teardown belongs to TUI-209/216; session and extension disposal belongs to runtime owners. This entry estimates product-host ordering, signal ownership and resume presentation.
entries.rust: Native clear/exit distinguishes fresh key presses from repeats, preserves clear-versus-double-exit semantics, and uses emergency_exit for a busy run. Its emergency status is 130, while normal shutdown closes the ask-user bridge, sets running false, aborts and awaits update tasks, joins the key worker before restoring the terminal, aborts remaining tasks, clears the reload mailbox and prints a resume hint (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui.rs:2077-2239; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui.rs:3352-3393`). Native Unix suspend and terminal restoration are already implemented in state and terminal helpers. Preserve repeat filtering and orderly task joins. A 50 ms key-worker poll does not bound a join when a synchronous handler is blocked, and the complete native sequence is not the TS signal-specific runtime-first path.
entries.port: Use a shared idempotent shutdown coordinator with an explicit cause, preserving native task cleanup and choosing the required runtime/terminal order for each cause. Keep emergency terminal-loss handling separate from ordinary disposal, guarantee restoration after cleanup failures where possible, and retain correct persisted-session resume quoting.
entries.priority_reason: Shutdown order controls extension cleanup, terminal usability and whether queued work or input leaks during process exit.

entries.title: Bounded tmux keyboard-configuration startup diagnostics
entries.what: Warn about two tmux configurations that prevent the intended extended-key behavior without blocking startup indefinitely.
entries.mechanism:
The startup check runs only when TMUX is truthy. It asks tmux for extended-keys and extended-keys-format concurrently, and each child query has its own two-second timer. The child uses ignored stdin/stderr and piped stdout; a timeout kills it and resolves undefined, an error also resolves undefined, and only a zero exit returns trimmed stdout (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:1332-1384`).

If extended-keys cannot be read, no warning is shown. A value other than on or always warns that extended-keys should be enabled in ~/.tmux.conf. When that value is acceptable but extended-keys-format equals xterm, a separate warning recommends csi-u; other values do not generate this warning. The result is a diagnostic, not a configuration mutation or terminal capability guarantee. Stdout accumulation has no explicit byte cap, although elapsed process lifetime is bounded by the timer.

The documentation supplies manual setup guidance and examples. External terminal versions or actual tmux availability were not tested; this audit read the implementation and docs only. Underlying keyboard negotiation and fallback behavior remain separate terminal contracts.
entries.interfaces: TMUX; subprocess tmux show -gv extended-keys / extended-keys-format; 2,000 ms timeout per query; diagnostic reference ~/.tmux.conf; warning presentation.
entries.dependency_text: TUI-208 owns negotiation and key decoding. This entry covers only the optional startup diagnostic and its child-process lifetime.
entries.rust: The fully read native startup/controller scopes initialize session, UI and background tasks without an equivalent tmux configuration diagnostic (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/run.rs:1-121`; `rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui.rs:802-959`; `rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui.rs:1499-1656`). Recorded negative searches for tmux, extended-keys and extended-keys-format in that controller/helper scope found no matching route. Native terminal negotiation and fallback input already exist under TUI-208; this missing diagnostic does not mean tmux or extended input is unsupported.
entries.port: Add a best-effort startup probe using asynchronous child processes, independent deadlines and a small output cap. Report the specific configuration mismatch without assuming a missing result means a broken terminal, and leave terminal negotiation authoritative.
entries.priority_reason: The diagnostic helps users understand ambiguous key behavior while remaining optional startup assistance.

entries.title: Session sharing host, gh lifecycle and viewer-link construction
entries.what: Export a session for sharing, show cancellable upload progress and report both the hosted viewer and gist links.
entries.mechanism:
The share command first checks gh authentication synchronously and exports the session to a fixed session.html in the operating-system temporary directory. A failed authentication status displays a login instruction, while a thrown check displays an installation instruction. The check has no explicit timeout, and the fixed export path is not made unique or exclusive (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:7630-7652`).

After export succeeds, a bordered loader replaces the editor. The host spawns gh gist create --public=false <temporary file>, collects stdout/stderr and waits for close. Cancelling aborts the loader, kills the child, restores the editor, attempts to unlink the file and reports cancellation. Completion ignores a result after cancellation; otherwise it restores the editor and cleans up before displaying either the trimmed stderr/unknown-error message or the links. Export failure occurs before this loader cleanup and can leave a partial temporary file (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:7653-7722`).

The asynchronous child has no error listener, timeout or output-size cap in this host, and the initial spawnSync authentication call is also unbounded. A successful close takes the last slash-separated stdout segment as a gist ID and checks only that it is nonempty. The viewer base is truthy ICE_SHARE_VIEWER_URL or https://pi.dev/session/, then # and the ID are appended without URL validation or escaping; both the viewer URL and raw gist URL are displayed. The command does not itself open a browser or copy a link (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/config.ts:538-541`).

These are the source's local commands and constructed links. No export, gh process, authentication, upload or network call was executed during the audit. The HTML document and custom-renderer export bridge belong to MISC-017–020.
entries.interfaces: /share; gh auth status; gh gist create --public=false; os.tmpdir()/session.html; BorderedLoader cancellation; ICE_SHARE_VIEWER_URL; default https://pi.dev/session/#<gistId>; stdout/stderr and close event.
entries.dependency_text: MISC owns export serialization/viewer behavior; this entry owns command orchestration, progress, temporary-file lifetime and link presentation.
entries.rust: Native /share is real: it obtains chronological entries from the main view, builds text-only User/Assistant Markdown, pipes it into gh gist create --filename session.md -, and reports stdout on success (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/sessions.rs:8-86`). It falls back to copying the transcript, then suggests /export if clipboard access fails. Preserve that useful fallback. The native path omits the TS HTML/viewer contract, authentication precheck, explicit visibility argument and cancellable loader; it uses blocking std::process calls and wait_with_output inside an awaited main-loop branch with no timeout (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui.rs:3038-3040`). No assumption about gh's default privacy setting or actual service response is made.
entries.port: Reuse the native command and fallback while selecting the intended HTML/viewer output. Move upload work off the interactive command loop, handle spawn failure/timeout/cancellation, cap output and use a unique temporary file with guaranteed cleanup. Validate the returned identifier before building links. These lifecycle improvements should not copy the TS process and temporary-file weaknesses.
entries.priority_reason: Sharing already exists natively, but the output contract and cancellation/error handling differ materially.

entries.title: Live main-screen and fullscreen renderer replacement
entries.what: Switch renderer modes while preserving the component tree, active focus and a stable TUI reference used by extensions and components.
entries.mechanism:
The renderer factory chooses a main-screen or alternate-screen implementation and enables application tool-toggle links only for fullscreen. Fullscreen uses three-line wheel scrolling and routes internal action URLs through the host, falling back to the browser helper when the action is not handled. A proxy gives components a stable reference while resolving the active renderer anew for property reads, writes, prototype checks and even previously extracted method calls (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:424-462`).

Switching to the current mode succeeds without work; switching with overlay entries returns false. Otherwise the host captures children, focus, terminal, cursor/shrink policies and debug callback, plus the main-screen render state when leaving that mode. It stops the old renderer with preserveScreen, clears its focus/children/layout root, creates the replacement on the same terminal, restores main-screen state when available, remounts children, invalidates and restores focus. Starting the replacement rebinds theme detection and extension terminal-input listeners, and optionally reasserts terminal progress for a running or compacting session (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:953-1019`).

The shared component tree includes a follow-end transcript scroll view, sticky prompt and a dock with pending messages, status, widgets, new-message pill, editor, child switcher and footer. Fullscreen gets a constrained layout root; regular mode retains the ordinary children. On final fullscreen stop the host dismisses overlays, switches to regular without restarting or restoring progress, renders the transcript there, and then stops the UI. This preserves a readable main-screen transcript rather than abandoning the alternate screen's content.

The source-read interactive-tui tests cover factory modes, stable-reference behavior, screen transition and transcript-preserving shutdown. They also distinguish fullscreen flash confirmation from ordinary transcript status. No renderer was started during this audit.
entries.interfaces: createInteractiveTui; createInteractiveTuiReference Proxy; switchUiMode(mode, restoreProgress, startRenderer); mountInteractiveTui; stopInteractiveTui; UiMode regular/fullscreen; shared terminal, component focus and main-screen capture/restore.

entries.rust: Native regular/fullscreen behavior is selected from args.tui_mode and configures the existing TUI, viewport/layout and plugin-panel regular-mode state during startup (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui.rs:990-1000; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui.rs:1300-1350; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui.rs:1571-1571`; terminal implementations in TUI-221/222). Both screen families are native capabilities. The fully read host has no equivalent live switch that remounts the same tree through a stable reference and refuses active overlays; native set_main_screen_mode alone does not establish that full lifecycle.
entries.port: Build a host transition operation around the existing native renderers, preserving focus, terminal ownership, transcript state and extension listeners. Reject or explicitly resolve live overlays, and make component references survive the renderer change through an adapter rather than invalidating callers.
entries.priority_reason: Runtime settings or extensions must not leave components bound to a stopped renderer or lose focus during a mode change.

entries.title: Clipboard image/text admission and latest-assistant copy feedback
entries.what: Paste clipboard content into the active editor and copy the latest assistant reply with mode-appropriate feedback.
entries.mechanism:
Clipboard paste tries an image before plain text. An image is written to a randomly named ice-clipboard-<UUID>.<extension> file in the system temporary directory, using png when MIME-to-extension lookup has no result. The host optionally inserts that path at the active editor's cursor, requests render and returns; it does not attach image bytes directly to the prompt or schedule cleanup of the file (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:3748-3782`).

When there is no image, nonempty clipboard text goes through editor.pasteText when available, otherwise optional insertTextAtCursor. Any read, write or editor error is silently caught. An image read or temporary-write exception therefore prevents the later text fallback for that invocation. The default editor's image-paste callback delegates to this host, which uses the currently active editor rather than hardcoding the default editor.

/copy retrieves the session's latest assistant text and reports an error if none is truthy. It awaits the clipboard helper and shows a normal status on success, except the configured app.message.copy action asks for flashConfirmation and an active fullscreen renderer flashes Copied! instead. Errors are displayed with their message/string conversion. The stable renderer proxy participates in the instanceof check, so copy feedback follows the current renderer after a mode switch (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:7724-7741`; `ice:packages/coding-agent/test/interactive-tui.test.ts:132-243`).

Preserve those file and remote-session behaviors; they differ from the TS image-first temporary-path insertion policy. Native /copy and the copy hotkey call copy_last_assistant on state.last_assistant_text; it reports an empty cache, copies when possible, and on failure shows up to 200 Unicode scalar characters plus an ellipsis (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/run.rs:313-337`; `rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui.rs:2133-2133; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui.rs:3004-3006`). entries.title: Session import, export, clone and new-session command orchestration
entries.what: Translate session file and replacement commands into runtime operations with explicit confirmation, cancellation and visible outcomes.
entries.mechanism:
Export and import share a small first-argument parser. It accepts an exact command or a command followed by a space, trims leading argument whitespace, returns the first matching-quote segment for quoted input, and otherwise returns the first whitespace-delimited token. It does not process escaped quotes or trailing arguments; an unterminated quote produces no argument. Export chooses JSONL only for a case-sensitive .jsonl suffix, otherwise HTML, and catches errors into a visible export failure (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:7541-7584`).

Import requires a nonempty path and asks whether to replace the current session before calling the runtime. Cancellation from either confirmation or runtime gets a cancellation notice. After confirmation it clears the status indicator; MissingSessionCwdError prompts for a replacement working directory and retries, a missing input file gets a nonfatal error, and other failures route to the fatal-runtime handler. The retry within the missing-cwd catch is itself awaited without another surrounding catch in this method (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:7586-7628`).

Clone uses the current leaf and reports Nothing to clone yet when no leaf exists. It calls runtimeHost.fork with position at, retains the draft on cancellation, and clears the editor only after a successful clone; errors become an ordinary error notice. New session clears the status indicator, calls runtimeHost.newSession, respects cancellation and then appends its success message; failures use the fatal-runtime handler (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:6691-6710; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:8062-8075`).

The import and clone tests directly verify host routing, path parsing, cancellation and draft behavior. Package-command-paths coverage is shared from the CLI owner. Serialization, session validation and replacement internals have their own owners; this audit read tests without importing or executing them.
entries.interfaces: /export [path]; /import <path>; /clone; /new; getPathCommandArgument; showExtensionConfirm; runtimeHost.importFromJsonl/fork/newSession; MissingSessionCwdError and SessionImportFileNotFoundError.

entries.rust: Native export is implemented with md/markdown, html or jsonl format arguments and generated filenames under cwd; an arbitrary TS-style output path is rejected as an unknown format (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/commands.rs:384-416`; `rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui.rs:3056-3084`). Native import trims the whole argument, copies a .jsonl file into the default directory and switches sessions without the TS replacement confirmation/missing-cwd retry (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/commands.rs:656-675`; `rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/sessions.rs:102-196`). /clone reuses the functioning native fork path, which must be preserved (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/commands.rs:431-445`; `rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui.rs:3137-3146`). By contrast /new is an alias of /clear and its main-loop branch only clears the chat container and redraws the welcome message; it does not invoke a new durable session (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/commands.rs:24-41`; `rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui.rs:2996-2999`). This exact route is a bounded native issue, not evidence that native session replacement is entirely absent.

Route /new through the runtime's real session creation operation. Keep success, cancellation and recoverable missing-cwd errors distinct, and make editor clearing follow successful replacement.
entries.priority_reason: A command that appears to replace or create a session must match the actual runtime state and preserve the draft on cancellation.

entries.title: Session naming and expanded identity, usage and cost display
entries.what: Show the current session's name, file identity, message counts and detailed usage, and report the normalized name after renaming.
entries.mechanism:
An empty /name request shows the current name when one exists and otherwise displays usage guidance. A nonempty name is trimmed, sent through the session setter and then read back so normalization can be reported before showing the saved value. The host appends these notices to the transcript and requests render (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:7743-7765`).

/session renders current-session information rather than opening the saved-session picker. It includes an optional name, file or In-memory label, session ID, total/user/assistant message counts, and tool call/result counts. Input volume is input plus cache-read plus cache-write; when cache activity exists, cached tokens and their one-decimal share are separated from uncached input plus cache writes. Output and total tokens are also shown (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:7767-7805`).

A cost section appears when total cost or missed-cache tokens are nonzero. Total cost uses three decimals; multiple provider/model usage groups add per-group cost and token totals. Cache rebilling shows token count and singular/plural misses, with a monetary amount only at or above 0.0001. The UI consumes existing statistics and cache-waste calculations; it does not independently bill, estimate provider prices or change session accounting. The whole panel is an ordinary padded Text component followed by render (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:7807-7828`).

That native view reports message count, total/cached/uncached tokens, cost, cache-hit ratio, cumulative input/output, lane/leaf and active operation (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui.rs:3086-3135`; `rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/commands.rs:738-772`). entries.title: Fast-mode command, capability gating and completion visibility
entries.what: Expose supported fast-mode preferences through a small interactive command and hide its completion on unsupported models.
entries.mechanism:
The command lowercases its already-trimmed argument. Status reports the current on/off value only when the selected model supports fast mode, otherwise it reports unavailability. On and off select an explicit value, no argument toggles it, and every other argument produces the usage message (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:6666-6689`).

Enabling on an unsupported model warns and returns without changing the setting. Disabling remains allowed, and a successful change calls session.setFastMode and reports the chosen state. Completion includes /fast only for supported models; the source-read status test verifies both visibility branches. This UI does not define service-tier requests, pricing or model capability by itself.
entries.interfaces: /fast [on|off|status]; supportsFastMode/getFastMode/setFastMode; supported-model slash completion; exact usage and unavailable states.
entries.dependency_text: SESSION-036 owns stored preference and advertised capability checks; SET-011 owns settings and AI-026 the Responses service-tier request/cost contract. Only command admission, completion visibility and feedback are estimated here.
entries.rust: The full native slash registry and interactive controller contain model, provider and thinking controls but no /fast registration or matching capability-gated command (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/commands.rs:799-871`; controller and helper search for FastCommand, /fast and fast-mode UI routes). Existing model/thinking functionality remains under TUI-044/026; missing this command does not establish absence of all native service-tier plumbing.
entries.port: Expose fast mode only through the accepted session capability API, preserve disabling an unsupported stored preference, and update completion when the model changes. Keep transport/cost behavior in the existing Responses owner instead of duplicating it in the UI.
entries.priority_reason: The control is small but must advertise capability accurately and avoid silently changing unsupported model behavior.

entries.title: Explicit rendered-transcript and message debug snapshot command
entries.what: Write a local diagnostic snapshot containing rendered lines with widths and the active session's message JSON.
entries.mechanism:
The debug callback renders the current UI at the terminal's column count and records the terminal geometry and timestamp. It serializes every rendered line with an index, measured visible width and JSON escaping, then appends every session message as JSONL. It creates the parent directory recursively and synchronously overwrites the application debug log before adding a success notice (`ice:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts:8077-8108`).

The destination is getAgentDir() plus APP_NAME-debug.log. Both /debug and the renderer's onDebug callback route to the same host method. There is no host-level size cap, redaction pass, append rotation or local catch in this method; render or filesystem errors propagate. This describes the diagnostic artifact the application would write. The audit did not run this command or inspect user messages or real profile directories.
entries.interfaces: /debug; ui.onDebug; ui.render(columns); visibleWidth; getDebugLogPath => <agent-dir>/<APP_NAME>-debug.log; JSON-escaped rendered rows and JSONL session messages.
entries.dependency_text: Terminal rendering and width calculation are existing dependencies. This entry owns only explicit snapshot construction and its configured destination.
entries.rust: No /debug registration or equivalent product-host rendered-line-plus-message snapshot route appears in the fully read native slash registry/controller and helper search (`rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/commands.rs:799-871`). Native render diagnostics and logging remain separate existing capabilities; they do not establish this specific user-triggered artifact contract.
entries.port: Provide an explicit snapshot command over the native renderer with the same useful geometry and row-width diagnostics. Choose a bounded, error-reporting file writer and clearly document message-content inclusion; reuse native logging configuration without assuming ordinary logs already implement this snapshot.
entries.priority_reason: A reproducible rendering snapshot helps diagnose layout faults without changing normal interaction.

entries.title: Consistent grapheme cell widths and output-only normalization
entries.what: Measure and navigate terminal cells consistently for Unicode, ANSI, tabs and streamed emoji, then normalize only the bytes written to the terminal.
entries.mechanism:
TS shares Intl.Segmenter instances for grapheme and word segmentation. Printable ASCII returns length directly; non-ASCII widths are cached in an insertion-order Map capped 512, evicting its first key rather than refreshing access order. Tabs occupy 3 cells. Supported CSI/OSC/APC sequences are removed before grapheme width calculation.

Grapheme width first counts terminal-spacing mark-only clusters, then zeroes clusters composed entirely of default-ignorable/control/mark/surrogate code points. RGI emoji clusters are 2 cells, and isolated regional indicators U+1F1E6..1F1FF are conservatively 2 even before a complete flag arrives. Other clusters use the first visible base's east-Asian width plus terminal-spacing marks and selected trailing visible code points after marks, half/fullwidth forms and Thai/Lao AM vowels. The exact mark exceptions are in utils.ts40–48 and must be kept as data, not approximated by scalar summation. Tests cover Indic conjuncts, Myanmar, combining marks, CJK and flag intermediates.

getGraphemeCellRange returns the whole nonzero-width grapheme cell interval containing a column, including the second cell of a wide glyph. normalizeTerminalOutput decomposes Thai U+0E33 to U+0E4D U+0E32 and Lao U+0EB3 to U+0ECD U+0EB2 throughout its input, then expands visible tabs to 3 spaces while leaving tabs inside recognized terminal sequences intact. It does not rewrite logical editor content. The Thai/Lao replacement happens before terminal-sequence parsing, so unlike tabs it is not restricted to visible text.
entries.interfaces: getGraphemeSegmenter, getWordSegmenter, visibleWidth, getGraphemeCellRange, normalizeTerminalOutput; cjkBreakRegex identifies Han/Hiragana/Katakana/Hangul/Bopomofo. Integer cell positions differ from UTF-16 source offsets and Rust byte offsets.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/utils.rs:9-67 counts UnicodeWidthStr per scalar and skips controls/tabs unless an OSC/APC prefix triggers delegation to ansi.rs. rust:crates/ice-tui/src/ansi.rs:15-87 measures the whole stripped string with UnicodeWidthStr. Those two public width paths can disagree on multi-scalar emoji, and neither applies the TS tab/spacing-mark/output-normalization contract. rust:crates/ice-tui/src/ansi.rs:135-142 only appends SGR0 when needed. rust:crates/ice-tui/src/utils.rs:354-377 exposes a grapheme wrapper whose index is an ordinal from enumerate(), unlike Intl's UTF-16 offset. Native general stripping recognizes more protocols than TS and should be preserved.
entries.port: Consolidate crates/ice-tui cell measurement around unicode-segmentation plus explicit terminal-width policy, keeping byte/UTF-16/cell coordinates distinct at boundaries. Add the fixed tab policy, mark exceptions and output-only Thai/Lao normalization to the terminal writer; retain native broad protocol stripping and test it separately. Use read TS fixtures as acceptance cases, not a scalar-width proxy.
entries.priority_reason: Visible behavior shared by terminal consumers must agree before higher-level component parity is reliable.

entries.title: ANSI-aware word wrapping and stable style carry across rows
entries.what: Wrap readable words and CJK graphemes without losing active styling or hyperlink clickability across logical and physical line breaks.
entries.mechanism:
TS extractAnsiCode recognizes CSI by scanning to m/G/K/H/J, OSC by BEL/ST, and APC by BEL/ST; unrecognized/incomplete sequences return null. This is deliberately narrower than a general terminal parser and can scan beyond an unsupported CSI final byte until a later accepted letter. Preserve native general parsing rather than reproducing that limitation silently.

AnsiCodeTracker separately tracks bold, dim, italic, underline, blink, inverse, hidden, strike, foreground/background and active OSC8 link including params and original BEL/ST terminator. Empty/0 SGR resets styling but not the link. It understands selective resets,8/16-color,256-color and RGB38/48;2;r;g;b with 5 consumed parameters. Logical CRLF/CR/LF lines inherit active codes. Tokens keep ANSI attached to following visible content; literal spaces form whitespace runs and CJK-script graphemes are independent break opportunities. Overflow trims trailing whitespace, suppresses whitespace at a new line, and breaks a long token at grapheme boundaries.

A wrapped nonfinal line closes underline and an active hyperlink, reopens active codes on continuation, and intentionally leaves background/other styles for caller padding. Final segments do not receive an automatic full reset. A whole input line that already fits is returned as-is. Empty input yields one empty line. TS has no explicit nonpositive-width guard here: an indivisible grapheme wider than the requested width may produce an empty prefix then an overwide grapheme, so the documented universal <=width claim has that boundary limitation.
entries.interfaces:
wrapTextWithAnsi(text, width):string[]; internal AnsiCodeTracker/getLineEndReset and token/long-word helpers. Source line 902's token assignment was transport-redacted; surrounding tokenization implementation and consuming loop were fully visible.

isWhitespaceChar(char:string):boolean uses /\s/.test(char); isPunctuationChar(char:string):boolean uses the exported PUNCTUATION_REGEX. These predicates accept strings and test for a matching character rather than enforcing length one. Exact punctuation pattern (verbatim):
```ts
export const PUNCTUATION_REGEX = /[(){}[\]<>.,;:'"!?+\-=*/\\|&%^$#@~`]/;
```
Source: `ice:packages/tui/src/utils.ts:971-985`.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/utils.rs:275-351 hard-wraps scalar characters, keeps leading wrap spaces, drops tabs/CR/control characters, drops a trailing empty newline and returns one empty line for width 0. It subsequently calls rust:crates/ice-tui/src/line_diff.rs:223-234 to isolate ANSI rows; therefore style carry is present, not wholly missing. That isolator appends full reset plus BEL OSC8 close on every parsed row and preserves supported SGR/OSC8 state. Exact defect in rust:crates/ice-tui/src/line_diff.rs:111-178: RGB checks index+5 and consumes 6 parameters, but standard 38/48;2;r;g;b has 5; normal RGB state is interpreted as unrelated SGR fragments on the next row, while an extra following parameter can be absorbed. Bold anddim share one native Intensity slot. Native atoms/slice/patch correctly use graphemes and reject unsupported controls to a fallback.
entries.port: Implement token/CJK word wrapping in crates/ice-tui with the common width function and an explicit attribute/link state machine; retain the native row-isolation/column-patch approach while fixing RGB parameter cardinality and independent bold/dim state. Choose/document final reset and padding ownership to match TS visible output without regressing safe independent row repaint. Keep width 0 and indivisible-wide-grapheme behavior explicit.
entries.priority_reason: Visible behavior shared by terminal consumers must agree before higher-level component parity is reliable.

entries.title: Bounded column slicing, ellipsis truncation and background continuation
entries.what: Clip and composite text by terminal cells while keeping grapheme boundaries, inherited styles and pane backgrounds intact.
entries.mechanism:
truncateToWidth returns empty at maxWidth<=0, optionally pads empty/short input, and returns original input if it fits even when the ellipsis itself is wider than the target. Otherwise it preserves a contiguous grapheme prefix within maxWidth-minus-ellipsis-width; it never skips a wide grapheme and resumes later. An oversized ellipsis is itself clipped by whole grapheme. Truncated results put SGR0 before and after nonempty ellipsis, or once after an empty ellipsis, then optional spaces to exact width. Retained ANSI codes are emitted only when followed by retained visible content. Tabs count 3; large-input scanning stops once overflow is established.

sliceWithWidth/sliceByColumn preserve sequences occurring in the selected span and replay pending prefix sequences at the first included grapheme. A glyph starting before startCol is excluded. strict=false may include a wide glyph extending past the right edge; strict=true excludes it. Return actual width separately and do not imply automatic padding. extractSegments takes beforeEnd, afterStart, afterLen and optional strictAfter; before is always boundary-strict, after inherits effective attributes/link through a pooled tracker, including changes hidden under the overlay.

applyBackgroundToLine pads only when content is short, then splits around SGRs that reset background (empty,0,49) and re-applies bgFn to each intervening span. It skips the parameter arguments of 38/48 extended colors so palette 0 or RGB component 49 are not mistaken for resets. It does not truncate an already-overwide input.
entries.interfaces: truncateToWidth(text, maxWidth, ellipsis='...', pad=false); sliceByColumn(line, start, length, strict=false); sliceWithWidth=>{text, width}; extractSegments=>{before, beforeWidth, after, afterWidth}; applyBackgroundToLine(line, width, bgFn).
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/ansi.rs:93-131 strips all ANSI despite its preserve_styles flag and includes an endpoint grapheme even if it exceeds requested width. rust:crates/ice-tui/src/utils.rs:71-155 slices scalar characters, preserves a raw pending escape history, may overrun wide boundaries and bases padding on total source column rather than selected width. rust:crates/ice-tui/src/utils.rs:159-224 returns an overwide suffix unchanged when target width saturates to 0 and puts the suffix before its final reset; no pad option. rust:crates/ice-tui/src/utils.rs:444-453 pads and calls bg_fn once, so SGR49 inside a panel is not generically reopened. Native rust:crates/ice-tui/src/line_diff.rs:238-269 already provides a stricter grapheme/style-aware private slice that blanks intersected wide cells; retain and reuse it instead of declaring all native clipping absent.
entries.port: Unify crates/ice-tui clipping/compositing around grapheme atoms, explicit result cell counts and shared SGR/OSC8 context. Port contiguous-prefix truncation and bounded ellipsis, offer strict/non-strict slice contracts intentionally, and reapply generic background closures after true resets. Preserve the native clipped-wide-cell blanking mode where layout requires it; compatibility wrappers can expose TS's exclusion semantics.

entries.title: OSC8 hyperlink hit-testing, selective removal and hover styling
entries.what: Identify the hyperlink under a terminal cell and change its presentation without confusing OSC parameters, text or closing sequences.
entries.mechanism:
TS recognizes OSC8 open/close with arbitrary parameter text, URL following the second semicolon, and either BEL or ST terminator. getOsc8LinkAtColumn tracks open URL and clears it on an empty URL; it returns the active URL for any occupied cell of a grapheme, including its second wide cell, with tabs counted 3. It ignores other recognized terminal sequences.

The shared rewrite routine visits visible runs with current link identity while preserving non-OSC8 controls. stripOsc8Links removes wrappers only for matching URLs, keeping text and styling; a closing sequence follows the link it closes. styleOsc8Link wraps each visible text run for the selected URL with caller-provided open/close sequences, so decoration is reapplied after intervening ANSI changes. This is link state/presentation, not URL authorization or process launching.
entries.interfaces: getOsc8LinkAtColumn(line, column):string|undefined; stripOsc8Links(line, predicate); styleOsc8Link(line, url, open, close). Only the hit-test helper is re-exported by the package index.

entries.title: Padded Text, Box, Spacer and first-line truncated components
entries.what: Render reusable text/padding containers with matching empty-content behavior, width accounting, backgrounds and cache invalidation.
entries.mechanism:
Text defaults text='', paddingX=1, paddingY=1, optional custom background. Raw empty or trim-empty text renders no rows. It expands every tab to 3 spaces before wrapping, uses max(1, width-2*paddingX), surrounds each wrapped row with both horizontal margins and pads to width, then adds width-filled top/bottom rows. An optional bgFn applies through background-reset-aware utility. Its cache keys text and width; setText, setCustomBgFn and invalidate clear it. Caller-owned mutable background closures require invalidation if behavior changes without the setter.

Box defaults padding 1/1, returns no rows for no children or all-empty child output, renders children at max(1, width-2*paddingX), prepends left padding then pads/backgrounds each row. Cache compares width, exact rendered child lines and bgFn('test') sample; it still renders children before cache lookup. setBgFn relies on sampling rather than immediate invalidation; invalidate cascades. removeChild removes only the first identity match. There is no intrinsic border in Box.

Spacer defaults 1 empty row and supports setLines; it is unpadded and uncached. TruncatedText defaults zero margins, selects text before the first LF only, truncates at max(1, width-2*paddingX), surrounds/pads to full width and adds width-filled vertical rows. Empty text still renders one padded content row. These minimum-content-width policies can exceed an extremely narrow outer width when margins alone do not fit; do not claim hard clipping universally.

The unpadded Container exposes a mutable children array; addChild appends, removeChild deletes the first identity match, clear replaces the array, render concatenates every child at the same width, and invalidate calls optional child invalidation. It adds no layout sizing or implicit redraw.
entries.interfaces: Text(text='', paddingX=1, paddingY=1, bgFn?), setText, setCustomBgFn, invalidate; Box(addChild/removeChild/clear/setBgFn); Spacer(lines=1).setLines; TruncatedText(text, paddingX=0, paddingY=0). Container.children/addChild/removeChild/clear/render/invalidate.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/text.rs:28-125 has a content/width/theme-revision cache and setter, but subtracts only one horizontal padding, prefixes left padding only, emits empty unpadded vertical rows, does not suppress whitespace-only text or support custom background, and iterates str.lines before scalar wrapping. rust:crates/ice-tui/src/box_component.rs:29-208 largely mirrors caching/background sampling, but content width can be 0 and remove_child removes every pointer-equal duplicate. Background behavior differs through utils. rust:crates/ice-tui/src/spacer.rs:12-31 renders the requested empty rows but has no mutator/default constructor. rust:crates/ice-tui/src/truncated_text.rs:19-92 instead stores a fixed max_width/custom ellipsis/style, renders min(max_width, viewport), does not select only the first logical line or add margins/padding. Preserve its useful native setters/custom ellipsis while adding the TS component contract. Native inline tests were fully read, not run. rust:crates/ice-tui/src/container.rs:16-82 supplies Arc-shared child storage, append/clear and ordered rendering, but removes every pointer-equal duplicate and holds the child mutex while calling render/invalidate. Retain owned child snapshots and avoid reentrant callback deadlock when adapting mutable component trees.
entries.port: Adjust crates/ice-tui components and compatibility constructors to expose paired margins, explicit blank behavior and optional background closures. Retain native theme-revision cache invalidation and existing custom-ellipsis/style controls. Share corrected wrap/clip/background helpers, avoid duplicating style state, and keep narrow-width margin behavior deliberate.

entries.title: Legacy, Kitty and modifyOtherKeys key identity and printable decoding
entries.what: Give raw terminal sequence consumers consistent logical key names, modifier matching and printable text without confusing keyboard layout, key release or protocol modes.
entries.mechanism:
TS uses Shift=1, Alt=2, Ctrl=4, Super=8 and masks CapsLock64/NumLock128. Kitty encoded modifiers are one-indexed; CSI-u accepts alternate shifted/base-layout codepoints and press/repeat/release event fields, with modified arrows/Home/End/tilde navigation. Keypad 57399–57408 maps to 0–9,57409–57413 to ./ * - + (57410 is slash),57415='=',57416=',',57417–57426 to navigation/delete;57414 is keypad Enter. Shifted uppercase Latin identity normalizes to lowercase. Latin letters/digits/known symbols remain authoritative over physical base-layout keys; other layouts can use reported base key. Legacy CSI/SS3/Linux/rxvt navigation/function-key sequences are enumerated at keys.ts368–480, including shifted lowercase CSI and Ctrl lowercase SS3, $/^ tilde variants, Alt-b/f/p/n arrows and F1–F12. Function-key matches only permit no modifiers.

Explicit Kitty and xterm CSI27;mod;code~ matching works regardless of negotiated mode. Ambiguous legacy Alt printable/control forms are disabled in Kitty mode; LF and ESC+CR become Shift+Enter there, otherwise Enter/Alt+Enter. Raw CR remains Enter; keypad SS3 OM is Enter. Local WT_SESSION without truthy SSH_CONNECTION/SSH_CLIENT/SSH_TTY makes raw BS0x08 Ctrl+Backspace; DEL remains Backspace, and raw BS also matches Ctrl+h through the general raw-control path. Esc/return aliases and order-independent modifier strings match; parseKey emits modifiers in Shift, Ctrl, Alt, Super order, although raw uppercase ASCII parses as the uppercase character rather than the explicit shifted form. Unsupported modifier bits reject formatted key IDs.

isKeyRelease/isKeyRepeat scan supported :3/:2 suffix substrings (u,~, A–D, H, F), not a fully anchored event parser, and exempt bracketed-paste payloads. matchesKey does not itself suppress release events. decodeKittyPrintable permits only Shift and lock bits, prefers the reported shifted key, normalizes keypad keys, rejects controls/invalid codepoints, and returns String.fromCodePoint; it does not check the event-type field, so callers must discard releases where required. decodePrintableKey adds modifyOtherKeys with the same non-Control/Alt/Super printable policy.
entries.interfaces:
KeyId/Key helper permutations; matchesKey, parseKey, isKeyRelease, isKeyRepeat, decodeKittyPrintable, decodePrintableKey, setKittyProtocolActive, isKittyProtocolActive. Raw strings and Crossterm structured events need an explicit adapter, not interchangeable representations.

Exported supporting type (verbatim):
```ts
export type KeyEventType = "press" | "repeat" | "release";
```
Source: `ice:packages/tui/src/keys.ts:505-505`.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/keys.rs:1-524 has a public string parser, but uses Ctrl=1/Shift=2/Alt=4, fails to subtract 1, discards colon-containing parameters via filter_map and derives event type from the first keycode parameter. It misidentifies 1~ as F1, groups several F-key numbers together, maps keypad 57399 to Insert/57414 to Delete, omits alternate-layout/modifyOtherKeys/lock handling and accepts only ASCII printables. Key::to_key_id alphabetically sorts modifier names and exact-matches strings, conflicting with ctrl_alt helper order; global Kitty state does not affect parsing. Its printable decoder accepts ASCII CSI-u without checking modifiers or release type. These are source-established public-helper defects, not evidence all native typing is broken: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/terminal.rs:401-415 supplies Crossterm KeyEvent, and rust:crates/ice-tui/src/keybindings.rs:686-703 matches those directly. Bounded crates search found no call to decode_kitty_printable_from_str beyond its definition.
entries.port: Implement a single protocol parser with correctly normalized flags, event types and keypad mappings; keep raw printable decoding separate from shortcut identity. Bridge native structured events while retaining Crossterm's direct Unicode input path. Add table-driven acceptance cases from the read TS tests plus malformed/locked/released events; do not enable modifyOtherKeys until the active input reader can decode it. Preserve the observed TS caller-level release policy rather than claiming its printable helper suppresses releases.
entries.priority_reason: Raw-input extensions and compatibility paths need correct key identity; active native structured-event handling must remain intact.

entries.title: Incremental sequence framing and bracketed-paste assembly
entries.what: Deliver complete escape events and paste payloads across arbitrary stdin chunks while keeping ordinary input responsive.
entries.mechanism:
StdinBuffer emits individual data sequences immediately and retains incomplete CSI/OSC/DCS/APC/SS3/meta sequences behind a resettable 10 ms default timer. CSI ends at a final byte 0x40–0x7e; SGR mouse requires three numeric fields, old X10 mouse consumes ESC[M plus 3 code units; OSC accepts BEL/ST, DCS/APC ST. Lone ESC flushes as one unfinished sequence. Explicit flush returns buffered data without emitting, clears the timer and pending printable marker; clear/destroy discard buffer, paste state and timers. Empty input emits an empty data event when ordinary buffer is empty. A single Buffer byte>127 converts to ESC+(byte−128); other buffers use toString.

Bracketed paste recognizes ESC[200~ and collects through ESC[201~, including split markers while the ordinary 10 ms fragment budget has not expired; paste-mode buffering has no timeout/cap. Input before a paste is parsed and emitted, content is one paste event, suffix recursively processes; an incomplete pre-paste remainder is discarded by that branch. TS ProcessTerminal re-wraps the payload for existing editors. Ordinary text splitting uses UTF-16 code units, not graphemes, so this source does not guarantee one event per supplementary Unicode scalar. A raw ESC followed by a second ESC introducing [/] /O/P/_ emits a standalone first ESC to avoid WezTerm Escape-release suffix leakage. After an unmodified no-semicolon Kitty printable report, one immediately following matching single-code-unit raw character is suppressed, including across chunks; intervening sequences/paste/clear reset the marker. This is narrow duplicate-text suppression, not generic event deduplication.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/stdin_buffer.rs:1-312 is a batch queue/callback abstraction, not a protocol framer. It searches paste markers only inside each input argument, so a marker split between calls is missed (split end stays permanently inside paste). No partial-escape parser/timer/duplicate-text suppression exists. process updates last_input immediately before should_batch; its usual elapsed<1 ms branch emits the entire input chunk as Data, not individual sequences. Batching only occurs if that same call takes 1 ms to less than 16 ms before checking, and there is no timer-driven flush. A single oversized chunk can exceed the nominal64KiB buffer cap. Callbacks run under the callback mutex and, on some paths, buffer/paste-buffer locks, making reentrant on_event/flush/reset calls capable of deadlock. The bounded crates search found StdinBuffer construction only in its inline tests; primary terminal.rs uses Crossterm instead. Native rust:crates/ice-tui/src/windows_paste.rs:22-119 separately bulk-reads up to 1024 safe console records for a sole reader, preserves UTF-16 pairs and trailing Enter, and must not be removed.
entries.port: Provide the source-compatible incremental framer only at raw-stream boundaries, with callback dispatch outside locks and owned cancellable timers. Retain native structured-event and Windows bulk-paste paths; explicitly document which host owns each stream. Preserve TS observable assembly/dedup rules and document its UTF-16/timeout/unclosed-paste limits rather than attributing stronger behavior. Fixture tests should split every marker and protocol response at each boundary and verify one ordered payload without executing real terminal state.
entries.priority_reason: Fragmented input must not become commands or literal escape suffixes; the current native helper's name masks a materially different contract.

entries.title: Keyboard negotiation, platform modifier helpers and fallback input
entries.what: Negotiate enhanced keys without swallowing user input and restore terminal protocol state across start, drain and stop.
entries.mechanism:
TS starts raw UTF-8 stdin, enables bracketed paste, installs resize before Unix self-SIGWINCH, and enables Windows VT input after raw-mode setup. It pushes Kitty flags 7, queries flags, and appends a device-attributes sentinel (ESC[>7u ESC[?u ESC[c). Nonzero flags activate global/terminal Kitty state and disable modifyOtherKeys; zero flags or DA before Kitty enables xterm modifyOtherKeys level 2. There is no fixed whole-negotiation startup timeout; ordinary input is forwarded meanwhile. An incomplete ESC[ or ESC[?digits; prefix flushed by StdinBuffer receives a separate 150 ms fragment timer; valid continuations are consumed, invalid/expired prefixes replay as input. Pushed state is recorded independently of observed support so stop/drain can pop once.

On darwin TERM_PROGRAM=Apple_Terminal, raw CR becomes CSI13;2u only when the local native shift helper reports true. Unlike Rust's guard, this TS check does not exclude SSH. The lazy Darwin helper caches success/failure, supports x64/arm64, probes module-parent/module/executable native/prebuilds locations, validates isModifierPressed and returns false on unavailable/error. C reads combined-session CGEventSourceFlagsState for shift/command/control/option via a N-API bridge. entries.title: Stack allocation, visibility and direct rendering
entries.what: Allocate horizontal and vertical stack children deterministically under basis, grow, shrink, min/max, gap and viewport visibility constraints.
entries.mechanism:
Stack stores component entries in order; addChild normalizes finite numeric gap/grow/shrink/min/max to nonnegative floored integers (fallback gap/grow/min 0, shrink 1, max MAX_SAFE_INTEGER), while basis is retained and normalized by allocation. Defaults are basis auto, grow 0, shrink 1, min 0, max unlimited, align stretch. visible(viewport) filters entries before gaps/allocation; direct render passes effectively unbounded viewport height, while constrained layout uses real dimensions. removeChild removes the first identity match from both child/entry lists; clear empties both.

allocateStackSizes clamps basis or measured intrinsic size to min and max adjusted to at least min. With an available size, subtract gaps and repeatedly distribute remaining growth/overflow among eligible children until exhausted/no progress. Grow weight is grow; shrink weight is shrink*max(1, currentSize). Each ordered candidate receives at least 1 up to floor(currentRemaining*weight/totalWeight), capacity and remaining; remaining decreases inside the same pass. Recompute eligible weights on subsequent passes. Therefore this is an ordered iterative integer algorithm, not a single proportional division. Unsatisfied min constraints may still overflow.

Direct VStack renders children, applies natural basis/min/max sizes by slicing or blank-padding, and inserts gaps. HStack measures all visible children at outer width, allocates, re-renders each nonzero-width child at its own width, uses max rendered height and vertically offsets center/end children before ANSI-aware composition. Empty stacks render no rows.

Direct VStack305-325 ignores basis/min/max entirely. entries.title: Extensible constrained layout tree and nested scroll geometry
entries.what: Expose component layout nodes and produce one clipped geometry tree for rendering, cursor visibility and nested scroll hit routing.
entries.mechanism:
The symbol-based layout hook lets any component return vstack/hstack/scroll structure. A frame uses floor-normalized positive dimensions and a per-component/per-width render cache so measure and paint share results; fixed basis skips unnecessary intrinsic measurement. Leaves keep full rendered lines, allocate requested/natural height and shift lineOffset just far enough to keep their first cursor marker visible. VStack allocates each child vertically and computes natural height with gaps. HStack allocates widths, measures children at their own positive width, applies stretch/start/center/end vertical placement and represents zero-width children without painting.

Scroll layout recursively lays out the child at unbounded height and y−oldScrollTop, obtains actual constrained child geometry, updates state, translates descendants for the new scroll position and recalculates ancestor-intersected clips. Thus nested ScrollViews remain in the tree. Frame primary selection uses the first encountered scroll as fallback and replaces it whenever a later marked-primary scroll is encountered. getScrollViewBox searches by state identity; getScrollViewsAt returns containing clipped scrolls deepest-first. Every child has a real parent reference; coordinates may be negative for offscreen content.

Painting iterates only clipped visible row ranges, removes leading OSC133 A/B/C zone markers, composes at allocated x/width and handles Kitty top/bottom cropping through image metadata. The full-width painted-row cache keys line+width, scrollbar cache also sampled style; lines>4096 code units bypass, and cache clears when reaching 4096 entries. entries.title: Scroll state, follow-end and render notifications

entries.title: ANSI-safe row composition, blank clearing and image protection

entries.title: Overlay focus stack, hidden-state transitions and deferred restoration
entries.what: Maintain independent overlay membership, paint order, focus ownership and restoration so nested or temporarily hidden overlays do not steal focus from explicit caller targets.
entries.mechanism:
showOverlay captures preFocus, assigns a monotonically increasing focusOrder and appends membership. Visible capturing overlays take focus; nonCapturing overlays may still be explicitly focused. Hide permanently removes membership, retargets other entries' preFocus links that pointed to it, and if focused restores the highest focusOrder visible capturing overlay or its prior target. hideOverlay removes the last inserted entry, not the latest focused entry. setHidden is a reversible visibility flag; hiding restores focus and clears restore state, showing a visible capturing entry raises focusOrder and focuses. handle.focus checks membership and visibility, raises order, then focuses. hasOverlay uses current terminal-size visibility predicate; raw hasOverlayEntries includes hidden entries. All entries are invalidated including hidden ones.

Focus restoration has explicit eligible/blocked states. Moving from an eligible overlay to a target outside its preFocus ancestor chain blocks restoration on that target. A later explicit focus operation may carry or resolve the blocked state; unmounting the blocker allows restoration. handle.unfocus({target}) supports explicit target including null, and can store a deferred target while another blocker remains focused. Unfocus without target clears its restore claim. Structural focused flags are toggled for previous/new focusable components. The restoration graph and membership traversal, rather than simply popping a stack, determine behavior.
