entries.title: Overlay size resolution, screen anchoring and passive placement
entries.what: Resolve overlay width/height/position deterministically against the viewport and composite visible overlays in focus order without retaining stale document high-water rows.
entries.mechanism:
Margins may be one number or four edges, each clamped nonnegative. Available dimensions are at least 1. Numeric width is used directly; a valid nonnegative decimal percentage is floored against full terminal width. Default width=min(80, availableWidth). minWidth is applied before clamping into 1..availableWidth. maxHeight is optional, numeric or percentage of full terminal height and clamped 1..availableHeight; absent maxHeight does not clip content to the viewport. Render occurs once at resolved width, maxHeight clips only when supplied, then final position uses actual rendered height. Explicit numeric row/col or percentages position within free remaining extent plus margins; invalid percentage falls back to centered. Nine anchors are the alternative, followed by offsets and margin clamps.

Visible entries paint ascending focusOrder. Composite working height is max(current base rows, terminal rows, row+overlay rows), never historical maxLinesRendered; overlays address that resulting viewport. Blank overlay rows clear their allocated span through the compositor. This means presence of hidden entries can still cause the caller to enter overlay composition, but only visible entries render. TS allows passive/nonCapturing overlays to overlap; it is solely a focus policy.

entries.title: Terminal background queries and color-scheme reply ownership
entries.what: Parse terminal color replies with exact framing and ensure asynchronous requests, late replies and scheme notifications cannot leak response bytes into editor input.
entries.mechanism: OSC11 must be exactly ESC]11;body followed by BEL or ST. Body supports #RRGGBB or #RRRRGGGGBBBB and slash-separated rgb/rgba (prefix case-insensitive and optional); only first 3 slash fields matter, each nonempty hexadecimal channel of arbitrary digit width scales and rounds to 0..255. Scheme report is one or more concatenated CSI ?997;1n / ;2n, with only all-valid concatenations accepted and the last report deciding dark/light. queryTerminalBackgroundColor writes OSC11 and enqueues FIFO request records. A timeout resolves undefined but leaves its record and pending count so a late matching reply is swallowed against that record instead of resolving a newer request; no reply can therefore leave a timed-out record at the FIFO front indefinitely. Only replies while pending are intercepted; a matching malformed body still consumes and settles undefined. Scheme query subscribes once plus timeout then writes CSI ?996n; every matching report broadcasts to current subscriptions, including concurrent requests. Notification toggle uses CSI ?2031 h/l; received valid reports are recognized regardless of toggle. stop does not cancel outstanding color-query records/timers.
entries.interfaces:
parseOsc11BackgroundColor(string)->RGB|undefined, parseTerminalColorSchemeReport->'dark'|'light'|undefined; queryTerminalBackgroundColor({timeoutMs:number}):Promise<RgbColor|undefined>, queryTerminalColorScheme({timeoutMs:number}):Promise<TerminalColorScheme|undefined>, onTerminalColorSchemeChange, setTerminalColorSchemeNotifications.

entries.title: Main-screen differential rendering, shrink policy and transcript cursor accounting
entries.what: Update only changed transcript rows while preserving terminal scrollback, handling viewport movement, overlays and image row reservations.
entries.mechanism:
The renderer tracks previous lines/dimensions, logical content end, actual hardware row, viewport top and maximum rows rendered. It renders base, composites overlays, extracts viewport cursor and closes ordinary line styles. Initial full paint does not clear; width change always clears screen+scrollback; height change does so except TERMUX_VERSION; clearOnShrink triggers when new length is below historical maximum and there are no overlay entries. Full paint clips overwide ordinary text and uses Kitty reservation rows so image transmission does not scroll unexpectedly. Differential comparison expands changed ranges to affected old/new image blocks, deletes changed old image IDs, and repaints only first..last changed rows. Changes above previously visible rows or deletion that would move above viewport force clear/full paint. Pure deletion clears rows without scrolling when possible. Appending starts with CRLF after old content and advances viewport bookkeeping. In-viewport overlay changes use absolute screen rows to avoid relative drift. A differential ordinary line wider than terminal causes a crash log, terminal stop, then error; full paints clip instead. Debug-redraw and render dumps are opt-in and file failures are not caught.

captureRenderState copies text/dimensions/cursor/high-water state; restore blanks image lines and clears tracked image IDs. Normal stop moves to logical end and writes newline, unless preserveScreen or there was no history. No-change frames still reposition/hide/show cursor. Full-redraw counter increments only actual full paints.

entries.title: Alternate-screen frame assembly, teardown transcript and mode ownership
entries.what: Render a viewport-owned application frame and leave a readable transcript when exiting fullscreen while restoring terminal and image capability state.
entries.mechanism:
Without explicit layout root, TuiAltScreen wraps normal children in an implicit primary ScrollView with follow=end. setLayoutRoot identity changes clear cached layout and request a frame. Start clears selection/drag/flash timers and image upload cache, captures image protocol, temporarily disables iTerm2 images globally and invalidates if needed, resets render state, enters alternate screen, disables autowrap and enables requested mouse/focus modes before terminal keyboard setup. Each frame clamps width/height to at least 1, lays out root, strips leading OSC133 A/B/C zones, composites overlays, keeps last viewport-height rows, applies selection/action hover/flash, extracts cursor, closes nonimage styles and clips ordinary overwide rows. Full repaint occurs on first frame or dimension change; synchronized output wraps clearing, image actions, changed rows and explicit cursor visibility. Normal nonimage unchanged rows are skipped; any image change repaints all rows.

Stop first cancels selection/scrollbar/flash state, deletes Kitty images, disables mouse and reenables autowrap on the owning alternate screen, then terminal.stop disables keyboard there. After leaving the screen, preserveScreen only restores the original screen. Otherwise source rerenders the full document, strips cursor/leading zones, normalizes/clips rows and appends them to the restored main screen with per-line clearing, final reset/newline and cursor show. Temporarily disabled iTerm2 capability is then restored.

entries.title: Viewport wheel routing, prompt navigation and scrollbar dragging
entries.what: Route viewport keyboard and mouse gestures to the correct nested scroll view, preserving overscroll policies and active scrollbar state.
entries.mechanism:
The viewport input listener consumes focus-in/out, wheel, SGR mouse and otherwise recognized mouse sequences before focused components. Focus-out cancels active press/autoscroll/drag/hover and clears in-progress selection, while an already completed selection remains. SGR wheel supports button 64/65 (including modifier bits) and X10 six-character wheel frames; horizontal wheel codes are ignored as wheel, then mouse input is still swallowed. Wheel lines default 1 and floor/clamp to at least 1. Route deepest hit scroll views, pass unconsumed delta outward until zero or contain, then fall back to unseen primary if remainder remains; always request frame. Keyboard page movement uses max(1, viewportHeight-4), top/bottom and previous/next OSC133 A prompt row. Matching releases are consumed without movement.

Scrollbar hit tests only the thumb cell, disabled when any visible overlay exists. Hover toggles setScrollbarActive. Primary nonmotion press on thumb clears selection and records grabbed offset. Drag recomputes current geometry each event, clamps thumb offset and maps rounded fraction to max scrollTop; release stops drag. No track click behavior is implemented. Viewport key handling still runs through the listener even with overlays; it is not automatically suppressed by overlay focus.

Release requires the active press; same view, row, col without any drag activates the pressed URL via optional openUrl and catches callback errors. entries.title: Kitty and iTerm2 image serialization and deletion
entries.what: Transmit image payloads with correct continuation, cursor, placement and data-release controls, and support iTerm2 inline options.
entries.mechanism: isImageLine recognizes Kitty APC and iTerm2 File OSC anywhere in a line regardless of detected support, including large prefixed payloads. Kitty accepts already-base64 data, serializes a=T, f=100, q=2, adds C=1 only when moveCursor=false, and independently adds truthy columns, rows, imageId. Payloads up to 4096 characters use one frame; longer payloads use 4096-character chunks, full controls+m=1 on first, m=1 on intermediates and m=0 on last. Empty payload still produces a frame. Delete one uses a=d, d=I, i=id, q=2, all image data d=A, q=2, placements only d=a, q=2. iTerm2 defaults inline=1, emits defined width/height even 0, base64-encodes optional name, emits preserveAspectRatio=0 only when false and terminates with BEL. renderImage always uses Kitty f=100 and does not itself transcode other image formats.

entries.title: Image dimensions and aspect-preserving cell fitting
entries.what: Read image geometry and fit it to explicit width/height cell limits using current pixel cell dimensions.
entries.mechanism: Size fitting floors and clamps maxWidthCells and optional maxHeightCells to at least 1, clamps image pixel dimensions to 1, computes min(widthScale, heightScale), allows upscaling, and ceil/clamps resulting columns and rows. Default cells are 9x18; explicit zero cell dimensions are not validated. calculateImageRows shares fitting. Header helpers decode base64 and return null on caught failures. PNG requires 24 bytes and only first 4 signature bytes before big-endian width/height at 16/20. JPEG scans SOI and markers, recognizes SOF C0-C2, skips non-FF bytes and otherwise advances by 2+segmentLength when length>=2. GIF checks 87a/89a and reads little-endian width/height. WebP requires 30 bytes and RIFF/WEBP; handles VP8, VP8L dimension bits at 21..24 and VP8X 24-bit fields at 24/27. The public dispatcher uses exact MIME strings image/png, jpeg, gif, webp. These are header readers, not full decoders or validity checks.

entries.title: Unicode word navigation and atomic segments
entries.what: Move and delete by linguistic word, punctuation run or caller-defined atomic marker without merging distinct boundaries.
entries.mechanism: Backward slices text before the UTF16 cursor, segments with Intl.Segmenter or a supplied segment callback, skips trailing whitespace unless atomic, then consumes exactly one atomic segment, one word-like segment up to its last ASCII punctuation boundary, or a contiguous nonword/nonwhitespace run. Forward symmetrically skips leading whitespace then consumes one unit; inside word-like segments it stops at the first ASCII punctuation. Atomic checks precede whitespace/word logic. Word segmentation therefore splits CJK linguistic units and handles a whole paste marker independent of spaces inside it. Examples from read tests: forward hello world at 0=>5 and at 5=>11; foo.bar visits 0,3,4,7; backward 7=>4=>3=>0.

It has no linguistic segmentation or atomic marker hooks. Non-ASCII punctuation absent from the boundary list is treated as a word character; a cursor beyond scalar length can index out of bounds in backward helpers. Keep native line/current-word/word-end helpers, but do not treat them as source-equivalent word movement.

entries.title: Kill-ring and undo snapshot semantics
entries.what: Retain deleted-text history and detached undo snapshots with the source's accumulation, rotation and capacity behavior.
entries.mechanism: KillRing ignores empty text; every nonaccumulating push adds an entry even if equal to the latest. Accumulation replaces latest with prepend(text+latest) for backward deletion or append(latest+text) for forward. peek reads latest, rotate moves latest to oldest when length>1 and permanently changes subsequent yank order. There is no source capacity limit or deduplication. UndoStack.push structuredClone's arbitrary state, pop returns the detached snapshot directly, clear empties and length counts; no limit, redo or action grouping exists in the utility itself (consumers own grouping).

Actual native Input snapshots clone String and Editor state must be assessed separately; a generic owned Arc is not a deep clone. Preserve native RedoStack/UndoRedoManager and optional limits without silently claiming unbounded/deep-clone compatibility.
entries.port: Expose explicit compatibility capacity/dedup policy and document snapshot ownership for native state. Preserve redo/limits as native options, ensure undo snapshots own all mutable editor/paste metadata, and let consumer action state determine accumulation/coalescing.

entries.title: Fuzzy score precision, token matching and alphanumeric fallback
entries.what: Produce the same matching set and stable ordering for commands, providers and other selector text.
entries.mechanism: Case-fold both strings; empty query matches score 0 and longer query fails. Greedy in-order UTF16 matches score lower-is-better: consecutive counter starts from lastIndex=-1 so a match at text index 0 already receives -5; successive consecutive matches subtract counter*5, gaps after a prior match add 2 per skipped unit; boundaries at start or whitespace,-,_ ,.,/, colon subtract 10; every match adds index*0.1; exact normalized equality subtracts 100. Only after primary failure, anchored ASCII all-letters+all-digits or reversed two-block query is swapped, and a successful swapped score gets+5. fuzzyFilter splits trimmed query on whitespace/slash, requires every token independently against the same text, sums scores and stable-sorts; empty/tokenless query returns the original array.
entries.interfaces: FuzzyMatch {matches, score:number}; fuzzyMatch and generic fuzzyFilter(items, query, getText).
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/fuzzy.rs:35-267 mostly ports matching/filtering and keeps a stable score sort, but score is i32 and each 0.1*position penalty is individually truncated; consecutive bonus excludes the first index 0 match. Matching positions are Unicode scalars rather than UTF16. swap_alphanumeric does not validate both entire blocks: it can skip intervening punctuation and accepts trailing mixed characters, producing matches the source's anchored regex rejects. Keep borrowed/owned native filter variants and Unicode-safe traversal, but calibrate scoring/matching contract explicitly.
entries.port: Use exact scaled integer tenths or floating score, reproduce first-match and stable-tie rules, and restrict swap fallback to the two anchored ASCII forms. Define non-BMP indexing intentionally in the compatibility layer and keep native owned/borrowed APIs.
entries.priority_reason: Subtle score and fallback differences reorder suggestions across many dialogs and can introduce false matches.

entries.title: Single-line input mutation, paste and undo integration
entries.what: Provide source-compatible single-line editing, configured actions, bracketed paste and repeatable kill/yank/undo behavior.
entries.mechanism: setValue preserves/clamps existing cursor; a separate setValueAndMoveCursorToEnd places it at end; neither resets history/action state. Input first buffers bracketed paste across chunks, strips one start marker wherever found, finds end across accumulated data, inserts content atomically then recursively handles trailing input. Paste removes CRLF/CR/LF and expands tabs to four spaces; it does not apply the ordinary-input C0/DEL/C1 rejection to other pasted controls. Configured cancel, undo, submit (plus literal LF), deletion, kill/yank and movement precede Kitty printable decoding and ordinary input. Left/right/backspace/delete consume Intl graphemes. Word and line kills snapshot each change and accumulate by prior kill action/direction. Yank snapshots and inserts newest; yank-pop only after yank with>1 entries replaces the immediately preceding yanked span and permanently rotates ring. Undo restores only value/cursor and clears lastAction, leaving ring intact. Typing coalesces after a type-word action except each whitespace input pushes a new snapshot, so a space and following word form one unit. Boundary no-op kills do not reset prior action; cursor operations generally do. Submit/cancel callbacks do not clear input.

entries.title: Direct filesystem completion, quoted tokens and display paths
entries.what: Complete local paths with exact token boundaries, home/relative preservation, symlink handling and quoted directory continuation.
entries.mechanism: Token delimiters are space, tab, double/single quote, equals. Double-quote scanning toggles on every quote without escape interpretation; an unclosed quote beginning at a token boundary, optionally immediately after boundary '@', yields the whole quoted prefix. Otherwise use the last delimiter. Natural path suggestions require slash, leading dot,~/ or empty token after literal space; forced extraction accepts any token including empty. Parse @ and opening quote separately. Expand only ~/ or exact~, preserving trailing slash; resolve relative directory against captured basePath. Empty,./,../,~,~/,/ roots and trailing slash list that directory; otherwise split parent/basename. Read entries synchronously, case-insensitive prefix filter, stat symlinks to identify directories (broken/inaccessible link treated as file), preserve ./,~/, absolute/relative display forms and normalize backslashes to '/'. Append '/' to directory paths, quote if already quoted or containing a space, and show basename label. Sort by value.endsWith('/') then label.localeCompare: quoted directory values end in a quote, so they do not receive that directory-first branch. Catch directory failures to[].

entries.title: Editor visual-row movement, sticky column and paste continuation traversal
entries.what: Move through wrapped visual rows, preserve a preferred column across short lines and resizing, and avoid getting trapped inside a folded paste marker.
entries.mechanism: Build visual rows from the same concealed/wrapped presentation used to render. Nonfinal wrap rows have maximum cursor offset length-1; final rows allow end. The source's 'visual column' is a display-string UTF16 offset, not a terminal cell count. When a shorter target clamps position, remember the desired column; restore it on a row that fits, but after rewrapping a now-interior source position the current visual offset takes precedence. setCursorCol clears preferred/snap state and clamps first-line lower bound to protected prompt prefix. Snap any multi-unit grapheme/marker interior to segment start and retain pre-snap logical position so the next move uses its original visual row. Moving down into a marker continuation whose desired position is still inside the marker skips continuation rows until after the atom; a desired position past the tail may land in following content. Pages move max(5, floor(rows*.3)) visual rows. Horizontal/word/edit actions reset sticky state; Right at final document end replaces preferred column with current position.
entries.interfaces: preferredVisualCol, snappedFrom; visual row map, source/display maps; moveCursor/pageUp/pageDown and setCursorCol.
entries.rust:
rust:crates/ice-tui/src/editor.rs:965-1042 moves Up/Down and pages by logical row with a clamped byte column; page_scroll is fixed 10 logical rows. There is no preferred column, wrapped-row traversal, hidden-prefix map or marker continuation skipping, despite render producing multiple rows. set_cursor preserves valid byte boundaries, which is necessary but does not provide these visual semantics. Native editor inline tests for pages and movement use unwrapped ASCII and do not establish visual parity.

A further native caret-rendering defect is bounded to ANSI-bearing wrapped rows: the escape scan accepts '[' as a final byte in the '@' through '~' range, ending an ESC[ sequence before its SGR parameters. Those parameters may then be counted as visible cells or split while finding the cursor; the focused active-editor render invokes this calculation on styled/selection/paste-placeholder rows (rust:crates/ice-tui/src/editor.rs:216-245; rust:crates/ice-tui/src/editor.rs:1415-1480). This is an independently source-verified native bug, separate from the missing TS visual-row movement behavior; the coordinator owns its defect record.
entries.port: Reuse the exact render layout for navigation, store preferred source/display position explicitly and keep byte/UTF16/cell units separate. Port the source transition table and marker continuation cases, while documenting any intentional improvement to cell-based navigation for wide glyphs instead of assuming the current source already uses cells.
entries.priority_reason: Cursor movement must traverse what the user sees and retain intent after narrowing the terminal or crossing short lines.

entries.title: Editor character-jump mode and UTF-8-safe search boundaries
entries.what: Enter a one-target jump mode, search forward/backward across logical lines, and cancel cleanly on another control action.
entries.mechanism: Either jump binding enters direction mode. While pending, either jump binding cancels; a printable decoded sequence or data with first codepoint>=32 is consumed as the target string, while nonprintable input cancels and then falls through to normal handling. Search is case-sensitive, forward from cursor+1 UTF16 unit and backward from cursor-1, then full subsequent/prior lines; no match leaves cursor unchanged. A match uses normal cursor setter and clears action grouping. Source backward lastIndexOf with negative position clamps to zero and can match the current position at index 0 despite the skip-current comment; specify this as a source edge case, not a stronger exclusion guarantee.
entries.interfaces: jumpForward/jumpBackward key actions; jumpMode and jumpToChar(target, direction); multiline cursor state.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/editor.rs:1098-1156 uses a char target but computes forward slice start as cursor byte offset+target.len_utf8 and backward as cursor-target.len_utf8 with an exclusive prefix. Target width is not the width of the character under/before the cursor. For '你x' at byte 0 targeting ASCII x, line[1..] is an invalid UTF8 slice; ordinary jump can panic. Backward search also skips an immediately preceding target due to exclusive endpoint. Pending mode is consumed only by plain/Shift chars in hardcoded handle_key at 1200-1388; repeated jump resets direction rather than canceling and control actions can leave mode pending. Inline jump tests 1769-1840 are ASCII only.
entries.port: Compute search starts from actual next/previous grapheme or codepoint boundaries, keep ranges valid and define current-position exclusion explicitly. Implement pending-mode cancellation before normal action dispatch and retain multiline/case-sensitive matching. Include multibyte current character with ASCII target and immediate-backward-target cases in future regression validation.
entries.priority_reason: The current native jump path can panic on ordinary multibyte text; mode cancellation also differs visibly.

entries.title: Editor asynchronous completion scheduling, stale-result checks and menu acceptance
entries.what: Coordinate cancellable asynchronous suggestions with the current text/caret, explicit Tab force mode, menu navigation and atomic completion acceptance.
entries.mechanism: Provider replacement cancels prior work; default triggers @/# combine with unique provider single-code-unit nonwhitespace triggers except slash. Natural attachment-trigger requests debounce 20 ms; explicit or forced requests start immediately. Cancellation increments a start token, clears debounce timer and aborts active controller. Requests serialize by awaiting the previous task, then check current provider/enabled/token before capturing text+line+column, creating controller and incrementing request ID. On result require not aborted, enabled, matching IDs and exact text/caret snapshot; invalid/empty results close menu and request render. Exact case-sensitive value match then first prefix match selects best item. Natural and force menus retain their mode across updates; active cursor moves requery. Explicit forced singleton applies directly with undo/change/render; otherwise create SelectList with configured row cap and a narrow 12..32 slash prefix column versus 32 default. Tab accepts selected item and closes; Enter applies a prefix-starting-slash command then continues to submit, but other completion contexts only apply/close. Source limitations: the assignment at line 2405 was connector-redacted and its contents were not recovered; surrounding token guards were read. There is no catch around prior-task/provider await, so rejected provider promises can poison later serialized requests; an abort-ignoring unresolved provider blocks subsequent requests. Editor has no dispose cleanup for these timers/tasks. Forced singleton return does not explicitly clear an already-existing menu.
entries.interfaces: setAutocompleteProvider, isShowingAutocomplete, protected isAutocompleteEnabled; AbortController, request IDs/debounce token; SelectList; provider.applyCompletion; requestRender/onChange.
entries.rust:
rust:crates/ice-tui/src/editor.rs:1-2420 has no completion provider/menu/request lifecycle. Actual native host counterpart is rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/autocomplete.rs:12-201: synchronous provider calls on refresh/navigation/acceptance, centered bounded menu rendered in a separate container above editor, selection retained/clamped, explicit / or @ contexts alone consume Up/Down with clamped nonwrapping movement. It has no async debounce/abort/stale snapshot/force singleton or provider application hook. Acceptance re-queries rather than accepting a stored result and calls set_text, which clears paste registry and lacks undo snapshot. Preserve this existing host integration and byte-offset adapters, not a claim that native completion is wholly missing.

The native acceptance path reads get_text with folded-paste markers and then calls set_text, whose reset_pastes clears their stored bodies; it therefore loses the expansions of retained markers, unlike the separately correct native dequeue materialization (rust:crates/ice-tui/src/editor.rs:348-399; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/autocomplete.rs:119-158). In the same acceptance path, a required separator is appended at the end of the whole reconstructed draft after its suffix, while the caret advances as if that separator were next to the replacement. Completion in the middle of a draft can consequently leave the suffix attached to the replacement and put the cursor in the wrong location (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui/autocomplete.rs:143-155). These defects are tracked by the coordinator; no runtime test was executed.
entries.port: Move request ownership into a reusable editor/controller contract with owned provider handles, cancellation, text/caret generation checks and a disposal path. Preserve native menu placement if intentionally configured while matching source action precedence, best-match and atomic acceptance. Recover safely from rejection and ignored cancellation without serial queue poisoning; document these as strengthened error handling beyond the current TS source.
entries.priority_reason: Async custom completion must not apply stale text, discard folded pastes or hang all later requests after a provider failure.

entries.title: Markdown table column budgets and lossless multiline cells
entries.what: Fit tables into the content width while preserving complete cell content, styled long tokens and stable borders.
entries.mechanism: For N header columns reserve 3N+1 border/padding cells. If remaining budget<N, fall back to wrapped token.raw. Measure styled natural width and longest whitespace-delimited word per column capped 30, with minimum 1. If word minima exceed budget, allocate 1 each then proportional floor growth weighted by max(wordMin-1,0), distributing remainder left-to-right. If natural table fits, use max(natural, min); otherwise distribute extra budget proportionally to natural-minus-min growth, then round-robin leftover without exceeding natural widths. Wrap every header/body cell at its allocated width using ANSI wrapper, render each logical row as max(cell heights) physical rows and pad shorter cells. Bold all header cell padding/text; body rows retain inline styling. Source ignores parsed alignment metadata—its alignment test checks presence only, not right/center placement.
entries.interfaces: renderTable(token, availableWidth, nextTokenType, styleContext); getLongestWordWidth cap 30; wrapCellText; inline width and ANSI wrap contracts.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/markdown.rs:720-868 detects only rows starting/ending pipe, manually splits escaped/code pipes with a one-bit backtick toggle, and uses proportional rounded natural widths with minimum 1. It budgets3N+1 but emits compact borders without source cell padding, has no word minima/remainder reconciliation/narrow raw fallback, and truncates each cell to one line with ellipsis. Thus table text is lost instead of wrapped. Header is not bold. The splitter handles simple one-backtick spans but toggling each backtick does not model multi-backtick code delimiters. Existing native row dividers and Unicode grid should be preserved while repairing layout.
entries.port: Feed table nodes from the block parser into deterministic width allocation and lossless cell wrapping. Preserve escaped and multi-backtick pipe syntax using parser tokens, restore header emphasis/cell padding and explicitly document alignment as unsupported unless intentionally added. Cover narrow budgets, long URLs/inline code and multirow cells from the fully read TS tests.
entries.priority_reason: Truncated table cells can hide material answer content and commands; source behavior preserves them through wrapping.

entries.title: Markdown table style policy and default invalidation
entries.what: Expose the source table styles and per-instance/process-default precedence while preserving a consistent shared column layout.
entries.mechanism: Per-instance tableStyle wins over process default(initial'unicode'). Unicode and ASCII emit top/header/body separators/bottom; clean retains vertical cell separators/padding but no horizontal borders; clean-top-bottom adds continuous horizontal top/bottom only; raw wraps original Markdown. All styles use the same 3N+1 column geometry and multiline cell pass. setDefaultTableStyle changes a module variable and getDefaultTableStyle returns it; cached existing Markdown output is not invalidated automatically, so caller must invalidate to apply a changed default. Source accepts typed style values with no runtime validation; invalid foreign JS values can fail when glyphs are accessed.
entries.interfaces: MarkdownTableStyle union; setDefaultTableStyle/getDefaultTableStyle; per-instance options.tableStyle.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/markdown.rs:746-831 has only one compact Unicode table strategy and no default/instance style control. Native global theme revision participates in Markdown caching at 923-948, so it provides a useful invalidation mechanism to retain when table policy changes. The main application's appearance setting alone does not implement these glyph/layout choices in this primitive.
entries.port: Add explicit table style policy using the shared layout and wire appearance-triggered cache invalidation through the caller. Preserve native theme-revision cache invalidation and keep storage/UI ownership in the main TUI area. Use one layout pass so switching border glyphs does not accidentally alter wrapping.
entries.priority_reason: Appearance table preferences currently have no primitive implementation and existing cached messages need an intentional update path.

entries.title: Bounded Kitty upload reuse and placement redraw transactions
entries.what: Reuse already uploaded image data across moves and short offscreen intervals while bounding retained offscreen image count and estimated memory.
entries.mechanism:
Each image redraw parses placement metadata for every screen line. Visible IDs are recorded, and their cache entry is deleted/reinserted in Map order with current transmissionGeneration, transmissionBytes and estimatedDecodedBytes. Same-generation cached IDs use the lossless placement-only replacement line; changed generations retain the full transmission. Repeated visibility therefore refreshes retention order. Only offscreen entries count toward limits: at most 16 images,32 MiB transmission bytes and 64 MiB estimated decoded raster bytes. Evict oldest offscreen entries until all three limits hold, concatenate per-ID deleteKittyImage commands, and never evict an on-screen ID merely to meet these offscreen limits. This is not a total process/terminal-memory cap.

Cache preparation runs only for a full frame redraw or a changed row involving an old/new image, and only for captured Kitty protocol. Full redraw with an existing cache deletes all placements but preserves data; without cached uploads it deletes all Kitty image data. Image-only changes delete placements, then evicted data IDs are deleted before repaint. Every viewport row is repainted in image transactions so surrounding HStack text survives. previousScreen retains original transmission lines, not placement substitutions. Start clears cache; stop deletes Kitty data and clears it. Cropping/generation and encoded parsing are separate prerequisites. Source tests read image movement preserving siblings, reentry reuse,17th-offscreen count eviction and decoded quota; they were not executed.
entries.interfaces: Internal CachedKittyImage, prepareKittyScreen and terminal-owned upload map; getKittyImagePlacement generation and byte estimates; deleteAllKittyPlacements vs deleteAllKittyImages/deleteKittyImage; visible/offscreen frame identity.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/tui_alt_screen.rs:908-1054 tracks prior rows and emits removed-image cleanup but has no generation-indexed upload map, offscreen LRU quotas, placement-only reuse or all-rows image transaction. rust:crates/ice-tui/src/terminal_image.rs:249-281 deletes changed old placements by scanning image IDs; that row cleanup is useful existing behavior and does not provide retained data ownership. The full native renderer and its inline tests were read, not run.
entries.port: Add a terminal-owned upload cache over the metadata/parser service from TUI-227, keeping data versus placement deletion explicit. Count only offscreen data for the source retention policy, invalidate on protocol/terminal lifecycle changes and preserve unchanged surrounding line fragments when replacing transmission spans.
entries.priority_reason: Without bounded reuse, image scrolling repeatedly uploads large payloads or accumulates terminal state; lossless row substitution must preserve neighboring text.

entries.title: Shared chrome border families and narrow-width gate
entries.what: Apply one shared border-family contract to selectors and compatible chrome while leaving theme selection to the application adapter.
entries.mechanism:
chromeBorderGlyphs returns one of 11 families or null for none/unrecognized input. Exact corners/horizontal/vertical are: single(┌┐└┘,─,│), double(╔╗╚╝,═,║), round(╭╮╰╯,─,│), bold(┏┓┗┛,━,┃), single-double(┌┐╚╝,─,║), double-single(╔╗└┘,═,│), classic(++++,-,|), plus top-bottom-single/double/bold using only─/═/━ and no corners/sides. The mixed families deliberately use their listed top/bottom corners with one shared horizontal character; do not substitute a convention inferred from names.

applyChromeBorder returns the original lines unchanged for null glyphs or width<3, including top-bottom-only families; this means the comment's universal width guarantee does not hold on that bypass. Otherwise side families use inner=width-2 and top-bottom families inner=width. It always emits a colored top and bottom row, even for empty content, truncates each content row with ellipsis to inner width, pads by visible cell width and separately colors only side glyphs. The caller supplies lines already laid out at desired content width; the wrapper does not rerender a component. Color functions are assumed width-preserving.
entries.interfaces: ChromeBorderStyle union; chromeBorderGlyphs(style) -> {tl, tr, bl, br, h, v, sides}|null; applyChromeBorder(lines, width, style, color) -> string[]. Theme-to-family adapter remains main TUI-005.
entries.rust: rust:crates/ice-tui/src/select_list.rs:421-531 and rust:crates/ice-tui/src/settings_list.rs:378-513 render their own rows without this shared 11-family border wrapper. The fully read primitive exports rust:crates/ice-tui/src/lib.rs:1-173 expose no equivalent ChromeBorder API; scoped crates/ice-tui search for ChromeBorder/chrome_border/top-bottom-single/single-double found no matches. Existing native theme border colors/glyph uses elsewhere are preserved and owned by the main theme audit, not asserted globally absent.
entries.port: Implement the shared glyph map and width-gated wrapper in crates/ice-tui and use it from compatible selectors. Keep style resolution/theme updates in the main adapter, and preserve the exact bypass and empty-content rules; combine with corrected ANSI/grapheme truncation.
entries.priority_reason: A shared implementation keeps appearance border selections consistent across primitive selectors without duplicating family-specific layout.
